issue.body:
### Human Overview

we need tool definition to write on  LLM span now its only write in memory,   

also the model request's span isn't under LLM span, and in a script it ends up in a separate trace.

need those bug fix so we can replay a recorded model call 

An agent helped draft the details below; I reviewed the them 

### Checks

- [x] I have updated to the lastest minor and patch version of Strands
- [x] I have checked the documentation and this is not expected behavior
- [x] I have searched [./issues](./issues?q=) and there are no duplicates of my issue

### SDK Language

TypeScript

### Strands Version

1.24.0 (also 1.22.0, 1.23.0)

### Language Runtime Version

Node.js 22.23.2

### Operating System

Amazon Linux 2023 (arm64)

### Installation Method

npm

### Steps to Reproduce

1. `npm i @strands-agents/sdk zod @aws/aws-distro-opentelemetry-node-autoinstrumentation`
2. Save the `agent.mjs` from Additional Context (one agent, one tool).
3. Run: `AGENT_OBSERVABILITY_ENABLED=true OTEL_SEMCONV_STABILITY_OPT_IN=gen_ai_tool_definitions node --experimental-loader=@opentelemetry/instrumentation/hook.mjs --import @aws/aws-distro-opentelemetry-node-autoinstrumentation/register agent.mjs`
4. Inspect the `invoke_agent`, `chat` and AWS SDK `chat <model>` spans.

### Expected Behavior

- `invoke_agent` has `gen_ai.tool.definitions` with the opt-in, as in Python.
- The AWS SDK `chat <model>` span is a child of the Strands `chat` span, in the same trace.

### Actual Behavior

- `invoke_agent` has only `gen_ai.agent.tools` (names). `agent.js` never passes `toolsConfig` to the agent span, and `tracer.js` writes `gen_ai.tool.definitions` only when it is set.
- The model stream is not run inside `withSpanContext(modelSpan, …)`, unlike tool execution and multi-agent nodes. So the AWS SDK span starts its own trace in a script, or sits beside `invoke_agent` under an app span, never under `chat`.

### Possible Solution

Pass `toolsConfig` into the agent span options. Wrap `_streamFromModel(...)` and each `gen.next()` in `this._tracer.withSpanContext(modelSpan, …)`, as `tools/executors/executor.js` does. Related request: also pass `ctx.toolSpecs` to `startModelInvokeSpan` and record `gen_ai.tool.definitions` (semconv shape `{type:'function', name, description, parameters}`) on `chat` behind the same opt-in. Happy to send a PR.

### Additional Context

<details>
<summary>Extended context</summary>

Repro (`agent.mjs`):
```js
// agent.mjs
import { Agent, BedrockModel, tool } from '@strands-agents/sdk'
import { z } from 'zod'
const check = tool({ name: 'check_availability', description: 'Check whether a product is listed and in stock.',
  inputSchema: z.object({ productName: z.string() }), callback: () => '{"in_stock":true}' })
const agent = new Agent({ model: new BedrockModel({ region: 'us-east-1', modelId: 'us.anthropic.claude-haiku-4-5-20251001-v1:0' }), tools: [check], printer: false })
await agent.invoke('Is the espresso machine in stock?')
process.kill(process.pid, 'SIGTERM'); setTimeout(() => process.exit(0), 10000) // flush
```

Span layout without an app span:
```
traceA  chat us.anthropic…  @opentelemetry/instrumentation-aws-sdk  parent=None
traceB  chat                strands                                 parent=execute_agent_loop_cycle
traceB  invoke_agent Strands Agent                                  parent=None
```
Source references (1.23.0 `dist/src`; same code in 1.24.0): `agent/agent.js` L1116-1128 (agent span options, no `toolsConfig`), L1860-1864 (`startModelInvokeSpan({messages, modelId, systemPrompt})`), L1881 (model stream outside the span context); `telemetry/tracer.js` L213-215; correct pattern in `tools/executors/executor.js` L189-198 and `multiagent/graph.js` L394-398.

Use case: replaying a recorded LLM call from its trace needs the exact tools that call received, on the span that owns the call.

</details>

### Related Issues

#1113

issue.title: fix(memory): encode bytes in OpenAI converter reasoning blocks

labels.name: user-8213b3f8/repo-41623133
labels.description: PR size: S

issue.body:
Fixes #680

Agents using the OpenAI memory format crashed on any reply that carried hidden reasoning, and now that reply is saved and restored like any other.

**What this code is for**

`OpenAIConverseConverter` in `converters/openai.py` turns each Strands message into an OpenAI shaped JSON string before `AgentCoreMemorySessionManager` saves it to AgentCore Memory, and turns stored events back into Strands messages when a session is restored. Reasoning blocks have no OpenAI field, so they are kept as they are under `_strands_reasoning_content`.

**Before this PR**

A developer runs a Strands agent with `AgentCoreMemorySessionManager(converter=OpenAIConverseConverter)` on a model that returns reasoning as `reasoningContent.redactedContent`.

1. The model answers with a block `{"reasoningContent": {"redactedContent": b"..."}}`, where the value is raw `bytes`.
2. `append_message` calls `create_message`, which calls `OpenAIConverseConverter.message_to_payload`.
3. `_bedrock_to_openai` copies the block into `_strands_reasoning_content` unchanged, `bytes` included.
4. `json.dumps(openai_msg)` raises `TypeError: Object of type bytes is not JSON serializable`.
5. The agent call fails with `EventLoopException`, on every turn that has redacted reasoning.

**After this PR**

Same developer, same model, same turn.

1. Same as above through step 2.
2. `_bedrock_to_openai` passes each reasoning block through `encode_bytes_values`, so `bytes` becomes `{"__bytes_encoded__": true, "data": "<base64>"}`.
3. `json.dumps` succeeds and the event is saved.
4. On restore, `_openai_to_bedrock` passes each stored block through `decode_bytes_values`, so the model gets back the original `bytes`.
5. Reasoning blocks that hold only text are unchanged by both calls and still round trip as before.

**The diagram**

```mermaid
flowchart LR

classDef box fill:#eef1ff,stroke:#4c5bd4,color:#111827
classDef bad fill:#ffd6d6,stroke:#cc0000,color:#111827,stroke-width:3px
classDef good fill:#c8f0c8,stroke:#008800,color:#111827,stroke-width:3px

subgraph BEFORE["BEFORE: every redacted reasoning turn fails"]
direction TB
  B1["model returns redactedContent bytes"] --> B2["message_to_payload"]
  B2 --> B3["_bedrock_to_openai keeps raw block"]
  B3 --> B4{"json.dumps"}
  B4 -->|"bytes in block"| B5["TypeError, agent call fails"]
  B4 -->|"text only reasoning"| B6["saved"]
end

subgraph AFTER["AFTER: saved and restored as bytes"]
direction TB
  A1["model returns redactedContent bytes"] --> A2["message_to_payload"]
  A2 --> A3{"THE CHANGE: encode_bytes_values on block"}
  A3 --> A4{"json.dumps"}
  A4 -->|"bytes now base64"| A5["saved, decode_bytes_values on restore"]
  A4 -->|"text only reasoning"| A6["saved, unchanged"]
end

B1 ~~~ A1

class B1,B2,B3,B6 box
class A1,A2,A6 box
class B4,B5 bad
class A3,A5 good

linkStyle 3 stroke:#cc0000,stroke-width:5px
linkStyle 8 stroke:#008800,stroke-width:5px

style BEFORE fill:#fff5f5,stroke:#cc0000,color:#111827
style AFTER fill:#f3fff3,stroke:#008800,color:#111827
```

**The change**

In `converters/openai.py`, `reasoning_blocks.append(item)` becomes `reasoning_blocks.append(encode_bytes_values(item))` and `reasoning_items.append(rc)` becomes `reasoning_items.append(decode_bytes_values(rc))`. Both helpers come from `strands.types.session`, the same pair `SessionMessage.to_dict` and `SessionMessage.from_dict` use, which is how `AgentCoreMemoryConverter` already handles this. A new test, `test_redacted_reasoning_bytes_round_trip_in_openai_converter`, saves and restores a redacted block and checks the `bytes` come back equal.

**What changes for a user**

- Agents on models that return only redacted reasoning no longer crash when memory saves the turn.
- The restored history carries the redacted block as `bytes`, so the model receives it back on the next turn.
- Text reasoning blocks, tool calls and plain messages are saved and restored exactly as before.

issue.title: [world-vercel] Time out a stalled events WebSocket handshake
issue.body:
Thanks @rpinckne for the clear report and the repro, it made this easy to pin down.

**What broke:** if a server accepted the TCP connection but never answered the WebSocket upgrade, every event write for that run waited on the handshake with no deadline, until `maxDuration`. After a write timed out on a connected socket, the channel also stayed registered, so the next write paid another WS handshake instead of using HTTP.

**Root cause:** `connect()` opened the socket with no handshake deadline, and `request()` only arms its timeout after `ensureConnected()` resolves.

**Change** (in `WsEventsTransport`):
* The handshake gets a deadline of `getRequestTimeoutMs()`, the same knob the request deadline uses. It starts before the upgrade headers are resolved, since the OIDC refresh behind them is a plain `fetch` with no signal. When it fires, the waiting connect rejects with a `WsTransportError`, the socket is terminated, and the channel is closed, the same way `open()` already handles a failed first connect. This covers the first connect, eager reconnects and lazy reconnects, since they all go through `connect()`.
* When a write times out on a connected socket, the channel is now closed as well, so retries and later writes take HTTP. The `open()` doc is updated to match.
* The deadline is cleared on `open` and on `close`, so a normal handshake or a handshake that fails on its own is unaffected.

I used a plain timer plus `ws.terminate()` rather than the `handshakeTimeout` option so the transport knows the failure was a timeout without matching on the error message `ws` produces. Happy to switch if you prefer the option.

The streams WebSocket session already bounds its connect with its own budget and falls back to HTTP, so I left it alone.

**Tests:**
* End to end tests of `withEventPostRetry` with the real transport against a local server that never answers the upgrade, or never answers a frame: the write finishes over HTTP with one upgrade, and later writes go straight to HTTP. Both fail on main.
* A new test with a real local HTTP server that accepts the upgrade and never sends 101: the write now rejects after the timeout, the socket is dropped and the channel is closed. It hangs on main.
* In the existing fake socket suite: a stalled handshake fails the waiting write, closes the channel so `resolveWsTransport` returns null, covers a token fetch that never resolves, honours `WORKFLOW_REQUEST_TIMEOUT_MS`, is disarmed after a normal or failed handshake, and bounds a stalled eager reconnect with no further reconnect attempts. The existing request timeout test now expects the channel to close rather than reconnect.
* `pnpm typecheck` and `pnpm test` in `packages/world-vercel` pass (1150 tests), biome is clean apart from two warnings that already exist on main.

I'm new to this code, so any feedback on whether closing the channel on a timed out write is the behaviour you want is very welcome.

Fixes #4642

Happy (almost) Halloween! 🎃

issue.title: fix(workflow): stop storing a node's input as a user turn
issue.body:
### Link to Issue or Description of Change

**1. Link to an existing issue (if applicable):**

- Fixes #720

**Problem:**

Saved chat history now holds only what the person actually typed, instead of also showing messages they never sent.

A workflow is a chain of steps. When a step is an AI agent, the step before it hands it an input, and the agent has to see that input as the latest message so it answers it. `runLlmAgentAsNode` is the code that runs an agent as one of those steps.

Before:

Ana chats with a workflow that picks a city, looks up the time there, and then writes a reply.

1. Ana types "Hello".
2. The app saves "Hello" in her chat history.
3. The first step picks Paris and the second step finds the time in Paris.
4. The reply step is handed `{"timeInfo":"10:10 AM","city":"Paris"}` as its input.
5. That input is saved in Ana's chat history as a message from Ana.
6. Ana reopens the chat and sees a message from herself that she never typed.

**Solution:**

After:

Ana chats with the same workflow.

1. Ana types "Hello".
2. The app saves "Hello" in her chat history.
3. The first step picks Paris and the second step finds the time in Paris.
4. The reply step is handed `{"timeInfo":"10:10 AM","city":"Paris"}` as its input.
5. The input is placed in the working copy of the chat only while the reply step runs, so the agent still answers it.
6. When the step ends, the input is taken back out. Nothing is written to the saved history.
7. Ana reopens the chat and sees only "Hello" and the replies.

```mermaid
flowchart LR
  subgraph BEFORE
    B1[Ana types Hello] --> B2[Steps find the time in Paris] --> B3[Step input saved as a message from Ana] ==> B4[History shows a message Ana never typed]
  end
  subgraph AFTER
    A1[Ana types Hello] --> A2[Steps find the time in Paris] --> A3["THE CHANGE: step input kept only while the step runs"] ==> A4[History shows only what Ana typed]
    A3 --> A5[Agent still answers the step input]
  end
  B1 ~~~ A1
  linkStyle 2 stroke:#d32f2f,stroke-width:4px
  linkStyle 5 stroke:#2e7d32,stroke-width:4px
```

The change: `pushNodeInputAsUserTurn` adds the input to the working copy of the session only, and no longer writes it through the session service. `removeEvent` takes it back out in a `finally` block, so it is gone whether the agent finishes, stops early, or fails.

Which option and why: the analysis in the issue thread listed three options and pointed out that a contributor should not pick one alone. This PR takes the first option (keep the input out of the session service) plus a cleanup step, because that is exactly what the Python version of ADK does today:

- It adds the input to the working copy of the session only ([`_llm_agent_wrapper.py` line 380](https://github.com/google/adk-python/blob/571670d9f7e1760985d0bd41a009600ee14b6acd/src/google/adk/workflow/_llm_agent_wrapper.py#L380)) and removes it in a `finally` block when the agent finishes ([line 476](https://github.com/google/adk-python/blob/571670d9f7e1760985d0bd41a009600ee14b6acd/src/google/adk/workflow/_llm_agent_wrapper.py#L476)), added in google/adk-python#7320.
- Writing the input through the session service was tried in Python ([8aaf62a](https://github.com/google/adk-python/commit/8aaf62ab1e5c88365b8abc4c6a9101d7dcd3afce)) and reverted the same day ([7b0f7f0](https://github.com/google/adk-python/commit/7b0f7f019db043f24b3ab94682a8eccd32382189)).

The cleanup step also answers the concern raised about the first option: with the in memory session service and `--save_session`, the input used to stay in the list. Now it is removed before the step returns, so every session service ends up with the same history.

What changes for a user:

- Saved sessions, session reads from the API, and `--save_session` files hold one user message per turn: the one the person typed.
- Still works: the agent still receives and answers its step input, agents in task mode are untouched, a plain agent outside a workflow is untouched, and later steps still read earlier step outputs through their instructions.
- One difference: an agent step later in the same turn that reads the full history no longer sees an earlier step's input as a message from the person. This matches the Python version.

The existing test `persists the injected user turn through the session service` checked the old behavior, so it now checks the opposite (`keeps the node input out of the session service`). A new test runs a workflow through the real `Runner` with an `InMemorySessionService` and checks that the stored session holds only "Hello" while the model still received the step input. It fails on `main` with the extra `{"wrapped":"hello"}` user message.

### Testing Plan

**Unit Tests:**

- [x] I have added or updated unit tests for my change.
- [x] All unit tests pass locally.

- `npx vitest run --project unit:core --project unit:dev --project unit:integrations --project integration --project e2e`: 440 files passed, 6542 tests passed, 55 skipped
- `npm run build`, `npm run lint`, `npm run format:check`, `npm run ts:check`, `npm run ts:check:samples`: all pass
- `npm run test:cross-language`: only the Go A2A suites fail locally because Go is not installed on this machine; they do not touch this code

**Manual End-to-End (E2E) Tests:**

Not run against a live model. The new test drives the same path as the steps in #720 through the real `Runner` and session service.

### Checklist

- [x] I have read the [CONTRIBUTING.md](https://github.com/google/adk-js/blob/main/CONTRIBUTING.md) document.
- [x] I have performed a self-review of my own code.
- [ ] I have commented my code, particularly in hard-to-understand areas.
- [x] I have added tests that prove my fix is effective or that my feature works.
- [x] New and existing unit tests pass locally with my changes.
- [ ] I have manually tested my changes end-to-end.
- [ ] Any dependent changes have been merged and published in downstream modules.

issue.title: fix(python): return tool errors to the model instead of crashing
issue.body:
Fixes #250

When a Python tool throws an error, the agent used to crash the whole request; now the model is told the tool failed and can answer or try again.

**What this code is for**

`AgentTools.tool_handler` in `python/src/agent_squad/utils/tool.py` runs when `AnthropicAgent` or `BedrockLLMAgent` gets a reply from the model that asks for a tool. It finds each tool call in the reply, runs the matching `AgentTool` through `_process_tool`, and sends the results back to the model as tool results.

**Before this PR**

A user asks an agent something that makes the model call a tool, and that tool raises an exception (for example a database that is down).

1. The model replies with a `toolUse` block naming the tool.
2. `tool_handler` calls `self.callbacks.on_tool_start`.
3. `tool_handler` calls `self._process_tool(tool_name, input_data)`, which awaits the tool's `func`.
4. The tool raises, and nothing in `tool_handler` catches it.
5. The exception leaves `tool_handler`, the agent's `process_request` fails, and the user gets an error instead of an answer. `on_tool_error` is never called, so callbacks never see the failure.

**After this PR**

Same user, same failing tool.

1. Same as above through step 3.
2. The tool raises, and `tool_handler` catches it.
3. `tool_handler` calls `self.callbacks.on_tool_error` with the tool name, the input and the exception.
4. The tool result sent to the model is `Error processing tool '<name>': <message>`, the same text the TypeScript `AgentTools.processTool` already returns.
5. The model reads that result and replies to the user, or calls the tool again.

When the tool succeeds, nothing changes: `on_tool_end` is called and the tool output goes to the model as before.

**The diagram**

```mermaid
flowchart LR

classDef box fill:#eef1ff,stroke:#4c5bd4,color:#111827
classDef bad fill:#ffd6d6,stroke:#cc0000,color:#111827,stroke-width:3px
classDef good fill:#c8f0c8,stroke:#008800,color:#111827,stroke-width:3px

subgraph BEFORE["BEFORE: a tool error ends the request"]
direction TB
  B1["model asks for a tool"] --> B2["tool_handler"]
  B2 --> B3["_process_tool runs func"]
  B3 --> B4{"func raises?"}
  B4 -->|"not caught"| B5["request fails, on_tool_error never called"]
  B4 -->|"no error"| B6["on_tool_end, result to model"]
end

subgraph AFTER["AFTER: the model sees the error"]
direction TB
  A1["model asks for a tool"] --> A2["tool_handler"]
  A2 --> A3["_process_tool runs func"]
  A3 --> A4{"THE CHANGE: except Exception"}
  A4 -->|"func raised"| A5["on_tool_error, error text to model"]
  A4 -->|"no error"| A6["on_tool_end, result to model"]
end

B1 ~~~ A1

class B1,B2,B3,B6 box
class A1,A2,A3,A6 box
class B4,B5 bad
class A4,A5 good

linkStyle 3 stroke:#cc0000,stroke-width:5px
linkStyle 8 stroke:#008800,stroke-width:5px

style BEFORE fill:#fff5f5,stroke:#cc0000,color:#111827
style AFTER fill:#f3fff3,stroke:#008800,color:#111827
```

**The change**

In `AgentTools.tool_handler`, the call to `self._process_tool` now sits in a `try`. On `except Exception`, it calls `self.callbacks.on_tool_error` and sets the result to `f"Error processing tool '{tool_name}': {error}"`. The `on_tool_end` call moved into the `else` branch, so it runs only when the tool succeeded. The text matches the TypeScript `processTool`, so both packages send the model the same message. A missing tool still returns `Tool '<name>' not found` as before.

**What changes for a user**

- A tool that raises no longer crashes the agent; the model gets the error text and can recover.
- `on_tool_error` is now called when a tool raises, so logging and tracing callbacks see tool failures.
- `on_tool_end` is no longer called for a tool that raised, only `on_tool_error`.
- Tools that succeed behave exactly as before.
- Cancelling the request still stops it, because cancellation is not an `Exception` subclass and is not caught.

By submitting this pull request, I confirm that you can use, modify, copy, and redistribute this contribution, under the terms of your choice.

issue.title: [dart_mcp] StringSchema minLength/maxLength count UTF-16 code units instead of characters
issue.body:
Hey folks, hope you're doing well!

`StringSchema` validation in `dart_mcp` counts `minLength` / `maxLength` in UTF-16 code units instead of characters, so strings with emoji or other characters outside the BMP get the wrong result.

First off, thanks a lot for the schema validation work (#126). Having `Schema.validate` run on tool arguments out of the box is really handy, and it's what makes servers safe to write without hand rolled checks. `StringSchema` is the piece that enforces string constraints like `minLength`, `maxLength` and `pattern` on those arguments, and since `registerTool` defaults to `validateArguments: true`, this runs for every tool call.

### Current behavior

1. Define a string schema with `maxLength: 1` (or `minLength: 2`).
2. Validate the string `"😀"`, which is one character (one code point) but two UTF-16 code units in Dart.
3. The check uses `data.length`, so it sees a length of 2.
4. With `maxLength: 1` it reports `maxLengthExceeded`, and with `minLength: 2` it passes, which is the opposite of what the spec says in both cases.

ASCII strings and `"é"` behave correctly, since they're a single code unit.

### Expected behavior

JSON Schema 2020-12 validation, [§6.3.1 and §6.3.2](https://json-schema.org/draft/2020-12/json-schema-validation#section-6.3.1):

> The length of a string instance is defined as the number of its characters as defined by RFC 8259.

So `"😀"` should pass `maxLength: 1` and fail `minLength: 2`. The error messages already say "characters long", so I think the intent matches the spec and it's just the counting.

### Minimal repro

```dart
import 'package:dart_mcp/server.dart';

void main() {
  for (final (schema, value) in [
    (Schema.string(maxLength: 1), '😀'),
    (Schema.string(minLength: 2), '😀'),
    (Schema.string(maxLength: 1), 'é'),
  ]) {
    print(schema.validate(value).map((e) => e.error.name).toList());
  }
}
```

Observed with Dart SDK 3.13.7 against the package at `main` (70473568):

```
[maxLengthExceeded]   // expected []
[]                    // expected [minLengthNotMet]
[]                    // correct
```

### Code

- `minLength` check: https://github.com/dart-lang/ai/blob/70473568c3cc93b3332bd3f7dc59c1cb7195a5d5/pkgs/dart_mcp/lib/src/api/tools.dart#L1191
- `maxLength` check: https://github.com/dart-lang/ai/blob/70473568c3cc93b3332bd3f7dc59c1cb7195a5d5/pkgs/dart_mcp/lib/src/api/tools.dart#L1201
- `pattern` check: https://github.com/dart-lang/ai/blob/70473568c3cc93b3332bd3f7dc59c1cb7195a5d5/pkgs/dart_mcp/lib/src/api/tools.dart#L1212
- Existing string tests: https://github.com/dart-lang/ai/blob/70473568c3cc93b3332bd3f7dc59c1cb7195a5d5/pkgs/dart_mcp/test/api/tools_test.dart#L508

Related: #719 (the 2020-12 dialect umbrella). I don't think it covers this one, but it felt worth linking.

### Questions

The simplest fix I can see is switching both checks to `data.runes.length`, plus a few non ASCII cases next to the existing string tests. Does that sound right to you, or would you prefer something else here? I'd love any feedback or tips on what fits the package best.

One related thing I noticed while looking: the `pattern` check builds `RegExp(dataPattern)` without `unicode: true`, so `^.$` doesn't match `"😀"` and `\p{L}` doesn't match `"é"`. The 2020-12 core spec (§6.4) says patterns SHOULD use ECMA 262 "u" semantics. Would you like that folded into the same fix, kept separate, or left as is? Totally open to whatever you think is best, and happy to hear from anyone else who has run into this too.

If it helps, I'm happy to send a small PR with tests. Thanks again!

issue.title: [dart_mcp] Minor 2026-07-28 API & schema completeness fixes (Completion.meta, SamplingCapability, SamplingMessage, ResourceLink)

labels.name: repo-884bba4d
labels.description: Incorrect behavior (everything from a crash to more subtle misbehavior)

issue.body:
> [!NOTE]
> **Agent-Filed Issue — Please Validate Findings**: This issue was filed by an AI coding agent on behalf of @jakemac53 during an automated audit of the MCP `2026-07-28` specification update (https://github.com/dart-lang/ai/issues/668). Please independently validate the specification interpretation, current codebase behavior, and proposed changes before implementing.

## Summary

An audit of `pkgs/dart_mcp/lib/src/api/` against `schema/2026-07-28/schema.json` surfaced several small API omissions and bugs:

1. **`Completion` factory silently drops its `meta` argument**:
   - [`Completion({required List<String> values, int? total, bool? hasMore, Meta? meta})`](https://github.com/dart-lang/ai/blob/4581da98f69afa3b1d15c0559392134d03986cf5/pkgs/dart_mcp/lib/src/api/completions.dart#L68-L84) accepts `Meta? meta` in its parameter list, never writes `if (meta != null) Keys.meta: meta` into the underlying map, and does not `implements WithMetadata`.
2. **Untyped `ClientCapabilities.sampling` (`sampling.tools` and `sampling.context`)**:
   - In `schema.json`, `ClientCapabilities.sampling` has typed sub-capabilities `tools` and `context` (`SamplingCapability`), and [`sampling.mdx`](https://modelcontextprotocol.io/specification/2026-07-28/client/sampling) requires clients to declare `sampling.tools` to receive tool-enabled sampling requests (which the server enforces in [`_missingInputRequestCapability`](https://github.com/dart-lang/ai/blob/4581da98f69afa3b1d15c0559392134d03986cf5/pkgs/dart_mcp/lib/src/server/request_scoped.dart#L500-L511)).
   - [`ClientCapabilities.sampling`](https://github.com/dart-lang/ai/blob/4581da98f69afa3b1d15c0559392134d03986cf5/pkgs/dart_mcp/lib/src/api/initialization.dart#L279-L310) is still typed as raw `Map<String, Object?>?`, and [`SamplingSupport`](https://github.com/dart-lang/ai/blob/4581da98f69afa3b1d15c0559392134d03986cf5/pkgs/dart_mcp/lib/src/client/sampling_support.dart#L10-L16) sets `capabilities.sampling ??= {}` with no typed helper or `SamplingCapability` extension type for advertising `tools` or `context`.
3. **`SamplingMessage` missing `WithMetadata` / `Meta? meta`**:
   - `2026-07-28/schema.json` includes `_meta` on `SamplingMessage`, while [`SamplingMessage`](https://github.com/dart-lang/ai/blob/4581da98f69afa3b1d15c0559392134d03986cf5/pkgs/dart_mcp/lib/src/api/sampling.dart#L162-L176) does not implement `WithMetadata` or accept `Meta? meta` in its factory constructor.
4. **`ResourceLink` factory missing `size` & `Content` missing convenience members**:
   - [`ResourceLink`](https://github.com/dart-lang/ai/blob/4581da98f69afa3b1d15c0559392134d03986cf5/pkgs/dart_mcp/lib/src/api/api.dart#L701-L745) exposes `int? get size` (matching `Resource`), but its factory constructor omits `int? size`.
   - [`Content`](https://github.com/dart-lang/ai/blob/4581da98f69afa3b1d15c0559392134d03986cf5/pkgs/dart_mcp/lib/src/api/api.dart#L511-L565) has static aliases and type predicates for text, image, audio, and embedded resources, but omits `Content.resourceLink` and `bool get isResourceLink` (and its doc comment omits `ResourceLink`).

issue.title: [Bug]: `container machine logs -f` exits immediately when the log is empty
issue.body:
### I have done the following

- [x] I have searched the existing issues
- [ ] If possible, I've reproduced the issue using the 'main' branch of this project

### Steps to reproduce

Hey folks, hope you're doing well!

Quick summary: `container machine logs -f` (without `-n`) exits right away with no output when the log file is empty, instead of waiting for new lines.

For context, `container machine logs` shows a machine VM's stdio log, or its boot log with `--boot`, and `-f` is meant to keep following it as new lines arrive.

What happens today, traced on main (d5416e63):

1. Run `container machine logs -f <machine>` (or `container machine logs --boot -f <machine>`) while that log file is still empty, for example right after the machine starts.
2. Without `-n`, `tail()` in `Sources/ContainerCommands/Machine/MachineLogs.swift` (around lines 101 to 105) does `guard let data = try fh.readToEnd() else { return }`.
3. `FileHandle.readToEnd()` returns `nil` for a zero byte file (I checked this with a tiny Swift snippet on macOS).
4. So `tail()` returns before it reaches `if follow { followFile(fh:) }` (around lines 116 to 119).
5. The command exits immediately with no output and never follows the log.

Minimal repro of the Foundation part:

```swift
import Foundation

let path = NSTemporaryDirectory() + "empty.log"
FileManager.default.createFile(atPath: path, contents: Data())
let fh = try FileHandle(forReadingFrom: URL(fileURLWithPath: path))
print(try fh.readToEnd() as Any) // prints nil
```

Honest note: I haven't run this on a machine VM yet, I traced it in the code and confirmed the `readToEnd()` behavior with the snippet above.

### Problem description

Expected: with `-f`, an empty log should just start following and print lines as they show up, same as `container logs -f` does now. Without `-f`, returning early is totally fine. The `-n` path (around lines 75 to 98) looks fine too.

This is the sibling of #2374, which was fixed for `container logs` in #2377. Big thanks to @i098 for that fix! The PR description mentions it deliberately left machine logs alone since they have a separate implementation, so I figured it was worth a dedicated issue.

A small heads up, in case it's useful: #2023 by @gnavadev (nice work on the tailing fixes there) moves both commands into a shared `LogTailer.swift`. As far as I can tell the shared tailer still has the `guard ... else { return }` form, so as written it wouldn't cover machine logs and might bring the empty log case back for `container logs` after it lands. I may well be missing something there, so happy to be corrected.

Which direction would you prefer?

1. Mirror #2377 in `MachineLogs.swift` with `} else if let data = try fh.readToEnd() {`, so following still starts on an empty file.
2. Fold the fix into the shared tailer from #2023, so both commands get it in one place.

I'd be glad to send a small PR for whichever you like, and any feedback or tips on how you'd want it tested would be really appreciated. Others are very welcome to weigh in too!

### Environment

```markdown
- OS: macOS 26.6.2 (25G83)
- Xcode: n/a (traced in source, not built locally)
- Container: main at d5416e63
```

### Code of Conduct

- [x] I agree to follow this project's Code of Conduct

issue.title: feat(review): review each commit of a PR separately
issue.body:
With per commit review turned on by the host, `/review` reviews each commit of a PR on its own diff and commit message, instead of only the combined diff.

Closes #4470. It is opt in and host only. The commit messages piece was split out into #4603, as suggested, and that has now landed on `main`.

**What this code is for**

`PRReviewer.run()` in `pr_agent/commands/pr_reviewer.py` handles `/review`. It asks the git provider for the PR diff, renders `pr_reviewer_prompts.toml` with that diff, makes one model call (or a few when chunking), and publishes one review comment.

**Before this PR**

A maintainer on GitLab has an MR with 4 commits, each with a message that explains one change, and comments `/review`.

1. `PRReviewer.run()` asks `GitLabProvider.get_diff_files()` for the diff of the whole MR.
2. The prompt gets that combined diff, plus the title and description.
3. The model returns findings with file and line, but nothing says which commit a finding belongs to.
4. One review comment for the whole MR. The maintainer has to work out by hand which of the 4 commits needs the fixup.

**After this PR**

Same maintainer, same MR, with `per_commit_review = true` in the host config or `.pr_agent.toml`.

1. `PRReviewer.run()` sees `per_commit_review` and calls `_run_per_commit()`.
2. `get_pr_commits()` returns the 4 commits, oldest first, with their parents, read fresh from the provider on every run. Merge commits are dropped here without loading them. `_commit_review_records()` reads the commits already reviewed from hidden markers in PR-Agent's own comments. For each commit not already listed by SHA, `set_commit_review_scope()` loads its files once and returns a fingerprint of its own patch, and only commits whose fingerprint is not recorded are kept. On the first run there are no markers, so all 4 are kept.
3. For each commit, `set_commit_review_scope()` scopes the diff to that commit against its parent, and `commit_under_review` puts its message (clipped to `max_commits_tokens`) in the prompt, between random markers made fresh for each run. `commit_messages_str` is cleared, so the prompt does not also list every other commit's message.
4. `_run_review()` runs once per commit and publishes one comment that names and links the commit. It uses the incremental review header, so it never replaces the persistent full review.
5. A commit with no findings gets no comment when `pr_reviewer.publish_output_no_suggestions = false`. With `inline_key_issues = true`, findings land inline on that commit's own diff.
6. 4 comments, one per commit, each with a `<!-- pr-agent:reviewed-commit <fingerprint> <sha> -->` line two lines below the hidden `<!-- pr-agent:review:incremental -->` identity. On the next push with 1 new commit, only that commit is reviewed. Without the setting, `/review` takes exactly the old path.

**The diagram**

```mermaid
flowchart LR

classDef box fill:#eef1ff,stroke:#4c5bd4,color:#111827
classDef bad fill:#ffd6d6,stroke:#cc0000,color:#111827,stroke-width:3px
classDef good fill:#c8f0c8,stroke:#008800,color:#111827,stroke-width:3px

subgraph BEFORE["BEFORE: 1 review for 4 commits"]
direction TB
  B1["Maintainer comments /review"] --> B2["PRReviewer.run"]
  B2 --> B3["get_diff_files for the whole MR"]
  B3 --> B4{"one prompt, combined diff"}
  B4 -->|"findings not tied to a commit"| B5["1 comment for the whole MR"]
  B4 -->|"per_commit_review off"| B6["same as today"]
end

subgraph AFTER["AFTER: 1 review per commit"]
direction TB
  A1["Maintainer comments /review"] --> A2["PRReviewer.run"]
  A2 --> A3["get_pr_commits"]
  A3 --> A4{"THE CHANGE: per_commit_review on"}
  A4 -->|"each commit: own diff and message"| A5["1 comment per commit, linked"]
  A4 -->|"setting off or provider unsupported"| A6["whole PR review, as today"]
end

B1 ~~~ A1

class B1,B2,B3,B6 box
class A1,A2,A3,A6 box
class B4,B5 bad
class A4,A5 good

linkStyle 3 stroke:#cc0000,stroke-width:5px
linkStyle 8 stroke:#008800,stroke-width:5px

style BEFORE fill:#fff5f5,stroke:#cc0000,color:#111827
style AFTER fill:#f3fff3,stroke:#008800,color:#111827
```

**The change**

* `PRReviewer.run()` now branches on `per_commit_review` into `_run_per_commit()`, and the old body moved into `_run_review()` unchanged apart from the commit header and the checks below.
* `GitProvider` gets `get_pr_commits()` (returns `None` by default, so other providers fall back to a whole PR review with a notice) and `set_commit_review_scope()`. GitHub and GitLab implement both on top of the existing incremental diff path. On GitHub, new side file contents are read at the commit when a head SHA is set.
* `_run_per_commit()` reviews only commits whose fingerprint is not recorded, so a plain `/review` and the default `push_commands` no longer review every commit again on each push (454174f1, 40cb6ee2, b52fbf25, bf4dd1b6, 9b159195). `commit_patch_fingerprint()` in `git_provider.py` hashes each file's name and patch with the `@@ -a,b +c,d @@` numbers removed, so a rebase onto `main` that leaves a commit's own patch alone does not review it again, while an amend or `--autosquash` fixup does. On GitLab, when a file's diff comes back empty (collapsed, too large or binary), the commit SHA is mixed into the fingerprint so two different commits never share one; such a commit is reviewed again after a rebase. A commit is recorded only after its review succeeds, including when every file was filtered out: `_run_review()` puts the marker line two lines below the comment's hidden incremental review identity, and a commit that gets no comment (no findings with `publish_output_no_suggestions = false`) goes into one record comment that starts with `<!-- pr-agent:review:commits -->` and is edited in place through `publish_persistent_comment_full()`. With default settings and no merge commits, no record comment is created. Before writing, the record is read again and merged, trimmed to commits still in the PR, and cut from the oldest end if it would pass the 65000 character comment limit. Markers count only at those fixed lines and only in comments `is_comment_authored_by_pr_agent()` confirms. A marker in a comment confirmed as someone else's is ignored. Markers are found by that hidden identity rather than the visible heading, so changing `review_heading` never reviews commits again. When comment authorship cannot be checked for the run, or marker comments exist but none can be confirmed and the author of at least one cannot be verified (for example a GitHub App whose login cannot be resolved), the run falls back to one whole PR review with a notice instead of reviewing every commit on each push. Each commit's files are loaded once per run and reused for its review; a commit whose patch is already recorded under another SHA (a rebase) is recorded under the new SHA too, and a commit with no changes of its own is recorded, so neither is loaded again. A failed commit is not recorded, so the next run retries it; the record counts failed attempts, and automatic runs stop after `PER_COMMIT_MAX_AUTO_ATTEMPTS` (3) while a manual `/review` always retries. Selection does not use commit dates, so a commit authored before the last review but pushed after it is still reviewed. If the comments cannot be read, the run fails with the usual failure comment instead of reviewing every commit. The `-i` lookup and its `minimal_*_for_incremental_review` thresholds are not used here, so a manual `/review` never stops silently. `docs/docs/commands/review.md` says so, and also says that if PR-Agent's comments are removed, the next run reviews every commit again unless `max_commits_per_review` is set (93cb7440).
* The commit message block opens and closes with `{{ commit_message_begin }}` and `{{ commit_message_end }}` from `prompt_boundary_markers("COMMIT_MESSAGE")` (the helper #4603 added to `pr_agent/algo/artifacts.py`), so a commit message containing `<<<COMMIT_MESSAGE_END>>>` cannot close the block early. It sits right above #4603's `commit_messages_str` block, which keeps its own `COMMIT_MESSAGES` markers.
* `_should_publish_review_no_suggestions()` checks the parsed findings for a commit review, so a commit where the model returned nothing or prose stays quiet with `publish_output_no_suggestions = false`.
* `per_commit_review` and `max_commits_per_review` are in the `pr_reviewer` entry of `CLI_HOST_ONLY_KEYS_BY_SECTION` and `PER_DIRECTORY_HOST_ONLY_KEYS_BY_SECTION`, so `/review --pr_reviewer.per_commit_review=true` in a comment is rejected.
* `max_commits_per_review` defaults to 0 (no limit). When more commits than the cap are not reviewed yet, the whole PR is reviewed once with a notice, and after that review succeeds all its commits are recorded, so the next push goes back to one review per new commit. GitHub lists at most 250 commits per PR, so a PR with more is reviewed as a whole with a notice.
* Merge commits, root commits and empty commits are skipped. One failing commit does not stop the rest; the run is marked failed afterwards.
* Upstream `main` is merged in with merge commits (181edc4c, 9723af3a), not a rebase, so no history is rewritten. Conflicts: `convert_to_markdown_v2()` keeps main's `get_bot_display_name()` next to the commit header, `CLI_HOST_ONLY_KEYS_BY_SECTION` keeps main's new `pr_reviewer` keys plus ours, and the key count in `test_config_reference.py` is main's 319 plus our 2. After #4798, `run()` no longer checks `is_answer`, and the tests set `config.is_auto_command`. After #4838 renamed `pr_agent/tools` to `pr_agent/commands`, the tests import from `pr_agent.commands` and the config links point at `../commands/review.md` (ed7715a5). `_prepare_code_suggestions()` on GitHub skips `validate_comments_inside_hunks()` while a commit scope is set, so a finding outside that commit's diff stays in the commit's summary instead of moving to a nearby line. `pytest tests/unittest` on 912963d8: 17692 passed, 34 skipped. `ruff check`: clean.

**What changes for a user**

* Nothing unless the host turns on `per_commit_review`. Default `/review` is unchanged.
* With it on: one model call per reviewed commit. The first run reviews every commit, and later runs review only new commits or commits whose own changes changed, so `-i` is no longer needed in `push_commands`.
* Each commit's review sees only that commit's diff, so it can flag something a later commit fixes, or miss a helper added in an earlier commit.
* Only GitHub and GitLab support it. Other providers get the usual whole PR review with a one line notice.

comment.body:
Hey @IsmaelMartinez, hope you're doing well, and it's me again, thanks once more for the reviews on #4603! Thank you for running the `_Host` fake against the 20 commit case and the rebase, that's really reassuring to see.

Both doc points are in 93cb7440, in "Reviewing each commit separately". It now says that `minimal_commits_for_incremental_review` and `minimal_minutes_for_incremental_review` don't apply to per commit review, since each run picks the unreviewed commits from the markers in the bot's own comments instead of going through the `-i` thresholds. It also says that if those comments are removed, the next run reviews every commit again, and that setting `max_commits_per_review` caps that: with more unreviewed commits than the limit, the whole PR gets one review with a notice.

`main` had moved again, so I merged it back in 9723af3a. The only conflict was the key count in `test_config_reference.py`, now main's 319 plus our 2. Since #4838 renamed `tools` to `commands`, ed7715a5 points the per commit tests and the config doc links at the new paths. The unit suite (17692 passed) and ruff pass locally. I also resolved the two inline suggestions from yesterday, since they landed in 181edc4c.

Does the wording read right to you? Happy to tweak it, and any tips are always welcome. @Hi-Angel, hope things have calmed down on your side!

issue.title: fix(js): clear dynamic flag on actions registered by v2 plugins
issue.body:
Tools that a plugin provides were being registered again on every generate call, printing an error each time, and now they are registered once.

**What this code is for**

`registerActionV2` in `js/genkit/src/genkit.ts` takes every action a v2 plugin returns from `init()` or `resolve()` and puts it in the Genkit registry under the plugin's name. Later, `ai.generate({ tools })` in `js/ai/src/generate.ts` calls `maybeRegisterDynamicTools`, which registers any tool still marked `metadata.dynamic` into the registry for that one call.

**Before this PR**

A plugin author returns `tool({ name: 'weather', ... })` from `init()` and then calls `ai.generate({ tools: [weather] })` twice.

1. `tool()` builds the action with `metadata: { type: 'tool', dynamic: true }`.
2. `registerActionV2` registers it as `/tool/myPlugin/weather`, but leaves `dynamic: true` in place. Only `defineTool()` and `defineInterrupt()` delete it.
3. `ai.generate()` calls `maybeRegisterDynamicTools`, and `isDynamicTool(weather)` returns `true`.
4. So `registerAction` runs again on an action that already has `__registry` set, and `__registry` is moved to the child registry that this one generate call creates.
5. The log shows `ERROR: /tool/myPlugin/weather already registered.` once per tool on every generate call (and `already has an entry in the registry. Overwriting.` when it lands in the same registry, as in the issue).

**After this PR**

Same plugin, same two generate calls.

1. Same as above through step 1.
2. `registerActionV2` deletes `metadata.dynamic` before it calls `registerAction`.
3. `ai.generate()` calls `maybeRegisterDynamicTools`, and `isDynamicTool(weather)` now returns `false`, so it skips it.
4. `toolsToActionRefs` still turns the action into `/tool/myPlugin/weather`, and the model call finds it in the registry where the plugin put it.
5. No error lines, and `weather.__registry` stays `ai.registry`.
6. A tool built with `tool()` and passed straight to `generate()`, without a plugin, still has `dynamic: true` and is registered for that call as before.

**The diagram**

```mermaid
flowchart LR

classDef box fill:#eef1ff,stroke:#4c5bd4,color:#111827
classDef bad fill:#ffd6d6,stroke:#cc0000,color:#111827,stroke-width:3px
classDef good fill:#c8f0c8,stroke:#008800,color:#111827,stroke-width:3px

subgraph BEFORE["BEFORE: 1 ERROR line per tool per generate"]
direction TB
  B1["plugin init returns tool()"] --> B2["registerActionV2 registers it"]
  B2 --> B3["metadata.dynamic stays true"]
  B3 --> B4["ai.generate with tools"]
  B4 --> B5{"isDynamicTool(t)?"}
  B5 -->|"true for the plugin tool"| B6["registerAction again, ERROR logged"]
  B5 -->|"false"| B7["uses the registered tool"]
end

subgraph AFTER["AFTER: 0 ERROR lines"]
direction TB
  A1["plugin init returns tool()"] --> A2["registerActionV2 registers it"]
  A2 --> A3["THE CHANGE: metadata.dynamic deleted"]
  A3 --> A4["ai.generate with tools"]
  A4 --> A5{"isDynamicTool(t)?"}
  A5 -->|"false for the plugin tool"| A6["uses the registered tool, no log"]
  A5 -->|"true for a tool() passed directly"| A7["registered for this call, as before"]
end

B1 ~~~ A1

class B1,B2,B4,B5,B7 box
class A1,A2,A4,A5,A7 box
class B3,B6 bad
class A3,A6 good

linkStyle 4 stroke:#cc0000,stroke-width:5px
linkStyle 10 stroke:#008800,stroke-width:5px

style BEFORE fill:#fff5f5,stroke:#cc0000,color:#111827
style AFTER fill:#f3fff3,stroke:#008800,color:#111827
```

**The change**

One line in `registerActionV2`, right before `registry.registerAction(...)`:

```ts
delete resolvedAction.__action.metadata?.dynamic;
```

This is the same thing `defineTool()` does at `js/ai/src/tool.ts` before it registers. It runs for every action a v2 plugin hands back, from `init()` and from `resolve()`, so plain tools, `multipart: true` tools, and a resource built with `resource()` all stop being treated as dynamic once they are in the registry.

A new test in `js/genkit/tests/plugins_test.ts` builds a v2 plugin that returns a plain tool and a multipart tool from `init()` and a third tool from `resolve()`, calls `generate()` twice with all three, and checks that `logger.error` was never called and every tool's `__registry` is still `ai.registry`. Without the change it fails with six `already registered` errors.

Thank you @cabljac for the very clear report with file and line pointers, it made this quick to reproduce. The issue offered two directions, exporting a plugin facing `tool` factory from `genkit/plugin` or clearing `dynamic` in `registerActionV2`, and @aslamalkarywk7 also raised both in #6387 (thank you for that earlier work, the parent registry detail from that thread helped me check the child registry case). I went with the second one here since it is one line and also covers `resolve()`, but I would really value your view on which you prefer, and I am happy to switch to the factory or add one on top.

Two things I would love your opinion on:

- `defineTool()` also registers a `tool.v2` copy of a plain tool. A plugin tool still does not get that copy. `generate()` does not need it when the tool is passed as an action, so I left it out to keep this small. Would you like it added here?
- After this change, a tool from one Genkit instance's plugin that is passed to `generate()` on a different instance, which does not have that plugin, is no longer registered into that other instance for the call. That now matches how a `defineTool()` tool already behaves. Does that sound right to you?

**What changes for a user**

- Plugin tools passed to `ai.generate({ tools })` no longer print `already registered` or `Overwriting` errors.
- The plugin tool stays registered where the plugin put it, and its action metadata no longer carries `dynamic: true`.
- Tools passed to `generate()` by name still resolve as before.
- A tool built with `tool()` and passed straight to `generate()`, with no plugin involved, is still registered for that call as before.
- Models, embedders and other plugin actions never had `dynamic` set, so nothing changes for them.

- [x] PR title follows conventional commits
- [x] PR description contains context and the bug link
- [x] Tested (unit test, plus the reproduction from the issue before and after)
- [x] Docs/readmes: no change needed

Closes #6381

issue.title: fix(cli): repeating a single value option is silently accepted
issue.body:
Repeating an option that takes one value made deploy quietly do nothing and still report success, and now the CLI stops right away with a clear error.

**What this code is for**

`parseCommandLineArguments` turns what a person types after `cdk` into the `argv` object every command reads. It is generated by `yargs-gen.ts` from `cli-config.ts`, and it calls functions from `yargs-helpers.ts` through `.middleware(...)` before yargs validates the arguments.

**Before this PR**

A CI job runs `cdk deploy --concurrency 1 --concurrency 10 --all`.

1. yargs sees `--concurrency` twice and stores both values, so `argv.concurrency` is `[1, 10]`.
2. Nothing checks it, and `cli.ts` passes `concurrency: args.concurrency` on to the deploy.
3. The app is synthesized as normal.
4. `forAllArtifacts` checks `typeof n === 'number'`. `[1, 10]` is not a number, so it is used as the per type limit record.
5. `max['stack']` is `undefined`, so `active[node.type] < max[node.type]` is never true and no stack starts.
6. The promise never settles, Node has nothing left to run, and the process exits with code 0. CI shows green and nothing was deployed.

**After this PR**

Same CI job, same command.

1. Same as above through step 1: `argv.concurrency` is `[1, 10]`.
2. Before validation, `yargsRejectRepeatedOptions` asks yargs for the types it holds for the running command with `getOptions()`.
3. `concurrency` is in the `number` list and its value is an array, so it throws `ToolkitError('RepeatedOption', ...)`.
4. The CLI prints `--concurrency can only be specified once, but got: 1, 10` and exits with code 1, before synth starts.
5. A job that runs `cdk deploy -c a=1 -c b=2 --parameters P1=x --parameters P2=y` still gets every value, because `context` and `parameters` are declared with `type: 'array'` and are not in the `string` or `number` lists.

**The diagram**

```mermaid
flowchart LR

classDef box fill:#eef1ff,stroke:#4c5bd4,color:#111827
classDef bad fill:#ffd6d6,stroke:#cc0000,color:#111827,stroke-width:3px
classDef good fill:#c8f0c8,stroke:#008800,color:#111827,stroke-width:3px

subgraph BEFORE["BEFORE: 0 stacks deployed, exit code 0"]
direction TB
  B1["cdk deploy --concurrency 1 --concurrency 10"] --> B2["parseCommandLineArguments"]
  B2 --> B3["argv.concurrency is [1, 10]"]
  B3 --> B4{"forAllArtifacts: typeof n === 'number'"}
  B4 -->|"array, max['stack'] is undefined"| B5["no stack starts, exit 0"]
  B4 -->|"--concurrency given once"| B6["stacks deploy"]
end

subgraph AFTER["AFTER: clear error, exit code 1"]
direction TB
  A1["cdk deploy --concurrency 1 --concurrency 10"] --> A2["parseCommandLineArguments"]
  A2 --> A3["argv.concurrency is [1, 10]"]
  A3 --> A4{"THE CHANGE: string or number option holds an array"}
  A4 -->|"yes"| A5["RepeatedOption error, exit 1"]
  A4 -->|"no, e.g. -c a=1 -c b=2"| A6["parses as before, every value kept"]
end

B1 ~~~ A1

class B1,B2,B3,B6 box
class A1,A2,A3,A6 box
class B4,B5 bad
class A4,A5 good

linkStyle 3 stroke:#cc0000,stroke-width:5px
linkStyle 8 stroke:#008800,stroke-width:5px

style BEFORE fill:#fff5f5,stroke:#cc0000,color:#111827
style AFTER fill:#f3fff3,stroke:#008800,color:#111827
```

**The change**

The fix is the new `yargsRejectRepeatedOptions` in `yargs-helpers.ts`. It reads `getOptions()` from the yargs instance it is handed, joins the `string` and `number` lists, and throws on the first key whose `argv` value is an array. Because yargs fills those lists from each option's declared `type` for the command that is running, this covers every command and every global option without a hand kept list.

`yargs-gen.ts` registers it once with `.middleware(helpers.yargsRejectRepeatedOptions, true)` right after `.usage(...)`, so `parse-command-line-arguments.ts` gains that one generated line, and the three generator snapshots gain it too.

This follows the direction @ashishdhingra suggested in the issue: throw when an option is repeated, and apply that to every option that takes a single value. It also keeps the point @cmaster11 made in the report: switching off `duplicate-arguments-array` for everything would break options that are meant to repeat, like `-c`.

Booleans are left out on purpose. yargs already keeps the last value for repeated flags and counts (`--force --force` is `true`, `-v -v` is `2`), so they never arrive as arrays.

The new tests in `parse-command-line-arguments.test.ts` cover a repeated number (`deploy --concurrency`), a number through its alias (`flags -n 1 --concurrency 2`), a string with `choices` (`deploy --method`) and a global string through its alias (`synth -a a --app b`). All four fail on `main` and pass with this change. A last test checks that positionals, `-c`, `--parameters`, `-v -v` and `--force --force` still parse as before. Each rejection case loads a fresh copy of the module with `jest.isolateModules`, because yargs is shared across the process and a parse that throws does not reset its state.

**What changes for a user**

- Repeating a string or number option (`--concurrency`, `--method`, `--app`, `--profile` and the rest) now fails with a clear message and exit code 1, instead of a silent exit 0 or a value nobody chose.
- Options meant to repeat (`-c`, `--parameters`, `--plugin`, `--notification-arns`, `--tags` and other `array` options) work exactly as before.
- Repeated boolean flags and `-v -v` work exactly as before.
- I went with an error rather than letting the last value win, since that is what was suggested in the issue and it surfaces the mistake in CI. If you would rather have last value wins, or a different message, I am very happy to change it. I'd love to hear what you think.

Fixes aws/aws-cdk#30752

issue.title: Chat Completions streaming merges parallel tool calls when deltas have no `index`

comment.body:
Hey @OsamaAnsar, hope you're doing well! Thanks for the really clear repro, the synthetic chunk test made this super easy to poke at. Your rule of starting a new call when a delta carries an id or a name looks right to me, and I tried it locally against main.

Two small things I ran into along the way, curious what you both think:

1. The custom tool skip set is keyed by `index` too ([L303](https://github.com/openai/openai-agents-js/blob/7589b9c40120b89a7d2d28a5a60b4defe1ed7bf5/packages/agents-openai/src/openaiChatCompletionsStreaming.ts#L303), [L313](https://github.com/openai/openai-agents-js/blob/7589b9c40120b89a7d2d28a5a60b4defe1ed7bf5/packages/agents-openai/src/openaiChatCompletionsStreaming.ts#L313)). If a custom call shows up without an index, it adds `undefined`, and every later call without an index gets skipped. Locally, a custom call followed by `get_time` gave me zero function calls. So I think the skip check would need the same key the function calls end up using.

2. With empty ids, the split calls still come out with `callId: ''` ([L323](https://github.com/openai/openai-agents-js/blob/7589b9c40120b89a7d2d28a5a60b4defe1ed7bf5/packages/agents-openai/src/openaiChatCompletionsStreaming.ts#L323), [L330](https://github.com/openai/openai-agents-js/blob/7589b9c40120b89a7d2d28a5a60b4defe1ed7bf5/packages/agents-openai/src/openaiChatCompletionsStreaming.ts#L330)), and the runner rejects that before running any tool with `Tool invocation is missing a non-empty call ID.` ([runContext.ts L466](https://github.com/openai/openai-agents-js/blob/7589b9c40120b89a7d2d28a5a60b4defe1ed7bf5/packages/agents-core/src/runContext.ts#L466-L468)). I hit that with a single empty id call too, so I think the Gemini case needs a fallback id on top of the split.

For the fallback, the simplest default I can think of is filling one in only when the provider sends nothing, for example from the response id plus the call's position in the stream. One catch I noticed is that `response.id` can be empty as well (the converter already falls back to `FAKE_ID` there), so that version could repeat across turns. Would the maintainers prefer something like that, or a random id? It just needs to stay unique per call, since a reused id with different arguments also throws. Happy to test whatever fix lands against your four cases plus these two.

issue.title: server: read authorize parameters from the POST form body
issue.body:
Fixes #195

A sign in request sent as a POST form to `/authorize` was rejected for a missing `redirect_uri`; now the form values are read the same as query values.

**What this code is for**

`serveAuthorize` in `server/authorize.go` handles `/authorize`, the first step of an OAuth sign in. A relying party sends the user there with `client_id`, `redirect_uri`, `state`, `nonce`, `scope` and PKCE values. It checks the client and redirect, asks `WhoIs` who the user is, stores an `AuthRequest`, and redirects back with a `code`.

**Before this PR**

A relying party signs a user in by sending `POST /authorize` with `client_id` and `redirect_uri` in an `application/x-www-form-urlencoded` body.

1. `serveAuthorize` checks `r.Method` and allows `POST`.
2. It reads parameters with `uq := r.URL.Query()`, which only holds the query string.
3. The query string is empty, so `uq.Get("redirect_uri")` returns `""`.
4. The user gets `400 invalid_request - must specify redirect_uri`.

**After this PR**

Same relying party, same `POST /authorize`.

1. `serveAuthorize` checks `r.Method` and allows `POST`.
2. It calls `r.ParseForm()` and reads parameters from `r.Form`, which holds the body values and the query values.
3. `uq.Get("redirect_uri")` and `uq.Get("client_id")` return the values from the body.
4. The client and redirect checks pass and the user is redirected back with a `code`.

A `GET /authorize` with parameters in the query string goes through the same steps and works as before.

**The diagram**

```mermaid
flowchart LR

classDef box fill:#eef1ff,stroke:#4c5bd4,color:#111827
classDef bad fill:#ffd6d6,stroke:#cc0000,color:#111827,stroke-width:3px
classDef good fill:#c8f0c8,stroke:#008800,color:#111827,stroke-width:3px

subgraph BEFORE["BEFORE: POST form gets 400"]
direction TB
  B1["POST /authorize with form body"] --> B2["serveAuthorize allows POST"]
  B2 --> B3["uq := r.URL.Query()"]
  B3 --> B4{"redirect_uri in query?"}
  B4 -->|"POST body ignored"| B5["400 must specify redirect_uri"]
  B4 -->|"GET with query"| B6["redirect with code"]
end

subgraph AFTER["AFTER: POST form gets a code"]
direction TB
  A1["POST /authorize with form body"] --> A2["serveAuthorize allows POST"]
  A2 --> A3["r.ParseForm()"]
  A3 --> A4{"THE CHANGE: uq := r.Form"}
  A4 -->|"POST body read"| A5["redirect with code"]
  A4 -->|"GET with query"| A6["redirect with code, same as before"]
end

B1 ~~~ A1

class B1,B2,B3,B6 box
class A1,A2,A3,A6 box
class B4,B5 bad
class A4,A5 good

linkStyle 3 stroke:#cc0000,stroke-width:5px
linkStyle 8 stroke:#008800,stroke-width:5px

style BEFORE fill:#fff5f5,stroke:#cc0000,color:#111827
style AFTER fill:#f3fff3,stroke:#008800,color:#111827
```

**The change**

In `serveAuthorize`, `uq := r.URL.Query()` becomes a call to `r.ParseForm()` followed by `uq := r.Form`. Every later `uq.Get(...)` call is unchanged. When `r.ParseForm()` returns an error, the handler returns `400 invalid_request` with `failed to parse form`, the same way `server/ui.go` handles it.

`server/authorize_test.go` adds `usePOSTForm` and `rawBody` to `TestServeAuthorize`, with rows for a POST form that issues a code and keeps `state` and `nonce`, a POST form without `redirect_uri`, and a POST body that cannot be parsed.

**What changes for a user**

- Clients that send `/authorize` as a POST form now complete sign in.
- `GET /authorize` with a query string works as before.
- If a value is sent in both the body and the query string, `uq.Get` returns the body value, because `r.Form` lists body values first.
- A request whose body or query string cannot be parsed, such as an invalid `%` escape, now gets `400 invalid_request` instead of having the bad pair dropped. Taken on purpose, so a malformed request is reported instead of half read.

issue.title: fix(core): honor HTTPS_PROXY for X.509 workload identity mTLS
issue.body:
Apps that sign in with a client certificate (X.509 workload identity federation) could not get a token behind a required proxy, and now those requests go through the proxy and still present the certificate.

**What this code is for**

When a credential file has `credential_source.certificate`, `IdentityPoolClient.retrieveSubjectToken()` asks `CertificateSubjectTokenSupplier` to read the client certificate and key, then builds two `Gaxios` instances that use them: one for the STS token exchange at `sts.mtls.googleapis.com` and one (`this.transporter`) for the service account impersonation call. In gaxios, `#prepareRequest()` decides how each request connects: a caller supplied `agent` wins, otherwise it builds an `HttpsProxyAgent` when `HTTPS_PROXY`/`https_proxy` is set and `NO_PROXY` does not match, otherwise it builds an `https.Agent` from `cert` and `key`.

**Before this PR**

A workload in a network where all outbound traffic must go through a proxy runs `client.getAccessToken()` with `HTTPS_PROXY=http://127.0.0.1:3128`, as in the steps @moibueno shared in #9594.

1. `retrieveSubjectToken()` calls `createMtlsHttpsAgent()`, which returns `new https.Agent({key, cert})`.
2. That agent is passed as `new Gaxios({agent: mtlsAgent})` for STS and as `agent` on `this.transporter`.
3. In `#prepareRequest()`, `if (opts.agent)` is true, so gaxios skips the proxy branch.
4. The token request opens a direct TLS connection to `sts.mtls.googleapis.com:443`.
5. The proxy logs 0 CONNECT requests, the firewall drops the direct connection, and `getAccessToken()` fails.

There is a second problem in gaxios. Even a request that reaches the gaxios proxy branch with `cert` and `key` does not send the certificate to the server: `HttpsProxyAgent` uses those options only for its own connection to the proxy, and the TLS connection to the server behind the proxy gets no client certificate. I checked this with a local CONNECT proxy and a local server that asks for a client certificate: the request went through the tunnel, but the server saw an empty peer certificate.

**After this PR**

Same workload, same `HTTPS_PROXY`, same `getAccessToken()` call.

1. `retrieveSubjectToken()` calls `getMtlsOptions()`, which returns `{cert, key}` as strings.
2. Those are passed as `new Gaxios(mtlsOptions)` for STS and spread into `this.transporter`, with `agent: undefined` so an inherited agent cannot hide the certificate.
3. In `#prepareRequest()`, there is no agent yet, so the proxy branch runs, honoring `HTTPS_PROXY`, `https_proxy` and `NO_PROXY` the same way as every other gaxios request.
4. The new `HttpsProxyAgent` adds `cert` and `key` to the TLS connection to the server whenever `target.secureEndpoint` is true.
5. The proxy logs `CONNECT sts.mtls.googleapis.com:443`, the STS server receives the client certificate through the tunnel, and the token comes back. The impersonation call takes the same path.

When `NO_PROXY` matches the host, step 3 takes the existing `cert`/`key` branch instead and connects directly with an `https.Agent`, same as before.

**The diagram**

```mermaid
flowchart LR

classDef box fill:#eef1ff,stroke:#4c5bd4,color:#111827
classDef bad fill:#ffd6d6,stroke:#cc0000,color:#111827,stroke-width:3px
classDef good fill:#c8f0c8,stroke:#008800,color:#111827,stroke-width:3px

subgraph BEFORE["BEFORE: 0 CONNECT requests at the proxy"]
direction TB
  B1["getAccessToken() with HTTPS_PROXY set"] --> B2["retrieveSubjectToken() reads cert and key"]
  B2 --> B3["createMtlsHttpsAgent() returns https.Agent"]
  B3 --> B4{"opts.agent is set, proxy skipped"}
  B4 -->|"direct TLS to sts.mtls.googleapis.com"| B5["blocked, no token"]
  B4 -->|"no proxy in the network"| B6["direct mTLS works"]
end

subgraph AFTER["AFTER: CONNECT through the proxy, certificate sent"]
direction TB
  A1["getAccessToken() with HTTPS_PROXY set"] --> A2["retrieveSubjectToken() reads cert and key"]
  A2 --> A3["getMtlsOptions() returns cert and key"]
  A3 --> A4{"THE CHANGE: gaxios chooses the agent"}
  A4 -->|"HttpsProxyAgent adds cert to inner TLS"| A5["token through the proxy"]
  A4 -->|"NO_PROXY matches"| A6["direct mTLS, same as before"]
end

B1 ~~~ A1

class B1,B2,B3,B6 box
class A1,A2,A3,A6 box
class B4,B5 bad
class A4,A5 good

linkStyle 3 stroke:#cc0000,stroke-width:5px
linkStyle 8 stroke:#008800,stroke-width:5px

style BEFORE fill:#fff5f5,stroke:#cc0000,color:#111827
style AFTER fill:#f3fff3,stroke:#008800,color:#111827
```

**The change**

There are two edits, and both are needed for the token request to work behind a proxy, plus one cache change in gaxios that the second edit makes necessary.

- `google-auth-library`: `createMtlsHttpsAgent()` is replaced by `getMtlsOptions()`, and `retrieveSubjectToken()` passes `cert` and `key` to `Gaxios` instead of a prebuilt agent. This is the first option @moibueno suggested in the issue, and it reuses the proxy and `NO_PROXY` handling gaxios already has, so the library does not read proxy variables itself. `CertificateSubjectTokenSupplier` is not exported from the package index.
- `gaxios`: in the proxy branch of `#prepareRequest()`, when both `cert` and `key` are set, the `HttpsProxyAgent` instance gets a `connect` that adds them to the options for the TLS connection to the server (only when `target.secureEndpoint` is true). The options for the connection to the proxy itself stay as they were.
- `gaxios`: the proxy agent cache key now includes `cert` and `key` when both are set, instead of the proxy URL alone. Since the cached agent now presents its certificate to every https server it reaches, reusing it would send one caller's certificate on a later request made without one, and a first request without a certificate would make later mTLS requests go out without it.

Tests: `test.identitypoolclient.ts` checks that both the STS and impersonation requests use a proxy agent carrying the certificate with `HTTPS_PROXY`, that `https_proxy` plus a `NO_PROXY` match on the STS host sends STS direct with the certificate and impersonation through the proxy, and that a `transporterOptions.agent` does not drop the certificate. `test.getch.ts` checks that the proxy agent passes `cert` and `key` to the server connection, and that requests without a certificate or with a different one get their own agent. The first two auth tests and the new gaxios tests fail without this change.

A few things I would really value your opinion on, since you know this code far better than I do:

- `google-auth-library` depends on `gaxios` from npm (`^8.3.1`). Until the gaxios floor is raised, a user with `HTTPS_PROXY` set and an older gaxios would now go through the proxy without the certificate, so a setup that works today because direct connections happen to be allowed would start failing at STS. Would you prefer that I bump the floor in this PR, or right after the gaxios release, or do you usually handle that in the dependency floor updates?
- I kept both packages in one PR because neither half fixes the issue alone. I am very happy to split it into a gaxios PR and an auth PR if that is easier to review and release.
- Two existing gaxios tests (`should load the proxy from the cache with mTLS` and the Bun fetch test) expected a request without a certificate to reuse the cached mTLS proxy agent. I updated them so that request now gets its own agent with no certificate, because otherwise the certificate would reach servers it was not meant for. If that reuse was relied on somewhere I am not aware of, I would be grateful to hear it and happy to find another way.

**What changes for a user**

- With `HTTPS_PROXY` or `https_proxy` set, the STS token exchange and the impersonation call now go through the proxy and present the client certificate to Google.
- `NO_PROXY` is honored for these requests, the same way as for every other request the library makes.
- Without any proxy set, requests connect directly with the client certificate, as before.
- A custom `transporterOptions.agent` is still replaced for these requests, so the certificate is always used, as before.
- The workaround from the issue that replaced `createMtlsHttpsAgent` on the supplier is no longer needed; that method is no longer called.
- Thank you @moibueno for the very clear report and the two suggested fixes, which made this easy to follow.

- [x] Make sure to open an issue as a bug/issue before writing your code
- [x] Ensure the tests and linter pass
- [x] Code coverage does not decrease (if any source code was changed)
- [x] Appropriate docs were updated (if necessary)

Fixes #9594

issue.title: golink: escape the path remainder appended to non-template links
issue.body:
Fixes #255

Opening a go link with an encoded `%`, `?` or `#` after the link name returned a 500 or redirected to the wrong address; now those characters stay in the redirect path.

**What this code is for**

`serveGo` handles a request such as `http://go/who/100%25`. It splits the path into the link name (`who`) and the rest (`100%`), loads the link, and calls `expandLink` to build the redirect target. For a link without a template, `expandLink` adds the rest of the path to the end of the long URL.

**Before this PR**

A person has a link `who` that points to `http://who/` and opens `http://go/who/100%25`.

1. `serveGo` reads `r.URL.Path`, which Go has already decoded, so the rest of the path is `100%`.
2. `expandLink` sees no `{{` in the long URL and adds `{{.Path}}` to it.
3. The template writes `100%` as is, giving `http://who/100%`.
4. `url.Parse` rejects it with `invalid URL escape "%"`.
5. The person gets a 500. For `/who/a%3Fb` the target becomes `http://who/a?b`, so `b` moves into the query.

**After this PR**

Same person, same request.

1. `serveGo` reads the same decoded rest of the path, `100%`.
2. `expandLink` calls `expandTemplate`, which sees no `{{` and calls `appendPath`.
3. `appendPath` adds `/` if needed and then the path written by `(&url.URL{Path: path}).EscapedPath()`, giving `http://who/100%25`.
4. `url.Parse` accepts it and the person is redirected to `http://who/100%25`. `/who/a%3Fb` redirects to `http://who/a%3Fb`.

**The diagram**

```mermaid
flowchart LR

classDef box fill:#eef1ff,stroke:#4c5bd4,color:#111827
classDef bad fill:#ffd6d6,stroke:#cc0000,color:#111827,stroke-width:3px
classDef good fill:#c8f0c8,stroke:#008800,color:#111827,stroke-width:3px
```

**The change**

In `golink.go`, the branch of `expandLink` for links without `{{` no longer adds `{{.Path}}` or `{{with .Path}}/{{.}}{{end}}` to the long URL. It moves into `expandTemplate`, which calls the new `appendPath`. `appendPath` returns the long URL unchanged when the rest of the path is empty, adds `/` when the long URL does not end in one, and adds the rest written by `EscapedPath`. That escapes `%`, `?`, `#` and spaces, and keeps `/`, `+` and `:` as they are. Links with a template run the same template code as before.

`golink_test.go` adds rows to `TestExpandLink` for `100%`, `a?b`, `a#b`, `a/b+c`, and `100%` with a query string.

**What changes for a user**

- `go/who/100%25` redirects to `http://who/100%25` instead of returning a 500.
- `go/who/a%3Fb` and `go/who/a%23b` keep `?` and `#` in the path instead of starting a query or fragment.
- Plain paths such as `go/who/a/b` and query strings on the request still redirect the same way.
- Links with a template still get the decoded value in `.Path`, so `{{PathEscape .Path}}` and the other template functions behave as before.

issue.title: fix(js/ai): keep primitive items in the array output format
issue.body:
Checklist: - [x] PR title is following https://www.conventionalcommits.org/en/v1.0.0/ - [x] PR description contains enough context, bug link, code samples for new APIs - [x] Tested (manually, unit tested, etc.) - [ ] Docs/readmes updated (not needed, no API or documented behavior for object arrays changes) Fixes #2008 Asking a model for a list of words or numbers now returns that list instead of an empty one. ## What this code is for When a developer asks for output in the `array` format, `extractItems` reads the model's text and pulls out each finished item of the list. It runs on every streamed chunk and again on the final message. ## Before Priya builds a feature that suggests colour names. 1. Priya calls generate with output format `array` and a schema whose items are strings. 2. The model replies `["red", "green", "blue"]`. 3. Genkit scans the reply for items but only collects ones that open with `{`. 4. Priya gets `[]` as the output, and every streamed chunk is empty too. ## After Priya builds a feature that suggests colour names. 1. Priya calls generate with output format `array` and a schema whose items are strings. 2. The model replies `["red", "green", "blue"]`. 3. Genkit collects every finished item in the list: a string once its closing quote arrives, a number, `true`, `false` or `null` once the next comma or closing bracket arrives, an object or nested array once it closes. 4. Priya gets `["red", "green", "blue"]`, and the streamed chunks carry each colour as it completes. ```mermaid flowchart LR subgraph BEFORE direction TB B1["Model replies with a list of colour names"] --> B2["Genkit keeps only items that open with a brace"] B2 ==> B3["Priya gets an empty list"] end subgraph AFTER direction TB A1["Model replies with a list of colour names"] --> A2["THE CHANGE
Genkit keeps every finished item"] A2 ==> A3["Priya gets the colour names"] A2 --> A4["A list of objects comes back as before"] end B1 ~~~ A1 linkStyle 1 stroke:#c62828,stroke-width:4px linkStyle 3 stroke:#2e7d32,stroke-width:4px ``` ## The change `extractItems` in `js/ai/src/extract.ts` now tracks nesting depth across both braces and brackets instead of counting braces only. At the top level of the list it takes a string at its closing quote, takes any other value at the next comma or closing bracket, and takes an object or nested array when it closes. Single and double quotes are both treated as strings, so a bracket or comma inside a string does not end an item. When no opening bracket has arrived yet, the returned cursor stays at 0, so the next chunk still searches for the start of the list. New cases in `js/ai/tests/extract_test.ts` and `js/ai/tests/formats/array_test.ts` cover strings, numbers, booleans, `null`, nested arrays, a number split across two chunks, and a reply where the opening bracket arrives in a later chunk. They fail on main and pass with this change. ## What changes for a user Lists of strings, numbers, booleans, `null` and nested lists now come back from the `array` format, both streamed and final. Lists of objects return the same items at the same points in the stream as before. Text before the list, such as a code fence or a short intro, is still skipped. A number that is still arriving is held back until the next comma or closing bracket, so a chunk never reports `2` when the full value is `23`.

**What this code is for**
