issue.title: fix(payments): send MPP credential in the header the challenge selects

labels.name: user-8213b3f8/repo-41623133
labels.description: PR size: S

issue.body:
Fixes #702

A paid MPP request whose server asks for the credential in `Payment-Authorization` now sends it there, so the payment is accepted and the caller's own login token is kept.

**What this code is for**

`PaymentManager.generate_payment_header` handles an HTTP 402 response. For MPP it reads the `WWW-Authenticate: Payment` challenges with `parse_www_authenticate`, picks one with `select_challenge`, pays it through `ProcessPayment`, and returns the header to attach when the request is sent again. The Strands plugin and the LangGraph middleware put that header on the retried request with `apply_payment_header`.

**Before this PR**

An agent calls an mppx server created with `requiresAuth: true`, sending `Authorization: Bearer <token>`.

1. The server replies 402 with a challenge that includes `header="Payment-Authorization"`.
2. `parse_www_authenticate` keeps the challenge and `select_challenge` selects it.
3. `ProcessPayment` is called and the payment is made.
4. `_generate_mpp_payment_header` always returns `{"Authorization": "Payment <credential>"}`.
5. `apply_payment_header` writes that over the caller's `Authorization: Bearer <token>`.
6. The server looks for the credential only in `Payment-Authorization`, finds nothing, and the request fails after the money was spent.

**After this PR**

Same agent, same server.

1. Same as above through step 3.
2. `_generate_mpp_payment_header` sees `header` on the selected challenge and returns `{"Payment-Authorization": "Payment <credential>"}`.
3. `apply_payment_header` adds it next to `Authorization: Bearer <token>`, which stays as it was.
4. The server reads the credential from `Payment-Authorization` and serves the resource.
5. A challenge without `header` still returns `{"Authorization": "Payment <credential>"}`.
6. A challenge with any other `header` value is dropped by `_is_valid_challenge`, so it is never paid.

**The diagram**

```mermaid
flowchart LR

classDef box fill:#eef1ff,stroke:#4c5bd4,color:#111827
classDef bad fill:#ffd6d6,stroke:#cc0000,color:#111827,stroke-width:3px
classDef good fill:#c8f0c8,stroke:#008800,color:#111827,stroke-width:3px

subgraph BEFORE["BEFORE: paid, then rejected"]
direction TB
  B1["402 with header=Payment-Authorization"] --> B2["select_challenge"]
  B2 --> B3["ProcessPayment"]
  B3 --> B4{"always Authorization"}
  B4 -->|"Bearer token overwritten"| B5["server finds no credential"]
  B4 -->|"challenge without header"| B6["Authorization: Payment, works"]
end

subgraph AFTER["AFTER: paid and accepted"]
direction TB
  A1["402 with header=Payment-Authorization"] --> A2["select_challenge"]
  A2 --> A3["ProcessPayment"]
  A3 --> A4{"THE CHANGE: header on challenge?"}
  A4 -->|"yes"| A5["Payment-Authorization: Payment, Bearer kept"]
  A4 -->|"no"| A6["Authorization: Payment, works"]
end

B1 ~~~ A1

class B1,B2,B3,B6 box
class A1,A2,A3,A6 box
class B4,B5 bad
class A4,A5 good

linkStyle 3 stroke:#cc0000,stroke-width:5px
linkStyle 8 stroke:#008800,stroke-width:5px

style BEFORE fill:#fff5f5,stroke:#cc0000,color:#111827
style AFTER fill:#f3fff3,stroke:#008800,color:#111827
```

**The change**

The fix is in `_generate_mpp_payment_header`: the returned key is now `MPP_PAYMENT_AUTHORIZATION_HEADER if "header" in selected else "Authorization"`. The new constant `MPP_PAYMENT_AUTHORIZATION_HEADER = "Payment-Authorization"` lives in `constants.py`.

The second change is a check in `_is_valid_challenge`: a challenge whose `header` is anything other than `Payment-Authorization` is treated as invalid. The spec says a client must not send a credential for such a challenge, so this stops the SDK from paying one. If no other challenge is payable, `generate_payment_header` raises `PaymentError` as it already does when nothing can be selected.

Tests: `test_payment_authorization_header_param_is_accepted`, `test_unrecognized_header_param_is_rejected` in `test_mpp.py`, and `test_payment_authorization_challenge_returns_payment_authorization_header`, `test_unrecognized_header_challenge_is_not_paid` in `test_mpp_manager.py`.

**What changes for a user**

- Servers that send `header="Payment-Authorization"` now get the credential where they read it, and the request succeeds after payment.
- The caller's own `Authorization` header is no longer overwritten in that case.
- Servers that do not send `header` see no change.
- A challenge with an unknown `header` value is no longer paid. If it was the only option, the call now fails before any money moves instead of after.
- The credential's `challenge` object is built by the service from the raw challenge, which already includes `header`, so this PR does not touch that part.

issue.title: fix: anchor Claude Code hook command to CLAUDE_PROJECT_DIR
issue.body:
Refs #34

When Claude Code is started in a subfolder of a project, the 1Password env file hook failed on every Bash call, and this makes it find its script from any folder.

**What this code is for**

`install.sh --agent claude-code` copies the hook bundle into `.claude/claude-code-1password-hooks-bundle/` and writes `.claude/settings.json` from the template in this repo. That file tells Claude Code to run `bin/run-hook.sh 1password-validate-mounted-env-files` before each tool call, so mounted env files are checked first. `install.sh` rewrites `bin/run-hook.sh` in the template to the installed path with `sed`.

**Before this PR**

A developer opens a terminal in `src/` inside their project and starts Claude Code.

1. Claude Code is about to run a Bash command, so it fires the `PreToolUse` hook from `.claude/settings.json`.
2. The installed command is `.claude/claude-code-1password-hooks-bundle/bin/run-hook.sh 1password-validate-mounted-env-files`.
3. Claude Code runs it from the session's current folder, `src/`, not the project root.
4. The shell looks for `src/.claude/claude-code-1password-hooks-bundle/bin/run-hook.sh`, which does not exist.
5. Every Bash call prints `No such file or directory` and the env file check never runs.

**After this PR**

Same developer, same `src/` folder, same Bash command.

1. Same as above through step 1.
2. The installed command is now `"$CLAUDE_PROJECT_DIR"/.claude/claude-code-1password-hooks-bundle/bin/run-hook.sh 1password-validate-mounted-env-files`.
3. Claude Code sets `CLAUDE_PROJECT_DIR` to the project root for every hook ([hooks reference](https://code.claude.com/docs/en/hooks)), so the path is absolute.
4. The script is found and the env file check runs, whatever folder the session started in.

**The diagram**

```mermaid
flowchart LR

classDef box fill:#eef1ff,stroke:#4c5bd4,color:#111827
classDef bad fill:#ffd6d6,stroke:#cc0000,color:#111827,stroke-width:3px
classDef good fill:#c8f0c8,stroke:#008800,color:#111827,stroke-width:3px

subgraph BEFORE["BEFORE: hook fails on every Bash call from a subfolder"]
direction TB
  B1["developer starts Claude Code in src/"] --> B2["Bash call fires PreToolUse"]
  B2 --> B3["command runs with cwd src/"]
  B3 --> B4{"relative .claude/claude-code-1password-hooks-bundle/bin/run-hook.sh"}
  B4 -->|"looked up under src/"| B5["No such file or directory, check skipped"]
  B4 -->|"session started at project root"| B6["script found, check runs"]
end

subgraph AFTER["AFTER: hook runs from any folder"]
direction TB
  A1["developer starts Claude Code in src/"] --> A2["Bash call fires PreToolUse"]
  A2 --> A3["command runs with cwd src/"]
  A3 --> A4{"THE CHANGE: path starts with $CLAUDE_PROJECT_DIR"}
  A4 -->|"session started in src/"| A5["absolute path, script found, check runs"]
  A4 -->|"session started at project root"| A6["same absolute path, check runs"]
end

B1 ~~~ A1

class B1,B2,B3,B6 box
class A1,A2,A3,A6 box
class B4,B5 bad
class A4,A5 good

linkStyle 3 stroke:#cc0000,stroke-width:5px
linkStyle 8 stroke:#008800,stroke-width:5px

style BEFORE fill:#fff5f5,stroke:#cc0000,color:#111827
style AFTER fill:#f3fff3,stroke:#008800,color:#111827
```

**The change**

The template `.claude/settings.json` command changes from `bin/run-hook.sh ...` to `"$CLAUDE_PROJECT_DIR"/bin/run-hook.sh ...`. The existing `sed` in `install.sh` still replaces `bin/run-hook.sh`, so installed projects get `"$CLAUDE_PROJECT_DIR"/.claude/claude-code-1password-hooks-bundle/bin/run-hook.sh`. The quotes keep a project path with spaces in one piece. This is the fix.

The Claude Code example in `README.md` now shows the same command. It was also missing the `.claude/` part of the path, so copying it by hand failed even from the project root.

A new Bats test in `tests/install/install.bats` checks that `install.sh --agent claude-code` writes the anchored command. The full suite passes locally.

**What changes for a user**

- Sessions started in any subfolder now run the env file check instead of printing `No such file or directory` on every Bash call.
- Sessions started at the project root work as before.
- This repo's own `.claude/settings.json` still works, because its project root is the repo root.
- Projects installed before this change keep the old relative command until `install.sh` is run again or the line is edited, since `install.sh` never overwrites an existing `settings.json`.
- This covers only the path part of #34. The plugin request in that issue is not addressed here.

issue.title: [tabular] KNN: stop pandas FutureWarning when sampling per class
issue.body:
Fixes #5379

Fitting a KNN model on a classification dataset no longer prints a pandas deprecation warning on every fit, and the rows it trains on stay exactly the same.

**What this code is for**

`KNNModel._fit_with_samples` in `tabular/src/autogluon/tabular/models/knn/knn_model.py` fits KNN on growing row samples until it runs out of time. For `binary` and `multiclass` problems it picks rows per class through `sample_func`, so every class keeps at least one row in each sample.

**Before this PR**

A user calls `TabularPredictor(...).fit(train_data, hyperparameters={"KNN": {...}})` on a classification dataset with more rows than the first sample size.

1. `_fit_with_samples` builds `y_df`, a frame with one column, `label`.
2. For each sample size it runs `y_df.groupby("label", group_keys=False).apply(sample_func, ...)`.
3. pandas 2.2 and later see `apply` passing the grouping column `label` into `sample_func`.
4. pandas prints `FutureWarning: DataFrameGroupBy.apply operated on the grouping columns` for every sample size, on every fit.

**After this PR**

Same user, same call.

1. Same as above through step 1.
2. For each sample size it runs `y_df.groupby("label", group_keys=False)["label"].apply(sample_func, ...)`.
3. pandas runs `sample_func` on each class as a column of labels, which is not deprecated, so no warning.
4. `sample_func` picks the same number of rows with the same `random_state`, so `idx` holds the same row index as before.

**The diagram**

```mermaid
flowchart LR

classDef box fill:#eef1ff,stroke:#4c5bd4,color:#111827
classDef bad fill:#ffd6d6,stroke:#cc0000,color:#111827,stroke-width:3px
classDef good fill:#c8f0c8,stroke:#008800,color:#111827,stroke-width:3px

subgraph BEFORE["BEFORE: a FutureWarning on every fit"]
direction TB
  B1["user fits KNN on a classification dataset"] --> B2["_fit_with_samples builds y_df"]
  B2 --> B3["y_df.groupby('label').apply(sample_func)"]
  B3 --> B4["pandas warns: apply operated on the grouping columns"]
  B3 --> B5["idx = sampled rows"]
end

subgraph AFTER["AFTER: no warning, same rows"]
direction TB
  A1["user fits KNN on a classification dataset"] --> A2["_fit_with_samples builds y_df"]
  A2 --> A3["THE CHANGE: y_df.groupby('label')['label'].apply(sample_func)"]
  A3 --> A4["no warning"]
  A3 --> A5["idx = same sampled rows"]
end

B1 ~~~ A1

class B1,B2,B5 box
class A1,A2,A5 box
class B3,B4 bad
class A3,A4 good

linkStyle 2 stroke:#cc0000,stroke-width:5px
linkStyle 6 stroke:#008800,stroke-width:5px

style BEFORE fill:#fff5f5,stroke:#cc0000,color:#111827
style AFTER fill:#f3fff3,stroke:#008800,color:#111827
```

**The change**

One line in `_fit_with_samples`: `["label"]` is selected after `groupby("label", group_keys=False)` and before `.apply(sample_func, frac=samples / num_rows_max)`. `sample_func` only reads `len(chunk)` and calls `chunk.sample`, which behave the same on a column as on a one column frame. This form works on every pandas version in the supported range (`>=2.0.0,<2.4.0`), unlike `include_groups=False`, which only exists from pandas 2.2.

**What changes for a user**

- KNN fits on classification data no longer print the pandas `FutureWarning`.
- The rows picked for each sample are identical for the same seed, so trained models and scores do not change. Checked by comparing the old and new expressions on balanced, imbalanced and boolean labels at several sample fractions.
- Regression is untouched; it already samples with `np.random.choice`.
- When a future pandas release stops passing the grouping column to `apply`, this code keeps working without change.

#### AI assistance (tick exactly one)

- [ ] No AI tools were used for this PR.
- [x] AI tools were used. I have reviewed and understood every change and will answer review comments myself.
- [ ] I am an AI agent, and no human reviewed this PR before submission.

issue.body:
Hope you're doing well, @anthonykim1! Thank you for the checklist in #342186, it made these two items really easy to pick up.

Part of #342186

- `appendChunk` only appends to `lastSnapshot` while `backgroundShellId` is unset, so a long running detached watcher no longer keeps all of its output in the Agent Host while the terminal stays at 100 KB.
- `_drainingDetachedShells` now keeps `{ toolCallId, exitCode }` from the first exit report, so a failed read, a read without a code, or a reused shell ID settles the terminal with that code instead of none. The read's own code still wins.
- Tests: 9 new cases. 5 fail on `main` (the bounded `lastSnapshot` one and four exit code orders) and 4 guard behavior that already holds: the read's own code wins, a later report doesn't fill in a missing code (two orders), and a new command reusing the shell ID never hands its code to the old terminal.

```mermaid
flowchart LR
  c["background chunk"] --> t["terminal, kept at 100 KB"]
  c -.->|"before: always"| s["lastSnapshot"]
  c -.->|"after: only before backgroundShellId is set"| s
```

I left out item 3 (reading again without a cursor), since it resets and replays the terminal and felt like its own change. Also out of scope, and there before this PR: if `shell_completed` arrives before `completeToolCall` registers the detached shell, `_completeBackgroundShell` returns early and that code is dropped.

If you already have this in progress, I'm very happy to close it. And would you want a later report to fill in an exit code the first one didn't have? I kept the first report for now, since a reused shell ID can make a later code belong to a different command. Would love your thoughts or any tips.

issue.title: [BUG] @mastra/upstash: $not, $nor and $and/$or keep only the first key of a condition

labels.name: repo-0c4007c1
labels.description: Issues with Mastra's RAG system

labels.name: repo-0c4007c1
labels.description: Issue is fixed but not yet released

labels.name: repo-0c4007c1
labels.description: Issue entered the automatic triage queue

labels.name: repo-0c4007c1
labels.description: Triage severity: medium

issue.body:
### Describe the Bug

Hey Mastra team, hope you're all doing well! This is my first issue here, so any tips on how you like issues filed are very welcome. In the Upstash vector store, a `$not`, `$nor`, `$and` or `$or` condition with more than one key silently keeps only the first key. I saw how nicely #25353 (thanks @Bdysj, and @abhiaiyer91 for merging) fixed the same pattern for pg and libsql, and I think Upstash still has it.

`UpstashFilterTranslator` turns Mastra filters into Upstash filter strings for `query`, `updateVector` and `deleteVectors`. In `stores/upstash/src/vector/filter.ts`, `Object.entries(...)[0]` keeps just the first entry at lines 148 and 152 (field `$not`), 169 (operator `$not`) and 190 (each `$and`/`$or` element, which `$nor` reuses via line 117). The core type allows these filters (`$not: OperatorCondition` in `packages/core/src/vector/filter/base.ts:56`).

The result can be wrong in either direction, too wide or too narrow. Because `deleteVectors` and `updateVector` take filters (`index.ts:124,330,479`), the wrong rows can be deleted.

### Steps To Reproduce

1. In `stores/upstash/src/vector` on main, create `new UpstashFilterTranslator()` from `./filter` (it isn't exported from the package root).
2. Translate `{ price: { $not: { $gte: 10, $lte: 20 } } }`.
3. You get `price < 10`, so rows with price above 20 are missed.
4. Translate `{ $not: { a: 1, b: 2 } }` and you get `a != 1`.
5. Translate `{ $nor: [{ a: 1, b: 2 }] }` and you get `(a != 1)`.

```ts
import { UpstashFilterTranslator } from './filter';
const t = new UpstashFilterTranslator();
t.translate({ price: { $not: { $gte: 10, $lte: 20 } } }); // "price < 10"
t.translate({ $not: { a: 1, b: 2 } });                    // "a != 1"
t.translate({ $nor: [{ a: 1, b: 2 }] });                  // "(a != 1)"
t.translate({ price: { $not: { $gte: 10 } } });           // "price < 10" (correct)
t.translate({ price: { $gte: 10, $lte: 20 } });           // "(price >= 10 AND price <= 20)" (correct)
```

### Link to Minimal Reproducible Example

https://gist.github.com/abhiramshaji-cyber/9d69d9b1797946b589f161c3f713dc4a

### Expected Behavior

Every entry is used, like libsql does (`sql-builder.ts:486-504,522-530`):
- `(price < 10 OR price > 20)`
- `(a != 1 OR b != 2)`
- `(a != 1 OR b != 2)`

Would you be happy with negating each entry and joining them with OR, to match libsql? Or would you rather keep the `$not` wrapper as is? I know outside PRs are paused right now, so I'm happy to share a branch with the fix and tests for these cases (the current ones in `filter.test.ts` only cover single keys) if that would help.

### Environment Information

```shell
@mastra/upstash 1.6.0 (main @ 36bbc29)
Node v24.13.0, macOS
LLM Provider: n/a (filter translation only)
```

### Verification

- [x] I have searched the existing issues to make sure this is not a duplicate
- [x] I have included sufficient information for the team to reproduce and understand the issue

issue.title: Structured output fails when commentary and final-answer JSON messages are concatenated
issue.body:
### Describe the bug

Structured-output finalization concatenates separate assistant messages when a response contains reasoning items. This includes combining a `phase: "commentary"` message with a `phase: "final_answer"` message.

Each message can contain complete, independently valid JSON. Concatenating them produces invalid JSON and causes the SDK to reject an otherwise valid final answer.

For example, the reproduction below attempts to parse:

```text
{"answer":"checking"}{"answer":"done"}
```

### Debug information

- **Agents SDK version:** `@openai/agents-core@0.21.0`.
- **Related package versions:** `zod@4.4.3`.
- **Runtime and version:** Node.js `24.15.0`.
- **Operating system:** macOS `26.6.2`, ARM64, for the local reproduction.
- **Model and model provider:** `ScriptedModel`; no external provider is called.
- **Does the issue reproduce with the latest Agents SDK release?** Not yet tested against the latest release. Confirmed on the unmodified `0.21.0` package.
- **Does the issue occur consistently or intermittently?** Consistently with the deterministic reproduction. Both normal and streaming runs reproduce it.

Full captured stack trace below, with local filesystem prefixes shortened:

```text
ModelBehaviorError: Invalid output type: final assistant output did not match the expected schema.
    at createRedactedFinalOutputError (.../@openai/agents-core/dist/utils/finalOutputError.mjs:12:29)
    at processFinalOutputWithRedaction (.../@openai/agents-core/dist/utils/finalOutputError.mjs:26:15)
    at .../@openai/agents-core/dist/runner/turnResolution.mjs:1020:53
    at safeExecute (.../@openai/agents-core/dist/utils/safeExecute.mjs:3:29)
    at resolveTurnAfterModelResponse (.../@openai/agents-core/dist/runner/turnResolution.mjs:1020:35)
    at process.processTicksAndRejections (node:internal/process/task_queues:104:5)
    at async .../@openai/agents-core/dist/run.mjs:1098:44
    at async executeRun (.../@openai/agents-core/dist/run.mjs:345:35)
    at async .../@openai/agents-core/dist/run.mjs:366:40
    at async .../@openai/agents-core/dist/tracing/context.mjs:197:28
```

### Repro steps

Save the script below as `repro.mjs`, then run:

```sh
npm install @openai/agents-core@0.21.0 zod@4.4.3
node repro.mjs
```

No API key or network requests are needed to run the reproduction.

```typescript
import { Agent, Runner } from '@openai/agents-core';
import {
  ScriptedModel,
  assistantMessage,
} from '@openai/agents-core/testing';
import { z } from 'zod';

const model = new ScriptedModel([[
  { type: 'reasoning', content: [] },
  assistantMessage('{"answer":"checking"}', {
    id: 'msg_commentary',
    phase: 'commentary',
  }),
  assistantMessage('{"answer":"done"}', {
    id: 'msg_final',
    phase: 'final_answer',
  }),
]]);

const agent = new Agent({
  name: 'Repro',
  model,
  outputType: z.object({ answer: z.string() }),
});

const runner = new Runner({ tracingDisabled: true });
const result = await runner.run(agent, 'test', { maxTurns: 1 });

console.log(result.finalOutput);
```

Removing the reasoning item makes the same two-message response succeed, returning `{ answer: 'done' }`.

### Expected behavior

The SDK should parse and validate the final-answer message independently of preceding commentary:

```typescript
{ answer: 'done' }
```

Commentary and reasoning should remain available in history and traces without becoming part of the structured final-output document.

Combining content fragments within a single JSON message should remain supported. Separate, complete JSON documents should not be blindly concatenated before parsing.

comment.body:
Hey @bakikucukcakiroglu, hope you're doing well, and it's me again! Thank you for checking it against what you're seeing in production, that's really helpful to know, and sorry this one is biting you there.

One more detail that might help with the question for the maintainers: #1117 made `getOutputText` join every assistant segment on purpose, so a final answer that arrives split across several messages comes through whole. Going back to only the last message, the way the Python SDK reads it, would bring that split output problem back. Keeping only the `phase: 'final_answer'` messages and joining those keeps what #1117 fixed and still drops the commentary, which is why I leaned that way on the branch.

For whoever picks this up, does that direction sound right, or would you rather handle it another way? Happy to share anything from the repro or the branch that helps, and any tips are very welcome.

review.body:
Really nice work on this, the transport level probe in the description is great evidence, and reading the stream id from the stored metadata feels like the right call.

I saw you already flagged the same millisecond ordering as a known limitation. I poked at it a bit and I think it might be a one line fix, curious if you'd want to fold it in. Storing 3 events back to back on the real clock and replaying after the first, I got lost events in 1346 of 2000 runs and reordered ones in 320 more. The sort on line 56 orders by event id, so the random suffix decides ties. Since a Map already keeps insertion order, dropping the sort seems to be enough:

```ts
const sortedEvents = [...this.events.entries()];
```

With that I got 0 bad runs out of 2000 (three times over), the 4 new tests pass, and typecheck and lint are clean. I kept the spread so it stays a snapshot like today, in case something stores a new event while `send` is awaiting. The comment on line 55 would probably want a small tweak too. (I couldn't leave this as an inline suggestion since line 56 sits outside the diff.)

Also, v1.x has the same split at `src/examples/shared/inMemoryEventStore.ts:23`, maybe worth a backport if maintainers want one? And #1978 and #1984 touch the same spot (they also iterate the Map directly), just mentioning them so maintainers can line things up.

Thanks for this, the writeup with the `match(expand(...))` round trip made the bug really easy to follow, and the three tests read nicely. I tried a few more subsets and found one that still returns null (inline). Also `changeset-bot` says there's no changeset yet, not sure if you meant to add one. Happy to hear if I'm missing something here!

issue.title: feat(review): review each commit of a PR separately
issue.body:
With per commit review turned on by the host, `/review` reviews each commit of a PR on its own diff and commit message, instead of only the combined diff.

Closes #4470. It is opt in and host only. The commit messages piece was split out into #4603, as suggested, and that has now landed on `main`.

**What this code is for**

`PRReviewer.run()` in `pr_agent/commands/pr_reviewer.py` handles `/review`. It asks the git provider for the PR diff, renders `pr_reviewer_prompts.toml` with that diff, makes one model call (or a few when chunking), and publishes one review comment.

**Before this PR**

A maintainer on GitLab has an MR with 4 commits, each with a message that explains one change, and comments `/review`.

1. `PRReviewer.run()` asks `GitLabProvider.get_diff_files()` for the diff of the whole MR.
2. The prompt gets that combined diff, plus the title and description.
3. The model returns findings with file and line, but nothing says which commit a finding belongs to.
4. One review comment for the whole MR. The maintainer has to work out by hand which of the 4 commits needs the fixup.

**After this PR**

Same maintainer, same MR, with `per_commit_review = true` in the host config or `.pr_agent.toml`.

1. `PRReviewer.run()` sees `per_commit_review` and calls `_run_per_commit()`.
2. `get_pr_commits()` returns the 4 commits, oldest first, with their parents, read fresh from the provider on every run. Merge commits are dropped here without loading them. `_commit_review_records()` reads the commits already reviewed from hidden markers in PR-Agent's own comments. For each commit not already listed by SHA, `set_commit_review_scope()` loads its files once and returns a fingerprint of its own patch, and only commits whose fingerprint is not recorded are kept. On the first run there are no markers, so all 4 are kept.
3. For each commit, `set_commit_review_scope()` scopes the diff to that commit against its parent, and `commit_under_review` puts its message (clipped to `max_commits_tokens`) in the prompt, between random markers made fresh for each run. `commit_messages_str` is cleared, so the prompt does not also list every other commit's message.
4. `_run_review()` runs once per commit and publishes one comment that names and links the commit. It uses the incremental review header, so it never replaces the persistent full review.
5. A commit with no findings gets no comment when `pr_reviewer.publish_output_no_suggestions = false`. With `inline_key_issues = true`, findings land inline on that commit's own diff.
6. 4 comments, one per commit, each with a `<!-- pr-agent:reviewed-commit <fingerprint> <sha> -->` line two lines below the hidden `<!-- pr-agent:review:incremental -->` identity. On the next push with 1 new commit, only that commit is reviewed. Without the setting, `/review` takes exactly the old path.

**The diagram**

```mermaid
flowchart LR

classDef box fill:#eef1ff,stroke:#4c5bd4,color:#111827
classDef bad fill:#ffd6d6,stroke:#cc0000,color:#111827,stroke-width:3px
classDef good fill:#c8f0c8,stroke:#008800,color:#111827,stroke-width:3px

subgraph BEFORE["BEFORE: 1 review for 4 commits"]
direction TB
  B1["Maintainer comments /review"] --> B2["PRReviewer.run"]
  B2 --> B3["get_diff_files for the whole MR"]
  B3 --> B4{"one prompt, combined diff"}
  B4 -->|"findings not tied to a commit"| B5["1 comment for the whole MR"]
  B4 -->|"per_commit_review off"| B6["same as today"]
end

subgraph AFTER["AFTER: 1 review per commit"]
direction TB
  A1["Maintainer comments /review"] --> A2["PRReviewer.run"]
  A2 --> A3["get_pr_commits"]
  A3 --> A4{"THE CHANGE: per_commit_review on"}
  A4 -->|"each commit: own diff and message"| A5["1 comment per commit, linked"]
  A4 -->|"setting off or provider unsupported"| A6["whole PR review, as today"]
end

B1 ~~~ A1

class B1,B2,B3,B6 box
class A1,A2,A3,A6 box
class B4,B5 bad
class A4,A5 good

linkStyle 3 stroke:#cc0000,stroke-width:5px
linkStyle 8 stroke:#008800,stroke-width:5px

style BEFORE fill:#fff5f5,stroke:#cc0000,color:#111827
style AFTER fill:#f3fff3,stroke:#008800,color:#111827
```

**The change**

* `PRReviewer.run()` now branches on `per_commit_review` into `_run_per_commit()`, and the old body moved into `_run_review()` unchanged apart from the commit header and the checks below.
* `GitProvider` gets `get_pr_commits()` (returns `None` by default, so other providers fall back to a whole PR review with a notice) and `set_commit_review_scope()`. GitHub and GitLab implement both on top of the existing incremental diff path. On GitHub, new side file contents are read at the commit when a head SHA is set.
* `_run_per_commit()` reviews only commits whose fingerprint is not recorded, so a plain `/review` and the default `push_commands` no longer review every commit again on each push (454174f1, 40cb6ee2, b52fbf25, bf4dd1b6, 9b159195). `commit_patch_fingerprint()` in `git_provider.py` hashes each file's name and patch with the `@@ -a,b +c,d @@` numbers removed, so a rebase onto `main` that leaves a commit's own patch alone does not review it again, while an amend or `--autosquash` fixup does. On GitLab, when a file's diff comes back empty (collapsed, too large or binary), the commit SHA is mixed into the fingerprint so two different commits never share one; such a commit is reviewed again after a rebase. A commit is recorded only after its review succeeds, including when every file was filtered out: `_run_review()` puts the marker line two lines below the comment's hidden incremental review identity, and a commit that gets no comment (no findings with `publish_output_no_suggestions = false`) goes into one record comment that starts with `<!-- pr-agent:review:commits -->` and is edited in place through `publish_persistent_comment_full()`. With default settings and no merge commits, no record comment is created. Before writing, the record is read again and merged, trimmed to commits still in the PR, and cut from the oldest end if it would pass the 65000 character comment limit. Markers count only at those fixed lines and only in comments `is_comment_authored_by_pr_agent()` confirms. A marker in a comment confirmed as someone else's is ignored. Markers are found by that hidden identity rather than the visible heading, so changing `review_heading` never reviews commits again. When comment authorship cannot be checked for the run, or marker comments exist but none can be confirmed and the author of at least one cannot be verified (for example a GitHub App whose login cannot be resolved), the run falls back to one whole PR review with a notice instead of reviewing every commit on each push. Each commit's files are loaded once per run and reused for its review; a commit whose patch is already recorded under another SHA (a rebase) is recorded under the new SHA too, and a commit with no changes of its own is recorded, so neither is loaded again. A failed commit is not recorded, so the next run retries it; the record counts failed attempts, and automatic runs stop after `PER_COMMIT_MAX_AUTO_ATTEMPTS` (3) while a manual `/review` always retries. Selection does not use commit dates, so a commit authored before the last review but pushed after it is still reviewed. If the comments cannot be read, the run fails with the usual failure comment instead of reviewing every commit. The `-i` lookup and its `minimal_*_for_incremental_review` thresholds are not used here, so a manual `/review` never stops silently. `docs/docs/commands/review.md` says so, and also says that if PR-Agent's comments are removed, the next run reviews every commit again unless `max_commits_per_review` is set (93cb7440).
* The commit message block opens and closes with `{{ commit_message_begin }}` and `{{ commit_message_end }}` from `prompt_boundary_markers("COMMIT_MESSAGE")` (the helper #4603 added to `pr_agent/algo/artifacts.py`), so a commit message containing `<<<COMMIT_MESSAGE_END>>>` cannot close the block early. It sits right above #4603's `commit_messages_str` block, which keeps its own `COMMIT_MESSAGES` markers.
* `_should_publish_review_no_suggestions()` checks the parsed findings for a commit review, so a commit where the model returned nothing or prose stays quiet with `publish_output_no_suggestions = false`.
* `per_commit_review` and `max_commits_per_review` are in the `pr_reviewer` entry of `CLI_HOST_ONLY_KEYS_BY_SECTION` and `PER_DIRECTORY_HOST_ONLY_KEYS_BY_SECTION`, so `/review --pr_reviewer.per_commit_review=true` in a comment is rejected.
* `max_commits_per_review` defaults to 0 (no limit). When more commits than the cap are not reviewed yet, the whole PR is reviewed once with a notice, and after that review succeeds all its commits are recorded, so the next push goes back to one review per new commit. GitHub lists at most 250 commits per PR, so a PR with more is reviewed as a whole with a notice.
* Merge commits, root commits and empty commits are skipped. One failing commit does not stop the rest; the run is marked failed afterwards.
* Upstream `main` is merged in with merge commits (181edc4c, 9723af3a), not a rebase, so no history is rewritten. Conflicts: `convert_to_markdown_v2()` keeps main's `get_bot_display_name()` next to the commit header, `CLI_HOST_ONLY_KEYS_BY_SECTION` keeps main's new `pr_reviewer` keys plus ours, and the key count in `test_config_reference.py` is main's 319 plus our 2. After #4798, `run()` no longer checks `is_answer`, and the tests set `config.is_auto_command`. After #4838 renamed `pr_agent/tools` to `pr_agent/commands`, the tests import from `pr_agent.commands` and the config links point at `../commands/review.md` (ed7715a5). `_prepare_code_suggestions()` on GitHub skips `validate_comments_inside_hunks()` while a commit scope is set, so a finding outside that commit's diff stays in the commit's summary instead of moving to a nearby line. `pytest tests/unittest` on 912963d8: 17692 passed, 34 skipped. `ruff check`: clean.

**What changes for a user**

* Nothing unless the host turns on `per_commit_review`. Default `/review` is unchanged.
* With it on: one model call per reviewed commit. The first run reviews every commit, and later runs review only new commits or commits whose own changes changed, so `-i` is no longer needed in `push_commands`.
* Each commit's review sees only that commit's diff, so it can flag something a later commit fixes, or miss a helper added in an earlier commit.
* Only GitHub and GitLab support it. Other providers get the usual whole PR review with a one line notice.

comment.body:
Hey @IsmaelMartinez, hope you're doing well, and thank you for such a careful review. The inline suggestions made each fix really easy.

I've merged main into the branch (181edc4c). I used a merge commit rather than a rebase so the history isn't rewritten, and I'm happy for it to be squashed when it lands. Your `is_answer` and `is_auto_command` suggestions are applied. For the hunk relocation, I skip it while a single commit is being reviewed, so a finding outside that commit's diff stays in that commit's summary instead of landing on a nearby line of a different change.

While testing the `-i` style selection we found it had some gaps. Clean commits under `publish_output_no_suggestions = false` were reviewed again on every push. A commit that failed while a later one published, or one pushed after the last review, could be skipped. And every rebase reviewed everything again. So per commit review now keeps a record of a fingerprint of each commit's own changes, and only reviews commits whose changes it hasn't seen (latest in 9b159195). A rebase that leaves a commit's patch alone costs nothing. I also need to correct what I said on 11-09: the `-i` thresholds no longer apply here, sorry for the mix up.

The record is a hidden line under each commit's review heading. A separate record comment only appears for commits that get no comment of their own, such as clean commits under the quiet setting or commits with no changes. A failed commit is retried, and automatic runs stop after 3 failures. If the bot can't confirm it wrote the earlier markers (for example a GitHub App without a resolvable login), it falls back to one whole PR review with a notice rather than reviewing every commit on each push.

On `max_commits_per_review`, I'd keep the default at 0. Hi-Angel preferred no cap, and with fingerprints a push or rebase only pays for commits whose changes are new, so the remaining cost is the first run, which hosts can cap themselves. Happy to change it if you see it differently.

Would love your feedback on any of this, and any tips you have.

issue.title: Background shell streams in Agent Host chats keep all output in lastSnapshot and can lose a detached shell's exit code

labels.name: repo-cfcbddd9
labels.description: Issue identified by VS Code Team member as probable bug

labels.name: repo-cfcbddd9
labels.description: The run in terminal tool in chat

issue.body:
Follow-up to https://github.com/microsoft/vscode/pull/341700, which streams a detached background shell's output from the Copilot SDK's `session.rpc.tasks.readOutput` into its tool call's terminal. Review of that PR found three things, none of which block it. The reload and restart gaps are already tracked in https://github.com/microsoft/vscode/issues/341645.

**`lastSnapshot` grows without bound for background shells**

- `NonPtyShellTerminalStreams.appendChunk` appends every chunk to `stream.lastSnapshot` ([code](https://github.com/microsoft/vscode/blob/4cf035a20f2fd5e1c99c5635c32a834b761add25/src/vs/platform/agentHost/node/copilot/copilotNonPtyShellTerminals.ts#L360)) and nothing trims it. The terminal content itself is kept to a rolling buffer by `AgentHostTerminalManager._trimContent` ([code](https://github.com/microsoft/vscode/blob/4cf035a20f2fd5e1c99c5635c32a834b761add25/src/vs/platform/agentHost/node/agentHostTerminalManager.ts#L832-L834)), 100 KB per [`AGENT_HOST_TERMINAL_MAX_CONTENT_LENGTH`](https://github.com/microsoft/vscode/blob/4cf035a20f2fd5e1c99c5635c32a834b761add25/src/vs/platform/agentHost/common/terminalConstants.ts#L10).
- Once a stream has switched to chunks, `lastSnapshot` has two readers: `append` returns early for a chunked stream ([code](https://github.com/microsoft/vscode/blob/4cf035a20f2fd5e1c99c5635c32a834b761add25/src/vs/platform/agentHost/node/copilot/copilotNonPtyShellTerminals.ts#L278)), and `completeToolCall` compares it once when the tool call completes ([code](https://github.com/microsoft/vscode/blob/4cf035a20f2fd5e1c99c5635c32a834b761add25/src/vs/platform/agentHost/node/copilot/copilotNonPtyShellTerminals.ts#L406)). For a shell that keeps running after its call completed, nothing reads it again.
- Attached background shells have done this since https://github.com/microsoft/vscode/pull/339220, because the Copilot SDK streams their `tool.shell_output` chunks until exit. Detached shells are the long-lived ones (dev servers, watchers), and https://github.com/microsoft/vscode/pull/341700 feeds their reads through the same path in `appendDetachedShellOutput` ([code](https://github.com/microsoft/vscode/blob/4cf035a20f2fd5e1c99c5635c32a834b761add25/src/vs/platform/agentHost/node/copilot/copilotNonPtyShellTerminals.ts#L453-L459)), so a detached watcher that runs for hours keeps all of its output in the Agent Host process, untrimmed, until the chat is disposed.

**The exit code reported before the log drained is lost if the read then fails**

- When the task list, a `shell_completed` notification, or a `read_bash`/`stop_bash` result reports the exit while the log is still being read, `_completeBackgroundShell` remembers the shell as draining and returns without keeping the reported `exitCode` ([code](https://github.com/microsoft/vscode/blob/4cf035a20f2fd5e1c99c5635c32a834b761add25/src/vs/platform/agentHost/node/copilot/copilotNonPtyShellTerminals.ts#L591-L596)).
- Normally the read's `exit.exitCode` settles the terminal. If the read fails instead, `stopReadingDetachedShell` finalizes with `undefined` ([code](https://github.com/microsoft/vscode/blob/4cf035a20f2fd5e1c99c5635c32a834b761add25/src/vs/platform/agentHost/node/copilot/copilotNonPtyShellTerminals.ts#L486-L491)), so the terminal shows the shell as exited without a code even though one was reported.

**A failed read gives up instead of reading again without a cursor**

- `_readDetachedShellOutput` stops on any error, logs a warning, and leaves the shell to the task list ([code](https://github.com/microsoft/vscode/blob/4cf035a20f2fd5e1c99c5635c32a834b761add25/src/vs/platform/agentHost/node/copilot/copilotAgentSession.ts#L2684-L2689)).
- The `TasksReadOutputRequest.cursor` docs in `@github/copilot-sdk` 1.0.23-preview.2 say a read fails when the output no longer reaches the cursor, for example because its log was removed, and to read again without a cursor. The terminal then stays at whatever had been read before the failure.

Steps to see the first one, in a local Agent Host Copilot session with `chat.agentHost.customTerminalTool.enabled` at its default, `false`:

1. Ask Copilot: "Use your shell tool to run `for i in $(seq 1 3000000); do echo \"line $i\"; done` in async mode with detach set to true. Do not read its output or wait for it. Reply with exactly STARTED."
2. Attach a debugger to the Agent Host, or take heap snapshots before and after. The shell's **Background Shells** terminal holds under 100 KB, while the stream's `lastSnapshot` holds the whole output, tens of MB.

The other two are from reading the code; the `readOutput` mock in `copilotAgentSession.test.ts` can force them.

Possible fix:

- [ ] Stop appending to `lastSnapshot` in `appendChunk` once the stream's `backgroundShellId` is set, with a test that streams past the terminal buffer limit and checks `lastSnapshot` stays bounded.
- [ ] Keep the reported exit code with the draining entry and use it in `stopReadingDetachedShell`, with a test: report `completed with exit code 2`, fail the read, expect `exitCode: 2`.
- [ ] On a read failure, read once more without a cursor before giving up. Reading without a cursor replays the log from the start, so reset the terminal before appending the replay.

comment.body: Hope you're doing well, @anthonykim1! Thanks so much for the clear checklist here, it made the first two items really easy to pick up. I opened #347246 for those (bounded `lastSnapshot` once a shell goes to the background, and the reported exit code kept with the draining entry), each with a test. I left the third item alone since it felt like its own change. If you already have any of this in progress, I'm very happy to close mine. Would love any feedback or tips you have!

issue.title: Structured output fails when commentary and final-answer JSON messages are concatenated
issue.body:
### Describe the bug

Structured-output finalization concatenates separate assistant messages when a response contains reasoning items. This includes combining a `phase: "commentary"` message with a `phase: "final_answer"` message.

Each message can contain complete, independently valid JSON. Concatenating them produces invalid JSON and causes the SDK to reject an otherwise valid final answer.

For example, the reproduction below attempts to parse:

```text
{"answer":"checking"}{"answer":"done"}
```

### Debug information

- **Agents SDK version:** `@openai/agents-core@0.21.0`.
- **Related package versions:** `zod@4.4.3`.
- **Runtime and version:** Node.js `24.15.0`.
- **Operating system:** macOS `26.6.2`, ARM64, for the local reproduction.
- **Model and model provider:** `ScriptedModel`; no external provider is called.
- **Does the issue reproduce with the latest Agents SDK release?** Not yet tested against the latest release. Confirmed on the unmodified `0.21.0` package.
- **Does the issue occur consistently or intermittently?** Consistently with the deterministic reproduction. Both normal and streaming runs reproduce it.

Full captured stack trace below, with local filesystem prefixes shortened:

```text
ModelBehaviorError: Invalid output type: final assistant output did not match the expected schema.
    at createRedactedFinalOutputError (.../@openai/agents-core/dist/utils/finalOutputError.mjs:12:29)
    at processFinalOutputWithRedaction (.../@openai/agents-core/dist/utils/finalOutputError.mjs:26:15)
    at .../@openai/agents-core/dist/runner/turnResolution.mjs:1020:53
    at safeExecute (.../@openai/agents-core/dist/utils/safeExecute.mjs:3:29)
    at resolveTurnAfterModelResponse (.../@openai/agents-core/dist/runner/turnResolution.mjs:1020:35)
    at process.processTicksAndRejections (node:internal/process/task_queues:104:5)
    at async .../@openai/agents-core/dist/run.mjs:1098:44
    at async executeRun (.../@openai/agents-core/dist/run.mjs:345:35)
    at async .../@openai/agents-core/dist/run.mjs:366:40
    at async .../@openai/agents-core/dist/tracing/context.mjs:197:28
```

### Repro steps

Save the script below as `repro.mjs`, then run:

```sh
npm install @openai/agents-core@0.21.0 zod@4.4.3
node repro.mjs
```

No API key or network requests are needed to run the reproduction.

```typescript
import { Agent, Runner } from '@openai/agents-core';
import {
  ScriptedModel,
  assistantMessage,
} from '@openai/agents-core/testing';
import { z } from 'zod';

const model = new ScriptedModel([[
  { type: 'reasoning', content: [] },
  assistantMessage('{"answer":"checking"}', {
    id: 'msg_commentary',
    phase: 'commentary',
  }),
  assistantMessage('{"answer":"done"}', {
    id: 'msg_final',
    phase: 'final_answer',
  }),
]]);

const agent = new Agent({
  name: 'Repro',
  model,
  outputType: z.object({ answer: z.string() }),
});

const runner = new Runner({ tracingDisabled: true });
const result = await runner.run(agent, 'test', { maxTurns: 1 });

console.log(result.finalOutput);
```

Removing the reasoning item makes the same two-message response succeed, returning `{ answer: 'done' }`.

### Expected behavior

The SDK should parse and validate the final-answer message independently of preceding commentary:

```typescript
{ answer: 'done' }
```

Commentary and reasoning should remain available in history and traces without becoming part of the structured final-output document.

Combining content fragments within a single JSON message should remain supported. Separate, complete JSON documents should not be blindly concatenated before parsing.

comment.body:
Hey @bakikucukcakiroglu, hope you're doing well! Thanks so much for the repro, having it run with `ScriptedModel` and no API key made this really easy to dig into. I also really liked your note that dropping the reasoning item makes it pass. That pointed straight at the cause.

From what I can tell, it comes from `getOutputText` in [`packages/agents-core/src/utils/messages.ts`](https://github.com/openai/openai-agents-js/blob/7589b9c40120b89a7d2d28a5a60b4defe1ed7bf5/packages/agents-core/src/utils/messages.ts#L98-L126). When the response has a reasoning item and only messages otherwise, it joins the text of every assistant message and never looks at `phase`. So the commentary JSON and the `final_answer` JSON end up as one string. Without reasoning it only takes the last message, which is why your second case works.

The final output goes through it in [`turnResolution.ts`](https://github.com/openai/openai-agents-js/blob/7589b9c40120b89a7d2d28a5a60b4defe1ed7bf5/packages/agents-core/src/runner/turnResolution.ts#L1638-L1642), and `asTool()` uses it too in [`agent.ts`](https://github.com/openai/openai-agents-js/blob/7589b9c40120b89a7d2d28a5a60b4defe1ed7bf5/packages/agents-core/src/agent.ts#L1065-L1069). So a text agent used as a tool hands the commentary back to the parent along with the answer.

The Python SDK doesn't seem to have this, since it reads only the last message ([`turn_resolution.py`](https://github.com/openai/openai-agents-python/blob/1fc77bbc8ac1446690f6ba62dd0d52779bdcf43f/src/agents/run_internal/turn_resolution.py#L1203-L1204)).

I tried a small fix on a branch: if any message has `phase: 'final_answer'`, join only those messages, and otherwise keep the current behavior. Messages with no phase work exactly as before, several `final_answer` messages split by reasoning still get joined, and commentary is left out wherever it shows up. Your repro is a test there, for `run`, streaming and `asTool()`: [compare view](https://github.com/openai/openai-agents-js/compare/main...abhiramshaji-cyber:openai-agents-js:fix/output-text-final-answer-phase)

One question for the maintainers: would you rather pick by phase like this, or just use the last message like Python does? Happy to change it either way, and to open a PR if that's useful. @bakikucukcakiroglu, does this match what you're seeing in production?

issue.title: Keep outgoing webhook token on update

labels.name: repo-8e1e942e
labels.description: Denotes a PR that will be considered when it comes time to generate release notes.

issue.body:
Fixes #39400

Editing an outgoing webhook the way the API docs show used to erase its secret token, so the receiving service could no longer verify it; the token now stays.

**What this code is for**

`PUT /api/v4/hooks/outgoing/{hook_id}` lets an admin change an outgoing webhook's name, description, channel, trigger words or callback URLs. The handler `updateOutgoingHook` loads the stored hook and passes both to `UpdateOutgoingWebhook`, which copies the fields the server owns from the stored hook and saves the result with `UpdateOutgoing`. Every time the hook fires, Mattermost sends the saved `Token` to the callback URL so the receiver can check the request came from this hook.

**Before this PR**

An admin renames an outgoing webhook by sending the request body shown in the API docs, which has no `token` field.

1. `updateOutgoingHook` decodes the body into `updatedHook`; `Token` is `""`.
2. `UpdateOutgoingWebhook` copies `CreatorId`, `CreateAt`, `DeleteAt` and `TeamId` from `oldHook`, but not `Token`.
3. `UpdateOutgoing` writes `Token = ''` to the `OutgoingWebhooks` row.
4. The next post with a trigger word sends a payload with an empty `token` to the callback URL.
5. The receiving service rejects it because the token no longer matches the one it was given.

**After this PR**

Same admin, same request.

1. Same as above through step 2.
2. `UpdateOutgoingWebhook` also sets `updatedHook.Token = oldHook.Token`.
3. `UpdateOutgoing` writes the original token back, along with the new name.
4. The next trigger word post sends the same token as before, and the receiver accepts it.
5. A token sent in the body is ignored the same way, so the only way to change it is still `POST /api/v4/hooks/outgoing/{hook_id}/regen_token`.

**The diagram**

```mermaid
flowchart LR

classDef box fill:#eef1ff,stroke:#4c5bd4,color:#111827
classDef bad fill:#ffd6d6,stroke:#cc0000,color:#111827,stroke-width:3px
classDef good fill:#c8f0c8,stroke:#008800,color:#111827,stroke-width:3px

subgraph BEFORE["BEFORE: saved token becomes empty"]
direction TB
  B1["admin sends PUT without token"] --> B2["updateOutgoingHook"]
  B2 --> B3["UpdateOutgoingWebhook"]
  B3 -->|"Token taken from request body"| B4["UpdateOutgoing saves empty Token"]
  B4 --> B5["receiver gets empty token"]
end

subgraph AFTER["AFTER: saved token unchanged"]
direction TB
  A1["admin sends PUT without token"] --> A2["updateOutgoingHook"]
  A2 --> A3["UpdateOutgoingWebhook"]
  A3 --> A4{"THE CHANGE: Token = oldHook.Token"}
  A4 -->|"token"| A5["receiver gets the original token"]
  A4 -->|"other fields"| A6["name, triggers, callback URLs still updated"]
end

B1 ~~~ A1

class B1,B2,B3 box
class A1,A2,A3,A6 box
class B4,B5 bad
class A4,A5 good

linkStyle 2 stroke:#cc0000,stroke-width:5px
linkStyle 6 stroke:#008800,stroke-width:5px

style BEFORE fill:#fff5f5,stroke:#cc0000,color:#111827
style AFTER fill:#f3fff3,stroke:#008800,color:#111827
```

**The change**

One line in `UpdateOutgoingWebhook` in `server/channels/app/webhook.go`: `updatedHook.Token = oldHook.Token`, next to the existing copies of `CreatorId`, `CreateAt`, `DeleteAt` and `TeamId`. That is the whole fix.

`TestUpdateOutgoingHook` gets a `RetainToken` case that updates a hook once with an empty `Token` and once with a different `Token`, and checks both the response and a fresh `GetOutgoingWebhook` still return the original token.

**What changes for a user**

- Updating an outgoing webhook through the API, with or without a `token` field, keeps its existing token.
- Integrations that verify the token keep working after the webhook is edited.
- Regenerating the token with `regen_token` works as before.
- Clients that sent the token back unchanged, like the Integrations page in the web app, see no difference.

#### Summary

Covered above.

#### Ticket Link

Fixes https://github.com/mattermost/mattermost/issues/39400

#### Release Note

```release-note
Fixed an issue where updating an outgoing webhook through the API without a token field cleared the webhook's token.
```

issue.title: feat(review): review each commit of a PR separately
issue.body:
With per commit review turned on by the host, `/review` reviews each commit of a PR on its own diff and commit message, instead of only the combined diff.

Closes #4470. It is opt in and host only. The commit messages piece was split out into #4603, as suggested, and that has now landed on `main`.

**What this code is for**

`PRReviewer.run()` in `pr_agent/commands/pr_reviewer.py` handles `/review`. It asks the git provider for the PR diff, renders `pr_reviewer_prompts.toml` with that diff, makes one model call (or a few when chunking), and publishes one review comment.

**Before this PR**

A maintainer on GitLab has an MR with 4 commits, each with a message that explains one change, and comments `/review`.

1. `PRReviewer.run()` asks `GitLabProvider.get_diff_files()` for the diff of the whole MR.
2. The prompt gets that combined diff, plus the title and description.
3. The model returns findings with file and line, but nothing says which commit a finding belongs to.
4. One review comment for the whole MR. The maintainer has to work out by hand which of the 4 commits needs the fixup.

**After this PR**

Same maintainer, same MR, with `per_commit_review = true` in the host config or `.pr_agent.toml`.

1. `PRReviewer.run()` sees `per_commit_review` and calls `_run_per_commit()`.
2. `get_pr_commits()` returns the 4 commits, oldest first, with their parents, read fresh from the provider on every run. Merge commits are dropped here without loading them. `_commit_review_records()` reads the commits already reviewed from hidden markers in PR-Agent's own comments. For each commit not already listed by SHA, `set_commit_review_scope()` loads its files once and returns a fingerprint of its own patch, and only commits whose fingerprint is not recorded are kept. On the first run there are no markers, so all 4 are kept.
3. For each commit, `set_commit_review_scope()` scopes the diff to that commit against its parent, and `commit_under_review` puts its message (clipped to `max_commits_tokens`) in the prompt, between random markers made fresh for each run. `commit_messages_str` is cleared, so the prompt does not also list every other commit's message.
4. `_run_review()` runs once per commit and publishes one comment that names and links the commit. It uses the incremental review header, so it never replaces the persistent full review.
5. A commit with no findings gets no comment when `pr_reviewer.publish_output_no_suggestions = false`. With `inline_key_issues = true`, findings land inline on that commit's own diff.
6. 4 comments, one per commit, each with a `<!-- pr-agent:reviewed-commit <fingerprint> <sha> -->` line two lines below the hidden `<!-- pr-agent:review:incremental -->` identity. On the next push with 1 new commit, only that commit is reviewed. Without the setting, `/review` takes exactly the old path.

**The diagram**

```mermaid
flowchart LR

classDef box fill:#eef1ff,stroke:#4c5bd4,color:#111827
classDef bad fill:#ffd6d6,stroke:#cc0000,color:#111827,stroke-width:3px
classDef good fill:#c8f0c8,stroke:#008800,color:#111827,stroke-width:3px

subgraph BEFORE["BEFORE: 1 review for 4 commits"]
direction TB
  B1["Maintainer comments /review"] --> B2["PRReviewer.run"]
  B2 --> B3["get_diff_files for the whole MR"]
  B3 --> B4{"one prompt, combined diff"}
  B4 -->|"findings not tied to a commit"| B5["1 comment for the whole MR"]
  B4 -->|"per_commit_review off"| B6["same as today"]
end

subgraph AFTER["AFTER: 1 review per commit"]
direction TB
  A1["Maintainer comments /review"] --> A2["PRReviewer.run"]
  A2 --> A3["get_pr_commits"]
  A3 --> A4{"THE CHANGE: per_commit_review on"}
  A4 -->|"each commit: own diff and message"| A5["1 comment per commit, linked"]
  A4 -->|"setting off or provider unsupported"| A6["whole PR review, as today"]
end

B1 ~~~ A1

class B1,B2,B3,B6 box
class A1,A2,A3,A6 box
class B4,B5 bad
class A4,A5 good

linkStyle 3 stroke:#cc0000,stroke-width:5px
linkStyle 8 stroke:#008800,stroke-width:5px

style BEFORE fill:#fff5f5,stroke:#cc0000,color:#111827
style AFTER fill:#f3fff3,stroke:#008800,color:#111827
```

**The change**

* `PRReviewer.run()` now branches on `per_commit_review` into `_run_per_commit()`, and the old body moved into `_run_review()` unchanged apart from the commit header and the checks below.
* `GitProvider` gets `get_pr_commits()` (returns `None` by default, so other providers fall back to a whole PR review with a notice) and `set_commit_review_scope()`. GitHub and GitLab implement both on top of the existing incremental diff path. On GitHub, new side file contents are read at the commit when a head SHA is set.
* `_run_per_commit()` reviews only commits whose fingerprint is not recorded, so a plain `/review` and the default `push_commands` no longer review every commit again on each push (454174f1, 40cb6ee2, b52fbf25, bf4dd1b6, 9b159195). `commit_patch_fingerprint()` in `git_provider.py` hashes each file's name and patch with the `@@ -a,b +c,d @@` numbers removed, so a rebase onto `main` that leaves a commit's own patch alone does not review it again, while an amend or `--autosquash` fixup does. On GitLab, when a file's diff comes back empty (collapsed, too large or binary), the commit SHA is mixed into the fingerprint so two different commits never share one; such a commit is reviewed again after a rebase. A commit is recorded only after its review succeeds, including when every file was filtered out: `_run_review()` puts the marker line two lines below the comment's hidden incremental review identity, and a commit that gets no comment (no findings with `publish_output_no_suggestions = false`) goes into one record comment that starts with `<!-- pr-agent:review:commits -->` and is edited in place through `publish_persistent_comment_full()`. With default settings and no merge commits, no record comment is created. Before writing, the record is read again and merged, trimmed to commits still in the PR, and cut from the oldest end if it would pass the 65000 character comment limit. Markers count only at those fixed lines and only in comments `is_comment_authored_by_pr_agent()` confirms. A marker in a comment confirmed as someone else's is ignored. Markers are found by that hidden identity rather than the visible heading, so changing `review_heading` never reviews commits again. When comment authorship cannot be checked for the run, or marker comments exist but none can be confirmed and the author of at least one cannot be verified (for example a GitHub App whose login cannot be resolved), the run falls back to one whole PR review with a notice instead of reviewing every commit on each push. Each commit's files are loaded once per run and reused for its review; a commit whose patch is already recorded under another SHA (a rebase) is recorded under the new SHA too, and a commit with no changes of its own is recorded, so neither is loaded again. A failed commit is not recorded, so the next run retries it; the record counts failed attempts, and automatic runs stop after `PER_COMMIT_MAX_AUTO_ATTEMPTS` (3) while a manual `/review` always retries. Selection does not use commit dates, so a commit authored before the last review but pushed after it is still reviewed. If the comments cannot be read, the run fails with the usual failure comment instead of reviewing every commit. The `-i` lookup and its `minimal_*_for_incremental_review` thresholds are not used here, so a manual `/review` never stops silently. `docs/docs/commands/review.md` says so, and also says that if PR-Agent's comments are removed, the next run reviews every commit again unless `max_commits_per_review` is set (93cb7440).
* The commit message block opens and closes with `{{ commit_message_begin }}` and `{{ commit_message_end }}` from `prompt_boundary_markers("COMMIT_MESSAGE")` (the helper #4603 added to `pr_agent/algo/artifacts.py`), so a commit message containing `<<<COMMIT_MESSAGE_END>>>` cannot close the block early. It sits right above #4603's `commit_messages_str` block, which keeps its own `COMMIT_MESSAGES` markers.
* `_should_publish_review_no_suggestions()` checks the parsed findings for a commit review, so a commit where the model returned nothing or prose stays quiet with `publish_output_no_suggestions = false`.
* `per_commit_review` and `max_commits_per_review` are in the `pr_reviewer` entry of `CLI_HOST_ONLY_KEYS_BY_SECTION` and `PER_DIRECTORY_HOST_ONLY_KEYS_BY_SECTION`, so `/review --pr_reviewer.per_commit_review=true` in a comment is rejected.
* `max_commits_per_review` defaults to 0 (no limit). When more commits than the cap are not reviewed yet, the whole PR is reviewed once with a notice, and after that review succeeds all its commits are recorded, so the next push goes back to one review per new commit. GitHub lists at most 250 commits per PR, so a PR with more is reviewed as a whole with a notice.
* Merge commits, root commits and empty commits are skipped. One failing commit does not stop the rest; the run is marked failed afterwards.
* Upstream `main` is merged in with merge commits (181edc4c, 9723af3a), not a rebase, so no history is rewritten. Conflicts: `convert_to_markdown_v2()` keeps main's `get_bot_display_name()` next to the commit header, `CLI_HOST_ONLY_KEYS_BY_SECTION` keeps main's new `pr_reviewer` keys plus ours, and the key count in `test_config_reference.py` is main's 319 plus our 2. After #4798, `run()` no longer checks `is_answer`, and the tests set `config.is_auto_command`. After #4838 renamed `pr_agent/tools` to `pr_agent/commands`, the tests import from `pr_agent.commands` and the config links point at `../commands/review.md` (ed7715a5). `_prepare_code_suggestions()` on GitHub skips `validate_comments_inside_hunks()` while a commit scope is set, so a finding outside that commit's diff stays in the commit's summary instead of moving to a nearby line. `pytest tests/unittest` on 912963d8: 17692 passed, 34 skipped. `ruff check`: clean.

**What changes for a user**

* Nothing unless the host turns on `per_commit_review`. Default `/review` is unchanged.
* With it on: one model call per reviewed commit. The first run reviews every commit, and later runs review only new commits or commits whose own changes changed, so `-i` is no longer needed in `push_commands`.
* Each commit's review sees only that commit's diff, so it can flag something a later commit fixes, or miss a helper added in an earlier commit.
* Only GitHub and GitLab support it. Other providers get the usual whole PR review with a one line notice.

comment.body:
Hey @IsmaelMartinez, hope you're doing well! No apology needed at all, and thank you for taking another look and for laying out the cost so clearly. You're right, on this branch a plain `/review` and the default `push_commands` walk every commit again, so a 20 commit PR would make 20 calls on every push.

In 6f96f7b, `per_commit_review` now always reviews only the commits since the last review, picked the same way `-i` picks them, and falls back to every commit on the first run when there's no earlier review. So hosts no longer need `-i` in `push_commands`. I kept the `minimal_commits_for_incremental_review` and `minimal_minutes_for_incremental_review` thresholds working as they do for `-i`. Would you rather per commit review skip them?

I've also left `main` unmerged as you asked earlier. Would you like me to merge it now, or keep it parked until after v1? Happy to adjust either way.

issue.title: RestApiTool sends null header and cookie params as "null" and objects as [object Object]

labels.name: repo-03a26658
labels.description: Something isn't working

labels.name: repo-03a26658
labels.description: [Status] The PR/issue is awaiting review from the maintainer

issue.body:
**Describe the bug**
`prepareRequestParams` in `RestApiTool` turns `null` header and cookie args into the literal string `"null"`, and object or array values in path, header and cookie params into `[object Object]` or a lossy comma string.

`RestApiTool` is what `OpenAPIToolset` builds for each operation in a spec: the model fills in the params, and `prepareRequestParams` (core/src/tools/openapi_tool/rest_api_tool.ts) maps them onto the URL, query, headers, cookies and body before the request goes out.

Query params already handle this nicely (thanks to #1135): `null`, `undefined` and `''` are skipped and objects are JSON encoded. Path (~L343), header (~L355) and cookie (~L357) just use `String(argValue)`.

**To Reproduce**
1. Have an operation with a path param `id`, header params `X-Tenant` and `X-Filter`, a cookie param `session`, and a query param `q`. Any of them nullable in the spec is enough, since `gemini_schema_util.ts` (~L160) tells the model `null` is allowed.
2. The model calls the tool with `{id: {kind: 'a'}, 'X-Tenant': null, 'X-Filter': {role: 'admin'}, session: null, q: null}`.
3. `runAsync` passes `request.args` straight into `prepareRequestParams`.
4. The request goes out as:
   - url: `.../items/%5Bobject%20Object%5D`
   - headers: `{"X-Tenant": "null", "X-Filter": "[object Object]"}`
   - `Cookie: session=null`
   - `q` is correctly left out

`undefined` becomes `"undefined"` the same way, and an array like `[1, null]` becomes `"1,"`.

Minimal repro:

```ts
import {prepareRequestParams} from './core/src/tools/openapi_tool/rest_api_tool.js';

const p = (name: string, paramLocation: string) =>
  ({name, originalName: name, paramLocation, paramSchema: {}, required: false});

const out = prepareRequestParams(
  {baseUrl: 'https://api.example.com', path: '/items/{id}', method: 'get'},
  [p('id', 'path'), p('X-Tenant', 'header'), p('X-Filter', 'header'), p('session', 'cookie'), p('q', 'query')],
  {id: {kind: 'a'}, 'X-Tenant': null, 'X-Filter': {role: 'admin'}, session: null, q: null},
);
console.log(out);
// url ends with /items/%5Bobject%20Object%5D
// headers: { "X-Tenant": "null", "X-Filter": "[object Object]", Cookie: "session=null" }
// no q in the query string
```

**Expected behavior**
- Header and cookie params that are `null` or `undefined` are skipped, the same way query params are.
- Arrays and objects in path, header and cookie params are serialized per OpenAPI `style: simple`, matching `adk-python`'s `_to_param_string` (rest_api_tool.py ~L92 to 117): arrays comma joined with `None` dropped, objects as `k,v` pairs, booleans as `true`/`false`. Python also skips `None` for header (~L527) and cookie (~L530).

**Desktop (please complete the following information):**
 - OS: any
 - TS version/environment: Node
 - ADK version: main at eedc561

**Additional context**
One thing I wasn't sure about: Python sends `None` into the path too (no guard there), so a `null` path param is a gap in both. Should that be handled here as well, maybe by leaving it out or raising a clear error? Would you be open to one PR covering header, cookie and path in the same style as #1135?

Also kindly pointing to @OsamaAnsar's #1208, which fixes the same kind of serialization for form bodies, so this would be its sibling for the other param locations.

Happy to open a PR for this if it sounds good to you.
