issue.title: execute_sql runs MERGE ... WHEN MATCHED THEN DELETE without the destructive confirmation
issue.body:
Hey folks, I think `execute_sql` lets a `MERGE ... WHEN MATCHED THEN DELETE` (or `THEN UPDATE`) run without the destructive SQL confirmation, even when it touches every row.

### What the confirmation is for

When `execute_sql` is in `confirmation.enabledTools` (opt in, and the client needs elicitation support), the server asks before running SQL it considers destructive. The prompt text in `database-operation-tools.ts:502` says it covers "DROP, DELETE, TRUNCATE or UPDATE without WHERE". A MERGE that deletes or updates every matched row seems to fit that intent pretty squarely.

### Current behavior

1. Create a table with two rows: `create table films (id int, title text); insert into films values (1, 'a'), (2, 'b');`
2. Run the server not read only, with `execute_sql` in `confirmation.enabledTools`, using a client that supports elicitation.
3. Call `execute_sql` with `merge into films f using films s on true when matched then delete`
4. No confirmation is shown (the decision is recorded as `bypass` with reason `not_destructive`).
5. Both rows are gone.

### Expected behavior

The same confirmation you get for `delete from films` should show up before the MERGE runs.

### Minimal repro

Against main at 7e5037b:

```ts
import { isDestructiveSql } from './packages/mcp-server-supabase/src/tools/destructive-sql.js';

isDestructiveSql('merge into films f using (select 1) s on true when matched then delete');                  // false
isDestructiveSql('merge into films f using films s on true when matched then delete');                       // false
isDestructiveSql('explain analyze merge into films f using films s on true when matched then delete');       // false
isDestructiveSql('merge into films f using films s on true when matched then update set title = null');      // false

isDestructiveSql('delete from films');                // true
isDestructiveSql('update films set title = null');    // true
```

From reading the code, I think this is why:

* `destructive-sql.ts:70` only flags statements that start with `drop`, `delete` or `truncate`.
* `isUpdateWithoutWhereFromScan` (`destructive-sql.ts:191` to `197`) needs the statement to start with `update`.
* The `explain analyze` recheck (`destructive-sql.ts:272` to `279`) runs those same checks on the body, so it misses MERGE too.
* `database-operation-tools.ts:78` then skips the confirmation with `not_destructive`.

```mermaid
flowchart LR
  A[execute_sql with MERGE] --> B{starts with drop, delete, truncate or update?}
  B -- no --> C[not_destructive]
  C --> D[runs with no confirmation]
```

### Related work

Huge thanks to @barryroodt for #408, which added this whole confirmation flow, and for #426, which moves the check onto a real parser. The data modifying CTE forms (`with d as (delete ... returning) select ...`, and `explain analyze` of them) are already listed as a known trade off in #408 and handled in #426, so I'm only raising MERGE here. From what I can see, `classifyStatement` in #426 doesn't have a `MergeStmt` branch yet, so MERGE would still slip through after it lands.

### Question

Would you rather have MERGE added as a small check on the current scanner, or handled as a `MergeStmt` case in #426? Totally happy either way, and I'm glad to send a PR for whichever you prefer (or leave it to Barry if it fits better in #426). Let me know if I've misread anything!

comment.body:
Hey @barryroodt, hope you're doing well! Thank you for the clear call here, and for reviewing and merging #533 so quickly. Keeping the regex fallback free of more special cases makes a lot of sense to me, and the parser work in #426 sounds like the right home for MERGE.

If it would help, I'm happy to turn the `MERGE ... WHEN MATCHED THEN DELETE` repro from this issue, along with the `dblink_exec` and `cron.schedule` cases you mentioned on #533, into test cases for #426 whenever you're ready for them. Would you like this issue kept open to track MERGE until the parser ships, or closed in favour of #426? Either works for me. Thanks again to you and @mattrossman for digging into it!

issue.title: [BUG] @mastra/upstash: $not, $nor and $and/$or keep only the first key of a condition

labels.name: repo-0c4007c1
labels.description: Issues with Mastra's RAG system

labels.name: repo-0c4007c1
labels.description: Issue is fixed but not yet released

labels.name: repo-0c4007c1
labels.description: Issue entered the automatic triage queue

labels.name: repo-0c4007c1
labels.description: Triage severity: medium

issue.body:
### Describe the Bug

Hey Mastra team, hope you're all doing well! This is my first issue here, so any tips on how you like issues filed are very welcome. In the Upstash vector store, a `$not`, `$nor`, `$and` or `$or` condition with more than one key silently keeps only the first key. I saw how nicely #25353 (thanks @Bdysj, and @abhiaiyer91 for merging) fixed the same pattern for pg and libsql, and I think Upstash still has it.

`UpstashFilterTranslator` turns Mastra filters into Upstash filter strings for `query`, `updateVector` and `deleteVectors`. In `stores/upstash/src/vector/filter.ts`, `Object.entries(...)[0]` keeps just the first entry at lines 148 and 152 (field `$not`), 169 (operator `$not`) and 190 (each `$and`/`$or` element, which `$nor` reuses via line 117). The core type allows these filters (`$not: OperatorCondition` in `packages/core/src/vector/filter/base.ts:56`).

The result can be wrong in either direction, too wide or too narrow. Because `deleteVectors` and `updateVector` take filters (`index.ts:124,330,479`), the wrong rows can be deleted.

### Steps To Reproduce

1. In `stores/upstash/src/vector` on main, create `new UpstashFilterTranslator()` from `./filter` (it isn't exported from the package root).
2. Translate `{ price: { $not: { $gte: 10, $lte: 20 } } }`.
3. You get `price < 10`, so rows with price above 20 are missed.
4. Translate `{ $not: { a: 1, b: 2 } }` and you get `a != 1`.
5. Translate `{ $nor: [{ a: 1, b: 2 }] }` and you get `(a != 1)`.

```ts
import { UpstashFilterTranslator } from './filter';
const t = new UpstashFilterTranslator();
t.translate({ price: { $not: { $gte: 10, $lte: 20 } } }); // "price < 10"
t.translate({ $not: { a: 1, b: 2 } });                    // "a != 1"
t.translate({ $nor: [{ a: 1, b: 2 }] });                  // "(a != 1)"
t.translate({ price: { $not: { $gte: 10 } } });           // "price < 10" (correct)
t.translate({ price: { $gte: 10, $lte: 20 } });           // "(price >= 10 AND price <= 20)" (correct)
```

### Link to Minimal Reproducible Example

https://gist.github.com/abhiramshaji-cyber/9d69d9b1797946b589f161c3f713dc4a

### Expected Behavior

Every entry is used, like libsql does (`sql-builder.ts:486-504,522-530`):
- `(price < 10 OR price > 20)`
- `(a != 1 OR b != 2)`
- `(a != 1 OR b != 2)`

Would you be happy with negating each entry and joining them with OR, to match libsql? Or would you rather keep the `$not` wrapper as is? I know outside PRs are paused right now, so I'm happy to share a branch with the fix and tests for these cases (the current ones in `filter.test.ts` only cover single keys) if that would help.

### Environment Information

```shell
@mastra/upstash 1.6.0 (main @ 36bbc29)
Node v24.13.0, macOS
LLM Provider: n/a (filter translation only)
```

### Verification

- [x] I have searched the existing issues to make sure this is not a duplicate
- [x] I have included sufficient information for the team to reproduce and understand the issue

comment.body:
Hey @DZH166, hope you're doing well, and thank you for picking this up! Negating every entry and joining them with OR is exactly what I had in mind, so it's great that it lines up with what libsql got in #25353.

One small pointer in case it's useful: `$nor` doesn't have its own branch. It goes through `formatNot('', { $or: value })` on line 117 of `stores/upstash/src/vector/filter.ts`, so it picks up the `$and`/`$or` fix at line 190 for free. The current `$not` and `$nor` tests in `filter.test.ts` all use a single key per condition, so a multi key case for each path (field `$not` at lines 148 and 152, operator `$not` at 169, `$and`/`$or` at 190, and `$nor`) would cover it nicely.

Since the issue still has the needs triage label, I'll leave the timing to the maintainers. Would the team be happy for this PR to go ahead once it's triaged? I'm glad to help test or review it either way.

issue.title: Validate post before following thread on set_unread

labels.name: repo-8e1e942e
labels.description: Denotes a PR that will be considered when it comes time to generate release notes.

issue.body:
Fixes #39348

Marking a thread unread with a post that is not in that thread used to wipe its unread counts and follow it anyway; now the request fails without touching the thread.

**What this code is for**

`POST /api/v4/users/{user_id}/teams/{team_id}/threads/{thread_id}/set_unread/{post_id}` is what the client calls when a person picks "Mark as unread" on a reply in a thread. The handler `setUnreadThreadByPostId` checks permissions, then `UpdateThreadReadForUserByPost` loads the post and moves the thread's last viewed time to just before that post, so the replies after it count as unread again. The thread is also followed so it shows up in the person's threads list.

**Before this PR**

A person has a thread with 2 unread replies and 1 unread mention, and separately has unfollowed another thread. A client sends `set_unread` with a `post_id` that belongs to a different thread.

1. `setUnreadThreadByPostId` checks the person can read the thread.
2. It calls `UpdateThreadFollowForUser(..., true)`, which sets `Following` to true and updates the viewed timestamp to now.
3. It calls `UpdateThreadReadForUserByPost`, which loads the post with `GetSinglePost`.
4. The `if post.RootId != threadID && postID != threadID` check fails and returns 400.
5. The person gets an error, but the thread already shows 0 unread replies and 0 mentions, and an unfollowed thread is followed again.

**After this PR**

Same person, same request.

1. `setUnreadThreadByPostId` checks the person can read the thread.
2. It calls `UpdateThreadReadForUserByPost` directly.
3. `GetSinglePost` loads the post, and the `post.RootId` check fails and returns 400 (or `GetSinglePost` returns 404 for a post that does not exist).
4. `UpdateThreadFollowForUser` is never called, so `Following`, the viewed timestamp and the unread counts stay exactly as they were.
5. With a valid post from the thread, the check passes, `UpdateThreadFollowForUser(..., true)` runs, then `UpdateThreadReadForUser` marks it unread, same as before.

**The diagram**

```mermaid
flowchart LR

classDef box fill:#eef1ff,stroke:#4c5bd4,color:#111827
classDef bad fill:#ffd6d6,stroke:#cc0000,color:#111827,stroke-width:3px
classDef good fill:#c8f0c8,stroke:#008800,color:#111827,stroke-width:3px

subgraph BEFORE["BEFORE: error, but unread counts cleared and thread followed"]
direction TB
  B1["client sends set_unread with a post from another thread"] --> B2["setUnreadThreadByPostId"]
  B2 --> B3["UpdateThreadFollowForUser true"]
  B3 --> B4["UpdateThreadReadForUserByPost"]
  B4 --> B5{"post.RootId == threadID ?"}
  B5 -->|"no: 400, follow already saved"| B6["counts at 0, thread followed"]
  B5 -->|"yes"| B7["UpdateThreadReadForUser"]
end

subgraph AFTER["AFTER: error, thread unchanged"]
direction TB
  A1["client sends set_unread with a post from another thread"] --> A2["setUnreadThreadByPostId"]
  A2 --> A3["UpdateThreadReadForUserByPost"]
  A3 --> A4{"THE CHANGE: post checked before follow"}
  A4 -->|"no: 400"| A5["counts and follow state unchanged"]
  A4 -->|"yes"| A6["UpdateThreadFollowForUser then UpdateThreadReadForUser"]
end

B1 ~~~ A1

class B1,B2,B4,B5,B7 box
class A1,A2,A3,A6 box
class B3,B6 bad
class A4,A5 good

linkStyle 4 stroke:#cc0000,stroke-width:5px
linkStyle 9 stroke:#008800,stroke-width:5px

style BEFORE fill:#fff5f5,stroke:#cc0000,color:#111827
style AFTER fill:#f3fff3,stroke:#008800,color:#111827
```

**The change**

The `UpdateThreadFollowForUser(..., true)` call moved out of `setUnreadThreadByPostId` in `api4/user.go` and into `UpdateThreadReadForUserByPost` in `app/user.go`, placed after `GetSinglePost` and the `post.RootId != threadID && postID != threadID` check. That ordering is the fix. The follow on a successful request is kept, it just runs after the post is known to belong to the thread.

`TestReadThreads` gets a new case that sends a post from another thread (400) and a post id that does not exist (404), for both a followed and an unfollowed thread, and checks the thread membership is identical before and after and the threads list still shows the same unread replies.

**What changes for a user**

- A failed "Mark as unread" no longer clears the unread replies and mentions on the thread.
- A failed request no longer follows a thread the person had unfollowed.
- A valid "Mark as unread" still follows the thread and marks the chosen reply and everything after it as unread.

#### Summary

Covered above.

#### Ticket Link

Fixes https://github.com/mattermost/mattermost/issues/39348

#### Release Note

```release-note
Fixed an issue where a failed request to mark a thread as unread cleared the thread's unread counts and followed the thread.
```

issue.title: fix(shift): stop a seeded $# from crashing shift
issue.body:
A `$#` seeded by the host could make `shift` hang or crash; now `shift` only touches the parameters that really exist, so it stays fast for any `$#`.

This is the small follow up to the `shift` loop we talked about in #729. Thanks again @jamalkamaladdin for spotting it there.

**What this code is for**

`handleShift` in `builtins/shift.ts` runs `shift [n]`. It moves `$n+1` and later down to `$1`, then sets `$#` and `$@`. Scripts normally set `$#` themselves through `set --`, function calls and `source`, but a host can also pass `"#"` in `env` when it creates `new Bash(...)`.

**Before this PR**

A host creates `new Bash({ env: { "#": "1000000", "1": "a", "2": "b" } })` and runs a script that calls `shift` 2000 times.

1. `handleShift` reads `$#` with `Number.parseInt`: 1000000.
2. It builds an array of 1000000 slots with one `env.get` per slot, then deletes and rewrites every slot, filling the missing ones with an empty string. Every `shift` does this again.
3. The 2000 shifts take about 215 seconds. With a `$#` of `1000000000` the array cannot be built and `shift` fails with `Invalid array length`.

**After this PR**

Same host, same script.

1. `leadingInteger` reads `$#` as a `BigInt` from at most 20 digits, so a huge digit string is never parsed.
2. Because `$#` is larger than `env.size`, `moveScanned` goes through `env` once and keeps only the keys `1` to `$#` that are stored: `1` and `2`.
3. It deletes those keys and writes the ones above `n` back `n` lower. The 999998 slots that were never stored stay unset.
4. The 2000 shifts finish in about 80 milliseconds, and `$#` ends at 998000.

A script that sets its own arguments (`set -- 1 2 ... 20000`, then shifts until `$#` is 0) has `$#` at most `env.size`, so it goes through `moveWalked` instead. That walks `1..$#` with plain numbers and moves each key in place: 10.3 s against 12.8 s on main for that whole loop.

**The diagram**

```mermaid
flowchart LR

classDef box fill:#eef1ff,stroke:#4c5bd4,color:#111827
classDef bad fill:#ffd6d6,stroke:#cc0000,color:#111827,stroke-width:3px
classDef good fill:#c8f0c8,stroke:#008800,color:#111827,stroke-width:3px

subgraph BEFORE["BEFORE: 2000 shifts take about 215 s"]
direction TB
  B1["host seeds $# = 1000000, script runs shift"] --> B2["handleShift"]
  B2 --> B3["Number.parseInt reads $#"]
  B3 --> B4{"walk every slot from 1 to $#"}
  B4 -->|"every shift"| B5["rewrites 1000000 slots, fills gaps with empty strings"]
  B4 -->|"set -- in a script"| B6["rewrites its own slots"]
end

subgraph AFTER["AFTER: 2000 shifts take about 80 ms"]
direction TB
  A1["host seeds $# = 1000000, script runs shift"] --> A2["handleShift"]
  A2 --> A3["leadingInteger reads $#, at most 20 digits"]
  A3 --> A4{"THE CHANGE: $# at most env.size?"}
  A4 -->|"no, moveScanned"| A5["moves the 2 stored keys, gaps stay unset"]
  A4 -->|"yes, moveWalked"| A6["walks 1 to $# with numbers, same keys"]
end

B1 ~~~ A1

class B1,B2,B3,B6 box
class A1,A2,A3,A6 box
class B4,B5 bad
class A4,A5 good

linkStyle 3 stroke:#cc0000,stroke-width:5px
linkStyle 8 stroke:#008800,stroke-width:5px

style BEFORE fill:#fff5f5,stroke:#cc0000,color:#111827
style AFTER fill:#f3fff3,stroke:#008800,color:#111827
```

**The change**

The fix is `moveStoredParams` in the new `helpers/stored-params.ts`, called from `handleShift`. It moves only stored keys: `moveWalked` when `count <= BigInt(env.size)`, `moveScanned` otherwise. Both find the same keys, so the choice only changes the cost, which is bounded by the smaller of `$#` and `env.size`. `moveScanned` checks `key.length` before the regex and `BigInt(key)`, so a long numeric key is never parsed.

`leadingInteger` in the same file reads at most 20 digits and is exact up to 2 ** 63 - 1. `handleShift` checks, in order: a bad `n` (`numeric argument required`), a non numeric `$#` (main's result), a `$#` above 2 ** 63 - 1 (`shift 0` returns 0, anything else fails with `bash: shift: $#: positional parameter count out of range` and status 1), then `n > $#` and `n === 0` as on main.

Two small changes elsewhere follow from gaps staying unset:

- `getVariable` in `expansion/variable.ts`: under `set -u`, `$N` raises `unbound variable` only when `N` is above `$#`, read with the same `positionalCount`. That keeps every `set -u` script that ran on main running.
- `setPositionalParameters` in `builtins/set.ts`: `set --` first removes every stored key from `1` to the old `$#` with `moveStoredParams(env, count, count)`, then runs its existing walk starting at `$# + 1`, deleting keys until the first missing one. Main's walk started at `1` and stopped at the first missing key, so after a `shift` left a gap, later keys would have stayed behind. With no gap, both remove the same keys.

**What changes for a user**

- Scripts, functions, `source` and `set --` with no gaps behave exactly as before, and every test here passes with and without #729 applied. That includes `set --` inside a sourced file clearing the caller's `$10` and `$11`. The bash comparison suite passes, and draining 20000 arguments is a little faster than main.
- A host seeded `$#` of any size no longer hangs or crashes `shift`, and the same script and `env` always give the same result, whatever other variables exist.
- Changed from main, only where a slot up to `$#` has nothing stored (a host seeded `$#` above the stored keys, or `$10` and later from `source` until #729 lands): after `shift` that slot stays unset instead of becoming an empty string. So `${2-U}` prints `U`, `${2+x}` prints nothing, `[ -v 2 ]` is false, and `v=$@` (which reads the stored `@` copy) has no doubled space for it. `"$@"`, `"$*"` and `$#` still count it as an empty field, and a bare `for x; do` still skips it, as on main. Filling the gaps is what made the work grow with `$#`, so this is on purpose.
- Changed from main: when a host seeded `$#` has a gap below it, `set --` now removes every stored key up to that `$#` and the run of keys right above it, where main stopped at the first gap.
- Changed from main: under `set -u`, `$N` with `N` at most `$#` expands to an empty string instead of failing with `unbound variable`, even before any `shift`. For example, until #729 lands, a file sourced with 11 arguments that runs `set -u; echo "${10}"` now prints an empty line where main stopped with `10: unbound variable`. A non numeric `$#` or one above 2 ** 63 - 1 counts as 0 here, so those keep main's errors. So a missing slot is unset for `${N-x}`, `${N+x}` and `[ -v N ]` but counts as set for `set -u`. Main failed there before a `shift` and passed after one; bash never has such a slot.
- Changed from main: a `$#` above 2 ** 63 - 1 makes every `shift` except `shift 0` fail with status 1 instead of crashing or hanging. Bash itself never has a `$#` that large.
- Not changed, already different from bash on main: `shift -1` says `numeric argument required` (bash says `shift count out of range`), `shift 3abc` shifts by 3 (bash says `numeric argument required`), a count above 2 ** 63 - 1 says `shift count out of range` (bash says `numeric argument required`), and the out of range message is always printed (bash prints it only with `shopt -s shift_verbose`).
- `getopts`, `"$*"` and some other expansions also loop up to `$#` (after this `shift` with a seeded 1e9, `echo "$*"` still fails), and `functions.ts` does too until #729 lands. Happy to look at those next if that helps.

Thanks so much for the careful review, all three points were spot on and the repros made them easy to confirm.

2bfa05b: shift now moves only the $1..$# keys that are actually stored, so the work no longer grows with a seeded $#. It walks 1..$# when $# is at most env.size and scans env once otherwise, and both find the same keys, so ${2-U} and [ -v 2 ] no longer change with unrelated variables. A seeded $# of 1000000 with 2000 shifts went from about 215 s to under 100 ms.

76a0e37, d1d5d5f and ba8e700: $# is read from at most 20 digits and exactly up to 2 ** 63 - 1, and stored keys longer than $# are skipped before any parsing. Above that bound, shift 0 still returns 0 like main and every other shift fails with status 1. The walk uses plain numbers, so draining 20000 arguments is a little faster than main (10.3 s against 12.8 s).

22e0607, ba8e700 and a2df117: since gaps now stay unset after a shift, set -u treats $1 to $# as set, reading $# with the same bounded parser, and set -- removes every stored key up to the old $# and keeps clearing the keys right above it, so scripts that ran on main keep running.

ac23d5c adds tests for the seeded gap under set -u, set -u with an unusable $#, and set -- with a large seeded $#. Every test passes with and without #729 applied, and the PR description lists every behaviour change from main.

Hey @jamalkamaladdin, hope you're doing well! Does keeping gaps unset sound right to you, or would you rather shift throw an ExecutionLimitError when $# is above maxArrayElements, the way "$@" does? Happy to switch, and I'd really love any tips.

issue.title: fix: Let Agent v3 run the legacy HTTP Request Tool and Call n8n Workflow Tool v1

labels.name: repo-361234ab
labels.description: Authored by a community member

labels.name: repo-361234ab
labels.description: Triage has been completed and issue is ready for internal teams

issue.body: ## Summary Agent v3 sends every tool call through the execution engine, which runs the tool node's `execute()`. #19997 added `execute()` to the AI tool nodes, but the legacy HTTP Request Tool (`toolHttpRequest`) and the Call n8n Workflow Tool v1 (versions 1 to 1.3) only have `supplyData()`. So the engine throws `has a "supplyData" method but no "execute" method` and the agent gets that error back instead of a result. This PR gives both nodes an `execute()`, using the same pattern as the Code Tool. The tool building moves into a `getTool(ctx, itemIndex, log)` function, and `execute()` invokes the tool once per input item and returns the result with `pairedItem`. When the engine runs the node, the tool skips `addInputData`, `addOutputData` and `logAiEvent` (the engine already records the run) and throws on errors, so the engine's continue on fail default for AI tools hands the error to the agent. Before: Agent v3.1 calls the tool, the engine throws, and the model sees `[{"error":"The node ... has a \"supplyData\" method but no \"execute\" method."}]`. After: the engine runs the tool, and the model sees the HTTP response or the child workflow's output. ```mermaid flowchart LR A[Agent v3] -->|tool call| E[Engine] E -->|before| X[throw: no execute] E -->|after| T["execute()"] --> G["getTool(log = false).invoke(item.json)"] G --> R["{ json, pairedItem }"] --> A ``` A few details: - HTTP Request Tool: the item is `{ response }`, the same shape the node already logs. HTTP failures and binary bodies still come back as readable error text, as they do today, so the model can react to them. Invalid model input throws. When the model input can't be parsed, the request is no longer sent at all, on both paths. Before, it still went out with the placeholders unfilled and the credentials attached. On `supplyData` the model now always gets `Input provided by model is not valid` for such input, instead of the error from the request that went out. An empty input on 1.0 is now validated too, so a required placeholder that is missing stops the request. When the tool fails, also while it is being built, the error carries the index of the failing item. - Call n8n Workflow Tool v1: the item is the child workflow's JSON (strings and other non object values are wrapped as `{ response }`), which matches what V2 returns from the engine. The child execution is linked with `setMetadata`, like V2 does. `execute()` follows the Code Tool's `execute()`: it calls `tool.invoke` and lets the tool's own Zod schema strip or validate the keys. Unlike the Code Tool, it first drops `toolCallId` from the engine item, because it isn't tool input and an open schema would pass it to the child workflow as data. The engine item also carries the agent input, and the node can't tell those keys from the model arguments. So two limits remain, the same as for V2 and the Code Tool: an open or record style schema (no properties, or `additionalProperties` true) passes the agent input fields to the child workflow too, and a schema that limits extra keys without declaring properties (for example only `patternProperties` or a typed `additionalProperties`) may reject them. The engine could fix this for V1, V2 and the Code Tool together by passing `action.input` separately through the task metadata, so each node gets the model's exact arguments. When the child workflow fails, or the tool can't be built (for example an invalid input schema), the error carries the index of the failing item, as in V2. - One small change I should mention for the Call n8n Workflow Tool v1 on the `supplyData` path: a child output that parses to something other than an object (a number or an array) is now logged as `{ response }` instead of the raw parsed value. The string the model receives is the same as before. - Apart from the changes above (the HTTP Request Tool no longer sends a request when the model input can't be parsed, an empty input on 1.0 is validated, and the Call n8n Workflow Tool v1 logs a non object child output as `{ response }`), the agent path through `supplyData` does not change. - One limit I want to flag, not changed here: the engine merges the agent input item into each tool item, so an optional key the model leaves out can be filled from the agent item, and an agent item key with the same name but a different type can make validation fail. This also affects the HTTP Request Tool 1.1 and the V2 and Code tools. ## Why Anyone with one of these nodes attached to Agent v3 or v3.1 can't use the tool at all. Thank you @kemrec for the clear repro, and @ardaerturk for confirming that `n8n-nodes-base.httpRequestTool` works as a replacement in the meantime. One question: I see the HTTP Request Tool is hidden and on the 3.x removal list (`removed-nodes-with-replacements.rule.ts`). Would you like both nodes fixed here, or only the Call n8n Workflow Tool v1? The changes are in two separate commits, so it's easy to drop the HTTP part if you'd prefer people move to the replacement node instead. ## How to test 1. Build a workflow: Manual Trigger, AI Agent 3.1, any chat model, and a legacy HTTP Request Tool (or a Call n8n Workflow Tool at version 1.3) connected as a tool. 2. Ask something that makes the agent call the tool. 3. Before this change the tool run fails with the "no execute method" error. After it, the response reaches the model. Tests: - `nodes/agents/Agent/test/integration/agent-v3.workflow.test.ts`: new case that runs Agent 3.1 with the legacy HTTP Request Tool through the real engine and checks that the HTTP response reaches the second model call. It runs for both 1.1 and 1.0, and fails on master with the exact error from the issue. - `ToolHttpRequest/test/ToolHttpRequest.execute.test.ts`: several items, pairing, no manual logging, HTTP error and binary responses, valid model input on 1.0 sent as `GET /users/42`, only the model arguments sent from the engine item on 1.0 and 1.1, invalid input on 1 and 1.1, that invalid input never sends the request, and the item index when the tool can't be built for the second item. `ToolHttpRequest.node.test.ts` checks the same on the `supplyData` path. - `ToolWorkflow.node.test.ts`: V1 `execute` with several items, subexecution metadata, the engine item without `toolCallId` for an object schema (agent keys stripped) and an open schema, a waiting child workflow, non object responses, a failing child workflow, and the item index when the second item fails, its input doesn't match the schema, or its tool can't be built. Locally `typecheck`, `lint` and the whole `@n8n/n8n-nodes-langchain` vitest suite pass. ## Related Linear tickets, Github issues, and Community forum posts Fixes #41604 ## Review / Merge checklist - [x] I have seen this code, I have run this code, and I take responsibility for this code. - [x] PR title and summary are descriptive. ([conventions](../blob/master/.github/pull_request_title_conventions.md)) - [ ] [Docs updated](https://github.com/n8n-io/n8n-docs) or follow-up ticket created. - [x] Tests included. - [ ] PR Labeled with `Backport to Beta`, `Backport to Stable`, or `Backport to v1` (if the PR is an urgent fix that needs to be backported)

comment.body:
Hey everyone, hope you're doing well! Thanks so much for all the careful review here.

In e8306c3 I simplified the Call n8n Workflow Tool v1 to follow the Code Tool's `execute()`: it lets the tool's own schema strip or check the keys, and it also drops `toolCallId` so that never reaches the child workflow. The one gap it shares with V2 and the Code Tool is that the engine item mixes the agent input with the model arguments, so open schemas still get the agent fields. Passing `action.input` separately through the task metadata would fix all three. Would you like that here, or in a follow up PR?

Thanks, fair point to double check. The engine item in these cases also carries `units: 'metric'`, which matches both `^u` (string) and `n` (number), and the expected query `{ city, turn }` leaves it out. I tried swapping `every()` for `some()` and this case failed on `units`, so I kept it as is. In b0e8e16 the filter now asks the tool's own schema instead of checking the patterns by hand, and this case still passes.

Thanks, good catch! In b0e8e16 an extra key is now checked against the tool's own input schema, so it only needs to fit one applicable `anyOf`/`oneOf` branch, while `allOf` parts and the top level schema still all have to accept it. Added tests where a key is allowed by just one branch, and where the only branch that allows it doesn't apply.

issue.title: @posthog/ai: Anthropic wrapper doesn't capture thinking tokens as $ai_reasoning_tokens
issue.body:
## Bug description

The Anthropic wrapper in `@posthog/ai` never sets `$ai_reasoning_tokens`, even when Claude reports thinking token counts.

The wrapper is there so Anthropic calls show up in LLM analytics with token counts and cost, same as the OpenAI and Gemini wrappers. Since 0.100.0, `@anthropic-ai/sdk` has `output_tokens_details: { thinking_tokens } | null` on both `Usage` and `MessageDeltaUsage`, so it exists on every version in the current peer range (`>=0.112.3 <0.135.0`). The Anthropic docs point people to `usage.output_tokens_details.thinking_tokens` for monitoring this, and when streaming it comes in on the final `message_delta`.

Right now:

1. A call with extended thinking enabled goes through the wrapper.
2. Anthropic returns `usage.output_tokens_details.thinking_tokens` (on the response, or on the last `message_delta` when streaming).
3. The streaming usage block in `packages/ai/src/anthropic/index.ts` (around L245 to L272) only reads `output_tokens`, and the non streaming path (around L390 to L397) does the same, so `reasoningTokens` is never set.
4. `captureAiGeneration.ts` (L192) only emits `$ai_reasoning_tokens` when `usage.reasoningTokens` is set, so the event goes out without it.

The Claude Agent SDK processor has the same gap: `AnthropicUsage` in `claude-agent-sdk/processor.ts` (around L70 to L76) and `readUsage` (around L870 to L880) don't read the field either.

Other wrappers already do this (`openai/telemetry.ts` L97 and L112, `gemini/usage.ts` L14, the Vercel middleware and the LangChain callbacks), so Anthropic is the odd one out. From what I can tell the ingestion side (`modality-tokens.ts` in PostHog/posthog) doesn't derive it from `$ai_usage` and drops `$ai_usage` afterwards, so Anthropic events never end up with the metric.

**Expected:** map `output_tokens_details.thinking_tokens` to `reasoningTokens` in the stream, non stream and agent SDK paths, like OpenAI and Gemini. A `null` `output_tokens_details` would just be treated as absent.

Cost isn't affected here. `output_tokens` already includes thinking, and the server only adds a separate reasoning cost for Gemini 2.5 and 3, so this is only about the reasoning token count being visible.

## How to reproduce

1. Wrap a mocked Anthropic client with `@posthog/ai` and have `messages.create` return:
   ```ts
   {
     id: 'msg_1',
     type: 'message',
     role: 'assistant',
     model: 'claude-sonnet-4-5',
     content: [{ type: 'text', text: 'hi' }],
     stop_reason: 'end_turn',
     usage: {
       input_tokens: 20,
       output_tokens: 600,
       output_tokens_details: { thinking_tokens: 512 },
     },
   }
   ```
2. Call `messages.create` through the wrapper (or stream with the same usage on the final `message_delta`).
3. The captured `$ai_generation` has `$ai_output_tokens: 600` but no `$ai_reasoning_tokens`.

## Related sub-libraries

- [ ] All of them
- [ ] posthog-js (web)
- [ ] posthog-js-lite (web lite)
- [ ] posthog-node
- [ ] posthog-react-native
- [ ] @posthog/react
- [x] @posthog/ai
- [ ] @posthog/convex
- [ ] @posthog/nextjs-config
- [ ] @posthog/nuxt
- [ ] @posthog/rollup-plugin
- [ ] @posthog/webpack-plugin

## Additional context

Related: #5375, which nicely captures the thinking text as reasoning content. This would be the count side of the same thing. #3160 covers Gemini reasoning cost.

Two questions before I touch anything:

- Would you want the Claude Agent SDK processor fixed in the same change, or kept separate?
- Is client side the right place for this, given the server drops `$ai_usage`? Or would you rather derive it during ingestion?

Happy to put up a PR for whichever way you prefer. Seen on main at a0e6485.

issue.title: feat(review): review each commit of a PR separately
issue.body:
With per commit review turned on by the host, `/review` reviews each commit of a PR on its own diff and commit message, instead of only the combined diff.

Closes #4470. It is opt in and host only. The commit messages piece was split out into #4603, as suggested, and that has now landed on `main`.

**What this code is for**

`PRReviewer.run()` in `pr_agent/commands/pr_reviewer.py` handles `/review`. It asks the git provider for the PR diff, renders `pr_reviewer_prompts.toml` with that diff, makes one model call (or a few when chunking), and publishes one review comment.

**Before this PR**

A maintainer on GitLab has an MR with 4 commits, each with a message that explains one change, and comments `/review`.

1. `PRReviewer.run()` asks `GitLabProvider.get_diff_files()` for the diff of the whole MR.
2. The prompt gets that combined diff, plus the title and description.
3. The model returns findings with file and line, but nothing says which commit a finding belongs to.
4. One review comment for the whole MR. The maintainer has to work out by hand which of the 4 commits needs the fixup.

**After this PR**

Same maintainer, same MR, with `per_commit_review = true` in the host config or `.pr_agent.toml`.

1. `PRReviewer.run()` sees `per_commit_review` and calls `_run_per_commit()`.
2. `get_pr_commits()` returns the 4 commits, oldest first, with their parents, read fresh from the provider on every run. Merge commits are dropped here without loading them. `_commit_review_records()` reads the commits already reviewed from hidden markers in PR-Agent's own comments. For each commit not already listed by SHA, `set_commit_review_scope()` loads its files once and returns a fingerprint of its own patch, and only commits whose fingerprint is not recorded are kept. On the first run there are no markers, so all 4 are kept.
3. For each commit, `set_commit_review_scope()` scopes the diff to that commit against its parent, and `commit_under_review` puts its message (clipped to `max_commits_tokens`) in the prompt, between random markers made fresh for each run. `commit_messages_str` is cleared, so the prompt does not also list every other commit's message.
4. `_run_review()` runs once per commit and publishes one comment that names and links the commit. It uses the incremental review header, so it never replaces the persistent full review.
5. A commit with no findings gets no comment when `pr_reviewer.publish_output_no_suggestions = false`. With `inline_key_issues = true`, findings land inline on that commit's own diff.
6. 4 comments, one per commit, each with a `<!-- pr-agent:reviewed-commit <fingerprint> <sha> -->` line two lines below the hidden `<!-- pr-agent:review:incremental -->` identity. On the next push with 1 new commit, only that commit is reviewed. Without the setting, `/review` takes exactly the old path.

**The diagram**

```mermaid
flowchart LR

classDef box fill:#eef1ff,stroke:#4c5bd4,color:#111827
classDef bad fill:#ffd6d6,stroke:#cc0000,color:#111827,stroke-width:3px
classDef good fill:#c8f0c8,stroke:#008800,color:#111827,stroke-width:3px

subgraph BEFORE["BEFORE: 1 review for 4 commits"]
direction TB
  B1["Maintainer comments /review"] --> B2["PRReviewer.run"]
  B2 --> B3["get_diff_files for the whole MR"]
  B3 --> B4{"one prompt, combined diff"}
  B4 -->|"findings not tied to a commit"| B5["1 comment for the whole MR"]
  B4 -->|"per_commit_review off"| B6["same as today"]
end

subgraph AFTER["AFTER: 1 review per commit"]
direction TB
  A1["Maintainer comments /review"] --> A2["PRReviewer.run"]
  A2 --> A3["get_pr_commits"]
  A3 --> A4{"THE CHANGE: per_commit_review on"}
  A4 -->|"each commit: own diff and message"| A5["1 comment per commit, linked"]
  A4 -->|"setting off or provider unsupported"| A6["whole PR review, as today"]
end

B1 ~~~ A1

class B1,B2,B3,B6 box
class A1,A2,A3,A6 box
class B4,B5 bad
class A4,A5 good

linkStyle 3 stroke:#cc0000,stroke-width:5px
linkStyle 8 stroke:#008800,stroke-width:5px

style BEFORE fill:#fff5f5,stroke:#cc0000,color:#111827
style AFTER fill:#f3fff3,stroke:#008800,color:#111827
```

**The change**

* `PRReviewer.run()` now branches on `per_commit_review` into `_run_per_commit()`, and the old body moved into `_run_review()` unchanged apart from the commit header and the checks below.
* `GitProvider` gets `get_pr_commits()` (returns `None` by default, so other providers fall back to a whole PR review with a notice) and `set_commit_review_scope()`. GitHub and GitLab implement both on top of the existing incremental diff path. On GitHub, new side file contents are read at the commit when a head SHA is set.
* `_run_per_commit()` reviews only commits whose fingerprint is not recorded, so a plain `/review` and the default `push_commands` no longer review every commit again on each push (454174f1, 40cb6ee2, b52fbf25, bf4dd1b6, 9b159195). `commit_patch_fingerprint()` in `git_provider.py` hashes each file's name and patch with the `@@ -a,b +c,d @@` numbers removed, so a rebase onto `main` that leaves a commit's own patch alone does not review it again, while an amend or `--autosquash` fixup does. On GitLab, when a file's diff comes back empty (collapsed, too large or binary), the commit SHA is mixed into the fingerprint so two different commits never share one; such a commit is reviewed again after a rebase. A commit is recorded only after its review succeeds, including when every file was filtered out: `_run_review()` puts the marker line two lines below the comment's hidden incremental review identity, and a commit that gets no comment (no findings with `publish_output_no_suggestions = false`) goes into one record comment that starts with `<!-- pr-agent:review:commits -->` and is edited in place through `publish_persistent_comment_full()`. With default settings and no merge commits, no record comment is created. Before writing, the record is read again and merged, trimmed to commits still in the PR, and cut from the oldest end if it would pass the 65000 character comment limit. Markers count only at those fixed lines and only in comments `is_comment_authored_by_pr_agent()` confirms. A marker in a comment confirmed as someone else's is ignored. Markers are found by that hidden identity rather than the visible heading, so changing `review_heading` never reviews commits again. When comment authorship cannot be checked for the run, or marker comments exist but none can be confirmed and the author of at least one cannot be verified (for example a GitHub App whose login cannot be resolved), the run falls back to one whole PR review with a notice instead of reviewing every commit on each push. Each commit's files are loaded once per run and reused for its review; a commit whose patch is already recorded under another SHA (a rebase) is recorded under the new SHA too, and a commit with no changes of its own is recorded, so neither is loaded again. A failed commit is not recorded, so the next run retries it; the record counts failed attempts, and automatic runs stop after `PER_COMMIT_MAX_AUTO_ATTEMPTS` (3) while a manual `/review` always retries. Selection does not use commit dates, so a commit authored before the last review but pushed after it is still reviewed. If the comments cannot be read, the run fails with the usual failure comment instead of reviewing every commit. The `-i` lookup and its `minimal_*_for_incremental_review` thresholds are not used here, so a manual `/review` never stops silently. `docs/docs/commands/review.md` says so, and also says that if PR-Agent's comments are removed, the next run reviews every commit again unless `max_commits_per_review` is set (93cb7440).
* The commit message block opens and closes with `{{ commit_message_begin }}` and `{{ commit_message_end }}` from `prompt_boundary_markers("COMMIT_MESSAGE")` (the helper #4603 added to `pr_agent/algo/artifacts.py`), so a commit message containing `<<<COMMIT_MESSAGE_END>>>` cannot close the block early. It sits right above #4603's `commit_messages_str` block, which keeps its own `COMMIT_MESSAGES` markers.
* `_should_publish_review_no_suggestions()` checks the parsed findings for a commit review, so a commit where the model returned nothing or prose stays quiet with `publish_output_no_suggestions = false`.
* `per_commit_review` and `max_commits_per_review` are in the `pr_reviewer` entry of `CLI_HOST_ONLY_KEYS_BY_SECTION` and `PER_DIRECTORY_HOST_ONLY_KEYS_BY_SECTION`, so `/review --pr_reviewer.per_commit_review=true` in a comment is rejected.
* `max_commits_per_review` defaults to 0 (no limit). When more commits than the cap are not reviewed yet, the whole PR is reviewed once with a notice, and after that review succeeds all its commits are recorded, so the next push goes back to one review per new commit. GitHub lists at most 250 commits per PR, so a PR with more is reviewed as a whole with a notice.
* Merge commits, root commits and empty commits are skipped. One failing commit does not stop the rest; the run is marked failed afterwards.
* Upstream `main` is merged in with merge commits (181edc4c, 9723af3a), not a rebase, so no history is rewritten. Conflicts: `convert_to_markdown_v2()` keeps main's `get_bot_display_name()` next to the commit header, `CLI_HOST_ONLY_KEYS_BY_SECTION` keeps main's new `pr_reviewer` keys plus ours, and the key count in `test_config_reference.py` is main's 319 plus our 2. After #4798, `run()` no longer checks `is_answer`, and the tests set `config.is_auto_command`. After #4838 renamed `pr_agent/tools` to `pr_agent/commands`, the tests import from `pr_agent.commands` and the config links point at `../commands/review.md` (ed7715a5). `_prepare_code_suggestions()` on GitHub skips `validate_comments_inside_hunks()` while a commit scope is set, so a finding outside that commit's diff stays in the commit's summary instead of moving to a nearby line. `pytest tests/unittest` on 912963d8: 17692 passed, 34 skipped. `ruff check`: clean.

**What changes for a user**

* Nothing unless the host turns on `per_commit_review`. Default `/review` is unchanged.
* With it on: one model call per reviewed commit. The first run reviews every commit, and later runs review only new commits or commits whose own changes changed, so `-i` is no longer needed in `push_commands`.
* Each commit's review sees only that commit's diff, so it can flag something a later commit fixes, or miss a helper added in an earlier commit.
* Only GitHub and GitLab support it. Other providers get the usual whole PR review with a one line notice.

comment.body: Thanks for double checking, this is really helpful! On the single parameter case, that fallback is on `master` today for every version of the tool, so I'd rather not change it in this PR, but I'd love to hear from the maintainers whether invalid input should be rejected there too. I added a unit test for the 1.0 happy path in 9e3752d0b6, so `{ input: '{"id":"42"}' }` going out as `GET /users/42` is now pinned at the node level. And good point on `getTool`: in the same commit it now runs inside the `try` in `execute()`, so a failure there on a later item also carries its `itemIndex`.

issue.title: Incompatibility between OpenAI and HF's Chat Completion `response_format`
issue.body:
Hi there!

OpenAI and HF api seem to have diverged on chat_completion `response_format`. That of the [OpenAI](https://github.com/openai/openai-python/blob/37f5615da1f4360710f6f45920dbb81387d1a4c5/src/openai/types/chat/completion_create_params.py#L272) has a `type` attribute which takes one of three values `text`, `json_object` (free-form JSON generation which isn't in TGI yet) and `json_schema`, and for the last one it has another `json_schema` attribute which itself contains `name`, `schema`, `description` and `strict` attributes. 

On the other hand, HF's `response_format: ChatCompletionInputGrammarType` [contains](https://github.com/huggingface/huggingface.js/blob/aeae64e4df999f61f5d872aa78545bd6a486c9a9/packages/tasks/src/tasks/chat-completion/spec/input.json#L228-L261) `type` and `value` attributes.

This might break the OpenAI api usability on HF models. Could we have compatibility between these two on this matter? Or does it need probably breaking changes in TGI and huggingface_hub?

@Wauplin

issue.title: McpAgent Streamable HTTP: no SSE keepalive on the GET stream — clients silently disconnect every ~100s behind the Cloudflare proxy idle read timeout

labels.name: repo-1a29122a
labels.description: Further information is requested

issue.body:
## Problem

Long-lived MCP client connections to a `McpAgent`-backed worker (Streamable HTTP) get cut by the Cloudflare proxy edge after ~100 seconds of no data on the SSE GET stream. The agents SDK (verified on 0.17.4) sends no keepalive on the client-facing stream — `keepAlive()` heartbeats exist only for Durable Object alarms (dist/index.js: "Keep the Durable Object alive via alarm heartbeats"), not for the response stream.

## Measured impact (single user, 4 workers on *.mcp-hub.stream, one day)

- ~1,500 `SSE stream disconnected: TypeError: The socket connection was closed unexpectedly` warnings/day across 4 MCP servers (Playwright 670, WortWert 690, Rille 114, Memex 102)
- No functional loss (opencode's StreamableHTTP client reconnects automatically), but: reconnect latency on the first tool call after idle, heavy client log growth, and the known ecosystem risk of transports sticking after repeated idle disconnects
- Cloudflare proxy read timeout is 100 s on Free/Pro/Business (Enterprise-only configurable), so any idle SSE GET over the proxy hits this

## Request

Emit an SSE comment ping (`: ping\n\n`) every ~30 s on the open GET stream of the Streamable HTTP transport (ideally as an option, e.g. `keepaliveIntervalMs`). This would keep idle client connections alive behind the proxy without changing MCP semantics — SSE comments are ignored by all compliant clients.

Happy to provide further logs/metrics if useful. Thanks for the SDK — apart from this it removed a whole class of SSE-framing bugs for us.

issue.title: `--metadata` values containing a comma get split into extra keys or rejected
issue.body:
Hi everyone, hope you're doing well!

Thanks for all the work on link-cli, and thanks @kreese-stripe for the repeatable `--metadata` flag in #219, it's a really nice way to tag agent spend requests with order ids and notes. I noticed one small thing with commas while reading through the parser and wanted to ask how you'd like it handled.

**Summary:** a `--metadata` value containing a comma is either silently split into extra keys or rejected, even though each flag is documented as a single `key:value` pair.

**What the code is for:** `--metadata` attaches arbitrary string data to a spend request, one `key:value` pair per flag, repeatable (`spend-request/schema.ts` L134 to L139, README "Metadata" section, value up to 500 chars). Each flag string goes through `parseKvString` (`utils/line-item-parser.ts` L25 to L35) and the results are merged with `Object.assign` (`spend-request/index.tsx` L276 to L285).

**Current behavior:**
1. Pass `--metadata "note:ship to 5th ave, apt:4B"`
2. `parseKvString` splits the whole string on `,` first (L27), then splits each piece at the first `:`
3. The request goes out with `"metadata":{"note":"ship to 5th ave","apt":"4B"}`, with no warning
4. With `--metadata "note:hello, world"`, the second piece has no `:`, so the command fails with `Error: Invalid field (missing ':'):  world`

**Expected behavior:** each `--metadata` flag is one pair, split at the first `:`, and the value is kept whole, commas included: `{"note":"ship to 5th ave, apt:4B"}` and `{"note":"hello, world"}`.

**Minimal repro** (built CLI on fa6d4c1, fake `LINK_ACCESS_TOKEN`, `LINK_API_BASE_URL` pointed at a tiny local server that just logs the request body):

```sh
export LINK_ACCESS_TOKEN=fake LINK_API_BASE_URL=http://localhost:4999
CTX="Buying a pair of running shoes for the user from the example store, as requested in chat, within the agreed budget."

node packages/cli/dist/cli.js spend-request create --payment-method-id csmrpd_test --merchant-name "Example Store" --merchant-url https://example.com --amount 5000 --context "$CTX" --no-request-approval --format json --metadata "note:ship to 5th ave, apt:4B"
# body sent: "metadata":{"note":"ship to 5th ave","apt":"4B"}

node packages/cli/dist/cli.js spend-request create --payment-method-id csmrpd_test --merchant-name "Example Store" --merchant-url https://example.com --amount 5000 --context "$CTX" --no-request-approval --format json --metadata "note:hello, world"
# "message": "Invalid field (missing ':'):  world"  (no request sent)

node packages/cli/dist/cli.js spend-request create --payment-method-id csmrpd_test --merchant-name "Example Store" --merchant-url https://example.com --amount 5000 --context "$CTX" --no-request-approval --format json --metadata "note:hello world"
# body sent: "metadata":{"note":"hello world"}
```

The same parser is used by `--line-item`, `--total` and UCP `--buyer` (`ucp/checkout-input.ts` L27 to L49), where the comma is the documented field separator, so I think that's a softer case. Still, there's no way to pass a value like `name:Shoes, red`, `display_text:Total, incl. tax` or `last_name:Smith, Jr.` from the CLI today, while MCP object input handles them fine. I also noticed `__tests__/line-item-parser.test.ts` doesn't cover commas in values yet.

For `--metadata`, I'd default to splitting once at the first `:` so it matches the docs. Does that sound right to you, or is anyone relying on packing several pairs into one flag with commas?

For the other flags, would you rather accept a JSON object string (like `--approval-detail` already does), support a `\,` escape, or leave them as they are? I'd be glad to put up a PR for whichever you prefer, and any tips or feedback on the approach are very welcome.

issue.title: [BUG] @mastra/upstash: $not, $nor and $and/$or keep only the first key of a condition

issue.body:
### Describe the Bug

Hey Mastra team, hope you're all doing well! This is my first issue here, so any tips on how you like issues filed are very welcome. In the Upstash vector store, a `$not`, `$nor`, `$and` or `$or` condition with more than one key silently keeps only the first key. I saw how nicely #25353 (thanks @Bdysj, and @abhiaiyer91 for merging) fixed the same pattern for pg and libsql, and I think Upstash still has it.

`UpstashFilterTranslator` turns Mastra filters into Upstash filter strings for `query`, `updateVector` and `deleteVectors`. In `stores/upstash/src/vector/filter.ts`, `Object.entries(...)[0]` keeps just the first entry at lines 148 and 152 (field `$not`), 169 (operator `$not`) and 190 (each `$and`/`$or` element, which `$nor` reuses via line 117). The core type allows these filters (`$not: OperatorCondition` in `packages/core/src/vector/filter/base.ts:56`).

The result can be wrong in either direction, too wide or too narrow. Because `deleteVectors` and `updateVector` take filters (`index.ts:124,330,479`), the wrong rows can be deleted.

### Steps To Reproduce

1. In `stores/upstash/src/vector` on main, create `new UpstashFilterTranslator()` from `./filter` (it isn't exported from the package root).
2. Translate `{ price: { $not: { $gte: 10, $lte: 20 } } }`.
3. You get `price < 10`, so rows with price above 20 are missed.
4. Translate `{ $not: { a: 1, b: 2 } }` and you get `a != 1`.
5. Translate `{ $nor: [{ a: 1, b: 2 }] }` and you get `(a != 1)`.

```ts
import { UpstashFilterTranslator } from './filter';
const t = new UpstashFilterTranslator();
t.translate({ price: { $not: { $gte: 10, $lte: 20 } } }); // "price < 10"
t.translate({ $not: { a: 1, b: 2 } });                    // "a != 1"
t.translate({ $nor: [{ a: 1, b: 2 }] });                  // "(a != 1)"
t.translate({ price: { $not: { $gte: 10 } } });           // "price < 10" (correct)
t.translate({ price: { $gte: 10, $lte: 20 } });           // "(price >= 10 AND price <= 20)" (correct)
```

### Link to Minimal Reproducible Example

https://gist.github.com/abhiramshaji-cyber/9d69d9b1797946b589f161c3f713dc4a

### Expected Behavior

Every entry is used, like libsql does (`sql-builder.ts:486-504,522-530`):
- `(price < 10 OR price > 20)`
- `(a != 1 OR b != 2)`
- `(a != 1 OR b != 2)`

Would you be happy with negating each entry and joining them with OR, to match libsql? Or would you rather keep the `$not` wrapper as is? I know outside PRs are paused right now, so I'm happy to share a branch with the fix and tests for these cases (the current ones in `filter.test.ts` only cover single keys) if that would help.

### Environment Information

```shell
@mastra/upstash 1.6.0 (main @ 36bbc29)
Node v24.13.0, macOS
LLM Provider: n/a (filter translation only)
```

### Verification

- [x] I have searched the existing issues to make sure this is not a duplicate
- [x] I have included sufficient information for the team to reproduce and understand the issue

issue.title: [inference] custom fetch isn't used for queue polling and result downloads
fix(langgraph): don't rerun a finished error handler on resume
issue.body:
Resuming a paused run no longer calls a node's error handler a second time when that handler already finished before the pause.

**What this code is for**

`_resumeErrorHandlersIfApplicable` in `libs/langgraph-core/src/pregel/loop.ts` runs at the start of a resumed step. It looks through `checkpointPendingWrites` for tasks that saved both `ERROR` and `ERROR_SOURCE_NODE`, marks each one done, and calls `scheduleErrorHandler` to put its handler task back into `this.tasks`. The runner then runs every task whose `writes` array is empty.

**Before this PR**

The graph from #3175: `work` throws and has an `errorHandler` that returns `Command({ update: { done: true }, goto: "after" })`, and `ask` runs next to it and calls `interrupt()`.

1. First `invoke`: `work` throws, the runner saves `ERROR` and `ERROR_SOURCE_NODE` for it, and its handler task runs in the same step. `handled` is 1.
2. The handler's writes (`done` and the `goto` to `after`) are saved under the handler task id. `ask` interrupts, so the step stops there.
3. Second `invoke` with `new Command({ resume: 7 })`. `_reapplyWritesToSucceededNodes(this.tasks)` hands saved writes back to the tasks in `this.tasks`, but the handler task is not in there yet.
4. `_resumeErrorHandlersIfApplicable` calls `scheduleErrorHandler`, which builds the handler task again with the same id and empty `writes`.
5. The runner sees empty `writes` and calls the handler again. `handled` is 2.

**After this PR**

Same as above through step 4.

5. Right after `scheduleErrorHandler` returns the handler task, `_resumeErrorHandlersIfApplicable` passes it to `_reapplyWritesToSucceededNodes`, which copies its saved writes onto it (leaving out `ERROR`, `ERROR_SOURCE_NODE`, `INTERRUPT` and `RESUME`) and adds it to `_reappliedTaskIds`.
6. The handler task now has writes, so the runner skips it and only `ask` runs. `handled` stays 1, and the final state is still `{ answer: 7, done: true }`.

**The diagram**

```mermaid
flowchart LR

classDef box fill:#eef1ff,stroke:#4c5bd4,color:#111827
classDef bad fill:#ffd6d6,stroke:#cc0000,color:#111827,stroke-width:3px
classDef good fill:#c8f0c8,stroke:#008800,color:#111827,stroke-width:3px

subgraph BEFORE["BEFORE: handler runs 2 times"]
direction TB
  B1["invoke: work throws, ask interrupts"] --> B2["errorHandler runs, its writes are saved"]
  B2 --> B3["invoke with Command resume 7"]
  B3 --> B4["scheduleErrorHandler builds the handler task"]
  B4 --> B5{"handler task writes are empty"}
  B5 -->|"saved writes never read"| B6["runner calls errorHandler again"]
end

subgraph AFTER["AFTER: handler runs 1 time"]
direction TB
  A1["invoke: work throws, ask interrupts"] --> A2["errorHandler runs, its writes are saved"]
  A2 --> A3["invoke with Command resume 7"]
  A3 --> A4["scheduleErrorHandler builds the handler task"]
  A4 --> A5{"THE CHANGE: _reapplyWritesToSucceededNodes"}
  A5 -->|"handler finished, writes found"| A6["runner skips it, only ask runs"]
  A5 -->|"handler interrupted or never ran"| A7["runner runs the handler as before"]
end

B1 ~~~ A1

class B1,B2,B3,B4 box
class A1,A2,A3,A4,A7 box
class B5,B6 bad
class A5,A6 good

linkStyle 4 stroke:#cc0000,stroke-width:5px
linkStyle 9 stroke:#008800,stroke-width:5px

style BEFORE fill:#fff5f5,stroke:#cc0000,color:#111827
style AFTER fill:#f3fff3,stroke:#008800,color:#111827
```

**The change**

`_resumeErrorHandlersIfApplicable` keeps the task that `scheduleErrorHandler` returns and calls `this._reapplyWritesToSucceededNodes({ [handlerTask.id]: handlerTask })` on it. That is the whole fix. It reuses the function finished nodes already go through, so the handler task also lands in `_reappliedTaskIds`, which the end of the step uses to tell writes that were handed back from writes of a task that runs again.

The handler task id comes from `_prepareNodeErrorHandlerTask` and is built from the checkpoint id and the failed task id, so the rebuilt task has the same id its writes were saved under.

New cases in `node_error_handler.test.ts`: the #3175 graph plus a second failing node whose handler returns `{}`, run under `sync`, `async` and `exit` durability (fails on main with both handlers at 2 runs), and a handler that itself calls `interrupt()`, which still runs again on resume.

Python has the same gap in `_resume_error_handlers_if_applicable` (langchain-ai/langgraph#9002). langchain-ai/langgraph#9034 took this same approach there but was closed while waiting on assignment, so Python would need the matching change.

**What changes for a user**

- A handler that finished before a sibling's interrupt runs once, and its update and `goto` still apply after the resume.
- A handler that wrote nothing has its saved `__no_writes__` marker handed back, so it is skipped too.
- A handler that called `interrupt()` itself still runs again on resume and gets the resume value, as before.
- A handler that never ran (for example stopped by `interruptBefore`) has nothing saved and runs on resume, as before.
- Several failed nodes in one step each get their own handler task and are handled separately.

I'd love a second opinion on placement: would you rather this live in `_resumeErrorHandlersIfApplicable` like here, or should the runner skip a handler whose writes are already saved? Happy to move it.

Fixes #3175

comment.body: Hi team, hope you're all doing well, and it's me again! I had a lot of fun digging into how error handlers get scheduled again on resume for this one. If anyone has tips on whether reusing `_reapplyWritesToSucceededNodes` for the handler task fits how you'd like the loop to work, or if there's a cleaner spot for it, I'd really love to hear your thoughts.

issue.title: unassign-inactive-assignees never detects linked PRs, so assignees with open PRs get unassigned

labels.name: user-c64ca2e7/repo-78cd3e02
labels.description: Issues that need to be triaged by the triage automation.

labels.name: user-3ef72433/repo-27383830
labels.description: Issues related to Build infra, Release mgmt, Testing, Eval infra, Capacity, Quota mgmt

issue.body:
### What happened?

It looks like `unassign-inactive-assignees` never recognizes a linked PR, so contributors with an open, ready PR are getting unassigned after 7 days anyway.

First, thank you for all the work getting this workflow running again (#29298, #29326, #29609, #29770). It's been running cleanly since Oct 17, which is how I noticed this.

**What the workflow is for:** per the [file header](https://github.com/google-gemini/gemini-cli/blob/6814e00d6b148c3a1d57244d5d7040f7c541009d/.github/workflows/unassign-inactive-assignees.yml#L3-L10), it frees up "help wanted" issues whose assignee has no non draft PR (open and ready, or merged) linked within 7 days.

**Current behavior:**

1. The workflow loads the issue timeline and looks at `cross-referenced` events.
2. [Line 184](https://github.com/google-gemini/gemini-cli/blob/6814e00d6b148c3a1d57244d5d7040f7c541009d/.github/workflows/unassign-inactive-assignees.yml#L180-L189) skips any event where `event.source.type !== 'pull_request'`.
3. As far as I can tell, the REST timeline API reports cross referenced PRs as `source.type: "issue"`, with `source.issue.pull_request` set instead.
4. So every event is skipped, and the [readiness check](https://github.com/google-gemini/gemini-cli/blob/6814e00d6b148c3a1d57244d5d7040f7c541009d/.github/workflows/unassign-inactive-assignees.yml#L201-L216) (`pulls.get`, then `isReady`) never runs.
5. `linkedPRAuthorSet` stays empty, and every non privileged assignee past 7 days is removed, even with an open, ready PR that closes the issue.

**Minimal repro:**

```sh
gh api repos/google-gemini/gemini-cli/issues/28052/timeline --paginate \
  --jq '.[]|select(.event=="cross-referenced")|{t:.source.type, pr:(.source.issue.pull_request!=null), n:.source.issue.number}'
```

Every PR (28054, 28069, 28200, ...) comes back as `"t": "issue", "pr": true`.

The run logs seem to agree: the `PR ... state=` line never prints in runs 41291334509, 41186944793, 41030516312, 40478041559 or 39019643178. A couple of examples:

- Run 41030516312 (Oct 30) unassigned the assignee on #22589, while #29859 (open, not a draft, closes #22589) had been open since Oct 21.
- Run 39019643178 (Oct 17) unassigned people on #27400, #22590, #27406, #19638 and #29546, which all had open non draft PRs.

Where the PR check stops today:

```mermaid
flowchart TD
  A[cross-referenced event] --> B{source.type === 'pull_request'?}
  B -- "no (API sends 'issue')" --> X[skip event]
  B -- yes --> C[pulls.get]
  C --> D{isReady?}
  D -- yes --> E[keep assignee]
  D -- no --> F[may unassign]
  X --> F
```

**Suggested fix (one line):**

```diff
-                  event.source.type !== 'pull_request' ||
+                  !event.source.issue?.pull_request ||
```

I also noticed #28798 was closed on Oct 28 on the idea that open PRs keep assignments indefinitely. From the logs it seems to be the reverse right now, so it might be worth a second look once this is sorted.

### What did you expect to happen?

An assignee with an open, non draft PR linked to the issue (or a merged one) should stay assigned, as the file header describes. The `PR ... state=` log line should show up for each linked PR.

### Client information

<details>
<summary>Client Information</summary>

Not applicable, this is the `.github/workflows/unassign-inactive-assignees.yml` GitHub Actions workflow on `main` (6814e00).

</details>

### Login information

Not applicable.

### Anything else we need to know?

One question I wasn't sure about: which policy would you prefer here? The smallest fix above counts any cross referencing non draft PR. A stricter option would be to only count PRs that actually close the issue (`closingIssuesReferences` via GraphQL), so a passing mention can't keep an assignment alive. Happy to open a PR for whichever you think fits best, and of course I may be missing some context.

comment.body: Hi maintainers, hope you're doing well! I know the triage queue is busy right now, so no rush at all. Would a small reproduction or any more detail from the timelines help here? Whenever someone gets a chance, it'd be great to know whether @ANUBprad is good to go ahead, and whether any linked non draft PR should count or only ones that close the issue.

Thanks for looking closely! I checked this locally: vitest 5 clears mock history before every test by default (`clearMocks: true`), so `manual.execute` starts each V1 test with no calls and the file passes as is. I left it unchanged.

issue.title: fix(pki): use the CA certificate subject as the CRL issuer
issue.body:
## Context

Thanks a lot for the really detailed report and repro in #9224, it made this easy to track down.

**Before:** the CRL issuer was built from the DN string we store when the CA is created (`internalCa.dn`). For an intermediate CA signed outside Infisical, the imported certificate can carry the same attributes in a different order, or extra ones, and import still passes because each configured field is checked on its own. So the CRL issuer and the CA certificate subject end up as different names, and OpenSSL, Windows and friends reject the CRL.

**After:** when the CA has an active certificate, the CRL issuer is the subject `Name` taken straight from that certificate, so the encoding and order match byte for byte (the same way issued certificates already use `caCertObj.subject`). The stored DN is only used when there is no certificate yet, which is the empty CRL made at CA creation. Importing a certificate now also signs a new CRL right away, with the imported certificate's subject as the issuer, so the CRL served after import already has the right issuer instead of waiting for a revocation or the daily job. The import passes the certificate it just parsed (`activeCaCert: certObj`) instead of reading the CA back from the database, so a read replica that has not caught up yet cannot hand back the old issuer. The CRL is signed before the database transaction and saved inside it, together with the new certificate, so if HSM or KMS signing fails the import fails with nothing saved.

```mermaid
flowchart LR
  I[import CA cert] --> J[use the imported cert's subject Name]
  J --> K[sign CRL before the transaction]
  K --> L[save cert and CRL in one transaction]
  A[revoke or daily job] --> B{CA has an active cert?}
  B -- yes --> C[decrypt cert, use its subject Name]
  B -- no --> D[use stored DN]
  C --> E[sign and save CRL]
  D --> E
```

Changes:
- `getCaCrlIssuer` in `certificate-authority-fns.ts`, used by `rebuildCaCrl` and the daily CRL job in `certificate-authority-queue.ts`
- `buildCaCrl` in `certificate-authority-fns.ts` signs and encrypts the CRL and returns it; `rebuildCaCrl` calls it and saves the result. It takes an optional `activeCaCert`, and when given uses that certificate's subject as the issuer
- `importCertToCa` calls `buildCaCrl` with the imported certificate before the transaction, and saves the CRL in the same transaction that sets `activeCaCertId`
- unit tests for a reordered subject with an extra RDN, the no certificate fallback, a missing certificate record, and a CA read that still shows no active certificate
- service tests for `importCertToCa`: the signed CRL issuer matches the imported subject byte for byte when it differs from the stored DN, a signing failure writes nothing, and the CRL is saved in the same transaction as the certificate

One thing I'd love your opinion on: if `activeCaCertId` points at a row that no longer exists, I throw `NotFoundError` rather than quietly falling back to the stored DN, since a CRL with the wrong issuer fails validation anyway. Happy to switch it to a fallback if you prefer that.

Fixes #9224

## Screenshots

Not applicable, backend only.

## Steps to verify the change

1. Create an intermediate CA with DN `C=US, O=Example, CN=Example Intermediate`.
2. Sign its CSR outside Infisical with the subject in a different order (for example `CN=Example Intermediate, OU=PKI, O=Example, C=US`) and import it.
3. Download the CRL and run `openssl crl -in crl.pem -noout -issuer`; it now matches `openssl x509 -in ca.pem -noout -subject`.
4. Issue a leaf, revoke it, and run `openssl verify -crl_check -CAfile chain.pem -CRLfile crl.pem leaf.pem`; it reports the cert as revoked instead of failing on the CRL.
5. `npx vitest run -c vitest.unit.config.mts src/services/certificate-authority`

## Type

- [x] Fix
- [ ] Feature
- [ ] Improvement
- [ ] Breaking
- [ ] Docs
- [ ] Chore

## Checklist

- [x] Title follows the [conventional commit](https://www.conventionalcommits.org/en/v1.0.0/#summary) format: `type(scope): short description` (scope is optional, e.g., `fix: prevent crash on sync` or `fix(api): handle null response`). 
- [x] Tested locally
- [ ] Updated docs (if needed)
- [ ] Updated AGENTS.md files (if needed)
- [x] Read the [contributing guide](https://infisical.com/docs/contributing/getting-started/overview)

comment.body: Thanks so much @carlosmonastyrski for fixing this in #9234! It covers the same issuer change, including the daily rotation job and import, so I'll close this one in favor of it. If anything else around CRLs would be useful, I'd be glad to help.

issue.title: fix(sdk): ignore child values snapshots in nested messages and values projections
issue.body:
When a subagent starts its own subagent, the parent's messages and state no longer get replaced by the child's while the child runs.

Thank you @okisdev for the very clear write up and reproduction in #2859, it made this easy to follow.

**What this code is for**

`messagesProjection(namespace)` and `valuesProjection(namespace)` in `libs/sdk/src/stream/projections/` keep a store for one namespace, so `useMessages(stream, subagent)` and `useValues(stream, subagent)` can show one subagent's own messages and state. For a namespace other than the root, each one calls `openProjectionSubscription`, which subscribes with `depth = 1` unless told otherwise.

**Before this PR**

A user watches a subagent at `["tools:parent"]` in a React app, and that subagent calls the `task` tool to start its own subagent.

1. `useMessages(stream, subagent)` opens `messagesProjection(["tools:parent"])`, which subscribes with `{ namespaces: [["tools:parent"]], depth: 1 }`.
2. The subagent's tools node runs at `["tools:parent", "tools:<id>"]`, and the child subagent's graph runs inside it, so the child's `values` snapshots are sent at that namespace.
3. That is one segment below `["tools:parent"]`, so `matchesSubscription` lets them through.
4. The nested `onEvent` only checks `event.method`, so the child's `values` event goes to `applyValuesEvent`.
5. `reconcileMessagesFromValues` treats that snapshot as the full list and drops every parent message.
6. The parent's messages vanish for the whole child run and come back on the parent's next `values` event. `valuesProjection` replaces the parent's state with the child's in the same way.

**After this PR**

Same user, same subagents.

1. Same as above through step 3. The subscription keeps depth 1, because the subagent's own model tokens arrive one segment below, at `["tools:parent", "model_request:<id>"]`, and its own tool results at `["tools:parent", "tools:<id>"]`.
2. `onEvent` skips a `values` event whose namespace is longer than `["tools:parent"]`, so the child's snapshot is ignored.
3. `messages` events are applied as before, so the subagent's own tokens and tool results still stream live.
4. `valuesProjection` subscribes with `depth: 0`, since it only reads `values`, so the child's snapshot never reaches it.
5. The parent's messages and state stay on screen for the whole child run.

**The diagram**

```mermaid
flowchart LR

classDef box fill:#eef1ff,stroke:#4c5bd4,color:#111827
classDef bad fill:#ffd6d6,stroke:#cc0000,color:#111827,stroke-width:3px
classDef good fill:#c8f0c8,stroke:#008800,color:#111827,stroke-width:3px

subgraph BEFORE["BEFORE: child values replace parent messages"]
direction TB
  B1["useMessages for tools:parent"] --> B2["subscribe with depth 1"]
  B2 --> B3["event one segment below"]
  B3 --> B4{"onEvent checks method only"}
  B4 -->|"child values applied"| B5["store rebuilt from child values"]
  B4 -->|"own messages"| B6["streamed live"]
end

subgraph AFTER["AFTER: parent messages stay"]
direction TB
  A1["useMessages for tools:parent"] --> A2["subscribe with depth 1"]
  A2 --> A3["event one segment below"]
  A3 --> A4{"THE CHANGE: values must be at tools:parent"}
  A4 -->|"child values"| A5["skipped"]
  A4 -->|"own messages"| A6["still streamed live"]
end

B1 ~~~ A1

class B1,B2,B3,B6 box
class A1,A2,A3,A6 box
class B4,B5 bad
class A4,A5 good

linkStyle 3 stroke:#cc0000,stroke-width:5px
linkStyle 8 stroke:#008800,stroke-width:5px

style BEFORE fill:#fff5f5,stroke:#cc0000,color:#111827
style AFTER fill:#f3fff3,stroke:#008800,color:#111827
```

**The change**

- `messagesProjection`, nested path: `if (event.params.namespace.length > ns.length) return;` before `applyValuesEvent`. This is the fix for the case in the issue.
- `valuesProjection`, nested path: `depth: 0` passed to `openProjectionSubscription`. Same fix for scoped state.

A graph always sends `values` at its own namespace, so nothing below it is ever the projection's own state. The prefix is already checked by `matchesSubscription`, so comparing lengths is enough, and a namespace given by name only (for example `["fetcher"]` matching `["fetcher:abc"]`) keeps working.

I left the `messages` channel, the media projections, `toolCallsProjection`, `channelProjection` and `extensionProjection` as they are. With the namespaces `langgraph-core` sends through `streamEvents` v3 (the path this repo's server uses), a child subagent's tokens, media and tool events land two segments below the parent, so depth 1 already keeps them out, and what arrives one segment below is the subagent's own output.

Tests: the scoped thread mock in `messages.test.ts` and the one in the new `values.test.ts` now filter with the real `matchesSubscription` and the params the projection sent. Each test runs for a first level and a second level namespace. The messages test pushes the child's snapshot at `[...ns, "tools:call"]`, a child token two segments down, the subagent's own model token at `[...ns, "model_request:x"]` and its own tool result at `[...ns, "tools:call"]`, and expects only the last two to be added. On `main` the store ends as `["c1", "p3", "p4"]` instead of `["p1", "p2", "p3", "p4"]`, and the values store passes through `"child"`. Both pass with this change. The full `@langchain/langgraph-sdk` suite and the `@langchain/react` browser suite pass, and `tsc`, `oxlint` and `oxfmt` are clean.

**What changes for a user**

- `useMessages(stream, subagent)` keeps showing the subagent's own messages while one of its own subagents runs.
- `useValues(stream, subagent)` keeps showing the subagent's own state instead of switching to the child's.
- The subagent's own tokens, tool results and media still stream live, exactly as before.
- Root projections, tool calls, raw channel logs and extension values are unchanged.

One question for the maintainers: the issue also mentions child `messages` events reaching the parent. Under `streamEvents` v3 a child's tokens sit two segments down, so depth 1 already drops them and I left `messages` alone. Since #3121, though, `graph.stream()` sends `messages` at the graph's namespace, and the Python server may do the same. On those paths a child's tokens would land one segment below the parent and still reach it. If those paths matter here, I could also skip `messages` whose extra segments are `tools:*` or `task:*` (the rule the root `stream.messages` uses), at the cost of the subagent's own tool results no longer streaming live under v3. Which would you prefer?

Fixes #2859

comment.body: Hi team, hope you're all doing well! I know there's a lot landing in the SDK right now, so no rush at all on this one. If it would help, I'm happy to also add the `tools:*` / `task:*` filter for `messages` from the question above, or change anything else about how the nested projections handle child snapshots.
