issue.title: RestApiTool sends null header and cookie params as "null" and objects as [object Object]

labels.name: repo-03a26658
labels.description: Something isn't working

labels.name: repo-03a26658
labels.description: [Status] The PR/issue is awaiting review from the maintainer

issue.body:
**Describe the bug**
`prepareRequestParams` in `RestApiTool` turns `null` header and cookie args into the literal string `"null"`, and object or array values in path, header and cookie params into `[object Object]` or a lossy comma string.

`RestApiTool` is what `OpenAPIToolset` builds for each operation in a spec: the model fills in the params, and `prepareRequestParams` (core/src/tools/openapi_tool/rest_api_tool.ts) maps them onto the URL, query, headers, cookies and body before the request goes out.

Query params already handle this nicely (thanks to #1135): `null`, `undefined` and `''` are skipped and objects are JSON encoded. Path (~L343), header (~L355) and cookie (~L357) just use `String(argValue)`.

**To Reproduce**
1. Have an operation with a path param `id`, header params `X-Tenant` and `X-Filter`, a cookie param `session`, and a query param `q`. Any of them nullable in the spec is enough, since `gemini_schema_util.ts` (~L160) tells the model `null` is allowed.
2. The model calls the tool with `{id: {kind: 'a'}, 'X-Tenant': null, 'X-Filter': {role: 'admin'}, session: null, q: null}`.
3. `runAsync` passes `request.args` straight into `prepareRequestParams`.
4. The request goes out as:
   - url: `.../items/%5Bobject%20Object%5D`
   - headers: `{"X-Tenant": "null", "X-Filter": "[object Object]"}`
   - `Cookie: session=null`
   - `q` is correctly left out

`undefined` becomes `"undefined"` the same way, and an array like `[1, null]` becomes `"1,"`.

Minimal repro:

```ts
import {prepareRequestParams} from './core/src/tools/openapi_tool/rest_api_tool.js';

const p = (name: string, paramLocation: string) =>
  ({name, originalName: name, paramLocation, paramSchema: {}, required: false});

const out = prepareRequestParams(
  {baseUrl: 'https://api.example.com', path: '/items/{id}', method: 'get'},
  [p('id', 'path'), p('X-Tenant', 'header'), p('X-Filter', 'header'), p('session', 'cookie'), p('q', 'query')],
  {id: {kind: 'a'}, 'X-Tenant': null, 'X-Filter': {role: 'admin'}, session: null, q: null},
);
console.log(out);
// url ends with /items/%5Bobject%20Object%5D
// headers: { "X-Tenant": "null", "X-Filter": "[object Object]", Cookie: "session=null" }
// no q in the query string
```

**Expected behavior**
- Header and cookie params that are `null` or `undefined` are skipped, the same way query params are.
- Arrays and objects in path, header and cookie params are serialized per OpenAPI `style: simple`, matching `adk-python`'s `_to_param_string` (rest_api_tool.py ~L92 to 117): arrays comma joined with `None` dropped, objects as `k,v` pairs, booleans as `true`/`false`. Python also skips `None` for header (~L527) and cookie (~L530).

**Desktop (please complete the following information):**
 - OS: any
 - TS version/environment: Node
 - ADK version: main at eedc561

**Additional context**
One thing I wasn't sure about: Python sends `None` into the path too (no guard there), so a `null` path param is a gap in both. Should that be handled here as well, maybe by leaving it out or raising a clear error? Would you be open to one PR covering header, cookie and path in the same style as #1135?

Also kindly pointing to @OsamaAnsar's #1208, which fixes the same kind of serialization for form bodies, so this would be its sibling for the other param locations.

Happy to open a PR for this if it sounds good to you.

comment.body: Thanks so much @OsamaAnsar, confirming it on eedc561 with the exact outputs really helps, and the `[1, null]` and `undefined` header cases are great finds. I'll make sure the tests cover both. Good call on #1208 too. I'll keep the change to the path, header and cookie branches and stay clear of the query branch, and if #1208 lands first I'm happy to rebase onto it, so no need to move yours. Would love your review once it's up! Maintainers, does one PR covering header, cookie and path sound good to you, and is skipping a `null` path param fine, or would you prefer a clear error there?

issue.title: feat(review): review each commit of a PR separately
issue.body:
With per commit review turned on by the host, `/review` reviews each commit of a PR on its own diff and commit message, instead of only the combined diff.

Closes #4470. It is opt in and host only. The commit messages piece was split out into #4603, as suggested, and that has now landed on `main`.

**What this code is for**

`PRReviewer.run()` in `pr_agent/commands/pr_reviewer.py` handles `/review`. It asks the git provider for the PR diff, renders `pr_reviewer_prompts.toml` with that diff, makes one model call (or a few when chunking), and publishes one review comment.

**Before this PR**

A maintainer on GitLab has an MR with 4 commits, each with a message that explains one change, and comments `/review`.

1. `PRReviewer.run()` asks `GitLabProvider.get_diff_files()` for the diff of the whole MR.
2. The prompt gets that combined diff, plus the title and description.
3. The model returns findings with file and line, but nothing says which commit a finding belongs to.
4. One review comment for the whole MR. The maintainer has to work out by hand which of the 4 commits needs the fixup.

**After this PR**

Same maintainer, same MR, with `per_commit_review = true` in the host config or `.pr_agent.toml`.

1. `PRReviewer.run()` sees `per_commit_review` and calls `_run_per_commit()`.
2. `get_pr_commits()` returns the 4 commits, oldest first, with their parents, read fresh from the provider on every run. Merge commits are dropped here without loading them. `_commit_review_records()` reads the commits already reviewed from hidden markers in PR-Agent's own comments. For each commit not already listed by SHA, `set_commit_review_scope()` loads its files once and returns a fingerprint of its own patch, and only commits whose fingerprint is not recorded are kept. On the first run there are no markers, so all 4 are kept.
3. For each commit, `set_commit_review_scope()` scopes the diff to that commit against its parent, and `commit_under_review` puts its message (clipped to `max_commits_tokens`) in the prompt, between random markers made fresh for each run. `commit_messages_str` is cleared, so the prompt does not also list every other commit's message.
4. `_run_review()` runs once per commit and publishes one comment that names and links the commit. It uses the incremental review header, so it never replaces the persistent full review.
5. A commit with no findings gets no comment when `pr_reviewer.publish_output_no_suggestions = false`. With `inline_key_issues = true`, findings land inline on that commit's own diff.
6. 4 comments, one per commit, each with a `<!-- pr-agent:reviewed-commit <fingerprint> <sha> -->` line two lines below the hidden `<!-- pr-agent:review:incremental -->` identity. On the next push with 1 new commit, only that commit is reviewed. Without the setting, `/review` takes exactly the old path.

**The diagram**

```mermaid
flowchart LR

classDef box fill:#eef1ff,stroke:#4c5bd4,color:#111827
classDef bad fill:#ffd6d6,stroke:#cc0000,color:#111827,stroke-width:3px
classDef good fill:#c8f0c8,stroke:#008800,color:#111827,stroke-width:3px

subgraph BEFORE["BEFORE: 1 review for 4 commits"]
direction TB
  B1["Maintainer comments /review"] --> B2["PRReviewer.run"]
  B2 --> B3["get_diff_files for the whole MR"]
  B3 --> B4{"one prompt, combined diff"}
  B4 -->|"findings not tied to a commit"| B5["1 comment for the whole MR"]
  B4 -->|"per_commit_review off"| B6["same as today"]
end

subgraph AFTER["AFTER: 1 review per commit"]
direction TB
  A1["Maintainer comments /review"] --> A2["PRReviewer.run"]
  A2 --> A3["get_pr_commits"]
  A3 --> A4{"THE CHANGE: per_commit_review on"}
  A4 -->|"each commit: own diff and message"| A5["1 comment per commit, linked"]
  A4 -->|"setting off or provider unsupported"| A6["whole PR review, as today"]
end

B1 ~~~ A1

class B1,B2,B3,B6 box
class A1,A2,A3,A6 box
class B4,B5 bad
class A4,A5 good

linkStyle 3 stroke:#cc0000,stroke-width:5px
linkStyle 8 stroke:#008800,stroke-width:5px

style BEFORE fill:#fff5f5,stroke:#cc0000,color:#111827
style AFTER fill:#f3fff3,stroke:#008800,color:#111827
```

**The change**

* `PRReviewer.run()` now branches on `per_commit_review` into `_run_per_commit()`, and the old body moved into `_run_review()` unchanged apart from the commit header and the checks below.
* `GitProvider` gets `get_pr_commits()` (returns `None` by default, so other providers fall back to a whole PR review with a notice) and `set_commit_review_scope()`. GitHub and GitLab implement both on top of the existing incremental diff path. On GitHub, new side file contents are read at the commit when a head SHA is set.
* `_run_per_commit()` reviews only commits whose fingerprint is not recorded, so a plain `/review` and the default `push_commands` no longer review every commit again on each push (454174f1, 40cb6ee2, b52fbf25, bf4dd1b6, 9b159195). `commit_patch_fingerprint()` in `git_provider.py` hashes each file's name and patch with the `@@ -a,b +c,d @@` numbers removed, so a rebase onto `main` that leaves a commit's own patch alone does not review it again, while an amend or `--autosquash` fixup does. On GitLab, when a file's diff comes back empty (collapsed, too large or binary), the commit SHA is mixed into the fingerprint so two different commits never share one; such a commit is reviewed again after a rebase. A commit is recorded only after its review succeeds, including when every file was filtered out: `_run_review()` puts the marker line two lines below the comment's hidden incremental review identity, and a commit that gets no comment (no findings with `publish_output_no_suggestions = false`) goes into one record comment that starts with `<!-- pr-agent:review:commits -->` and is edited in place through `publish_persistent_comment_full()`. With default settings and no merge commits, no record comment is created. Before writing, the record is read again and merged, trimmed to commits still in the PR, and cut from the oldest end if it would pass the 65000 character comment limit. Markers count only at those fixed lines and only in comments `is_comment_authored_by_pr_agent()` confirms. A marker in a comment confirmed as someone else's is ignored. Markers are found by that hidden identity rather than the visible heading, so changing `review_heading` never reviews commits again. When comment authorship cannot be checked for the run, or marker comments exist but none can be confirmed and the author of at least one cannot be verified (for example a GitHub App whose login cannot be resolved), the run falls back to one whole PR review with a notice instead of reviewing every commit on each push. Each commit's files are loaded once per run and reused for its review; a commit whose patch is already recorded under another SHA (a rebase) is recorded under the new SHA too, and a commit with no changes of its own is recorded, so neither is loaded again. A failed commit is not recorded, so the next run retries it; the record counts failed attempts, and automatic runs stop after `PER_COMMIT_MAX_AUTO_ATTEMPTS` (3) while a manual `/review` always retries. Selection does not use commit dates, so a commit authored before the last review but pushed after it is still reviewed. If the comments cannot be read, the run fails with the usual failure comment instead of reviewing every commit. The `-i` lookup and its `minimal_*_for_incremental_review` thresholds are not used here, so a manual `/review` never stops silently. `docs/docs/commands/review.md` says so, and also says that if PR-Agent's comments are removed, the next run reviews every commit again unless `max_commits_per_review` is set (93cb7440).
* The commit message block opens and closes with `{{ commit_message_begin }}` and `{{ commit_message_end }}` from `prompt_boundary_markers("COMMIT_MESSAGE")` (the helper #4603 added to `pr_agent/algo/artifacts.py`), so a commit message containing `<<<COMMIT_MESSAGE_END>>>` cannot close the block early. It sits right above #4603's `commit_messages_str` block, which keeps its own `COMMIT_MESSAGES` markers.
* `_should_publish_review_no_suggestions()` checks the parsed findings for a commit review, so a commit where the model returned nothing or prose stays quiet with `publish_output_no_suggestions = false`.
* `per_commit_review` and `max_commits_per_review` are in the `pr_reviewer` entry of `CLI_HOST_ONLY_KEYS_BY_SECTION` and `PER_DIRECTORY_HOST_ONLY_KEYS_BY_SECTION`, so `/review --pr_reviewer.per_commit_review=true` in a comment is rejected.
* `max_commits_per_review` defaults to 0 (no limit). When more commits than the cap are not reviewed yet, the whole PR is reviewed once with a notice, and after that review succeeds all its commits are recorded, so the next push goes back to one review per new commit. GitHub lists at most 250 commits per PR, so a PR with more is reviewed as a whole with a notice.
* Merge commits, root commits and empty commits are skipped. One failing commit does not stop the rest; the run is marked failed afterwards.
* Upstream `main` is merged in with merge commits (181edc4c, 9723af3a), not a rebase, so no history is rewritten. Conflicts: `convert_to_markdown_v2()` keeps main's `get_bot_display_name()` next to the commit header, `CLI_HOST_ONLY_KEYS_BY_SECTION` keeps main's new `pr_reviewer` keys plus ours, and the key count in `test_config_reference.py` is main's 319 plus our 2. After #4798, `run()` no longer checks `is_answer`, and the tests set `config.is_auto_command`. After #4838 renamed `pr_agent/tools` to `pr_agent/commands`, the tests import from `pr_agent.commands` and the config links point at `../commands/review.md` (ed7715a5). `_prepare_code_suggestions()` on GitHub skips `validate_comments_inside_hunks()` while a commit scope is set, so a finding outside that commit's diff stays in the commit's summary instead of moving to a nearby line. `pytest tests/unittest` on 912963d8: 17692 passed, 34 skipped. `ruff check`: clean.

**What changes for a user**

* Nothing unless the host turns on `per_commit_review`. Default `/review` is unchanged.
* With it on: one model call per reviewed commit. The first run reviews every commit, and later runs review only new commits or commits whose own changes changed, so `-i` is no longer needed in `push_commands`.
* Each commit's review sees only that commit's diff, so it can flag something a later commit fixes, or miss a helper added in an earlier commit.
* Only GitHub and GitLab support it. Other providers get the usual whole PR review with a one line notice.

comment.body: Thanks @IsmaelMartinez, that makes total sense, and thank you for spelling out what would settle it. Happy to keep this parked until after v1. When you get there, I'd be glad to run that replay of multi commit PRs (findings, false alarms, model calls) against #4603 so there's real data to compare. In the meantime, would you like me to leave this open, or close it and reopen after v1? I'll keep it open and stop merging main into it unless you'd prefer otherwise. @Hi-Angel, does that work for you too?

issue.title: execute_sql runs MERGE ... WHEN MATCHED THEN DELETE without the destructive confirmation
issue.body:
Hey folks, I think `execute_sql` lets a `MERGE ... WHEN MATCHED THEN DELETE` (or `THEN UPDATE`) run without the destructive SQL confirmation, even when it touches every row.

### What the confirmation is for

When `execute_sql` is in `confirmation.enabledTools` (opt in, and the client needs elicitation support), the server asks before running SQL it considers destructive. The prompt text in `database-operation-tools.ts:502` says it covers "DROP, DELETE, TRUNCATE or UPDATE without WHERE". A MERGE that deletes or updates every matched row seems to fit that intent pretty squarely.

### Current behavior

1. Create a table with two rows: `create table films (id int, title text); insert into films values (1, 'a'), (2, 'b');`
2. Run the server not read only, with `execute_sql` in `confirmation.enabledTools`, using a client that supports elicitation.
3. Call `execute_sql` with `merge into films f using films s on true when matched then delete`
4. No confirmation is shown (the decision is recorded as `bypass` with reason `not_destructive`).
5. Both rows are gone.

### Expected behavior

The same confirmation you get for `delete from films` should show up before the MERGE runs.

### Minimal repro

Against main at 7e5037b:

```ts
import { isDestructiveSql } from './packages/mcp-server-supabase/src/tools/destructive-sql.js';

isDestructiveSql('merge into films f using (select 1) s on true when matched then delete');                  // false
isDestructiveSql('merge into films f using films s on true when matched then delete');                       // false
isDestructiveSql('explain analyze merge into films f using films s on true when matched then delete');       // false
isDestructiveSql('merge into films f using films s on true when matched then update set title = null');      // false

isDestructiveSql('delete from films');                // true
isDestructiveSql('update films set title = null');    // true
```

From reading the code, I think this is why:

* `destructive-sql.ts:70` only flags statements that start with `drop`, `delete` or `truncate`.
* `isUpdateWithoutWhereFromScan` (`destructive-sql.ts:191` to `197`) needs the statement to start with `update`.
* The `explain analyze` recheck (`destructive-sql.ts:272` to `279`) runs those same checks on the body, so it misses MERGE too.
* `database-operation-tools.ts:78` then skips the confirmation with `not_destructive`.

```mermaid
flowchart LR
  A[execute_sql with MERGE] --> B{starts with drop, delete, truncate or update?}
  B -- no --> C[not_destructive]
  C --> D[runs with no confirmation]
```

### Related work

Huge thanks to @barryroodt for #408, which added this whole confirmation flow, and for #426, which moves the check onto a real parser. The data modifying CTE forms (`with d as (delete ... returning) select ...`, and `explain analyze` of them) are already listed as a known trade off in #408 and handled in #426, so I'm only raising MERGE here. From what I can see, `classifyStatement` in #426 doesn't have a `MergeStmt` branch yet, so MERGE would still slip through after it lands.

### Question

Would you rather have MERGE added as a small check on the current scanner, or handled as a `MergeStmt` case in #426? Totally happy either way, and I'm glad to send a PR for whichever you prefer (or leave it to Barry if it fits better in #426). Let me know if I've misread anything!

comment.body: Thank you so much for taking the time to reproduce this at that commit, @mattrossman, and for looping in @barryroodt! Keeping it in the backlog makes total sense. Barry, I'd value your view: would this case fit naturally into your parser work in #426, or would a small PR covering `MERGE ... WHEN MATCHED THEN DELETE` in the current classifier be helpful in the meantime? Either way, I'm glad to rework or close #533 to match whatever you both prefer.

```mermaid
style AFTER fill:#f3fff3,stroke:#008800,color:#111827
```

**The change**

* `PRReviewer.run()` now branches on `per_commit_review` into `_run_per_commit()`, and the old body moved into `_run_review()` unchanged apart from the commit header and the checks below.
* `GitProvider` gets `get_pr_commits()` (returns `None` by default, so other providers fall back to a whole PR review with a notice) and `set_commit_review_scope()`. GitHub and GitLab implement both on top of the existing incremental diff path. On GitHub, new side file contents are read at the commit when a head SHA is set.
* `_run_per_commit()` reviews only commits whose fingerprint is not recorded, so a plain `/review` and the default `push_commands` no longer review every commit again on each push (454174f1, 40cb6ee2, b52fbf25, bf4dd1b6, 9b159195). `commit_patch_fingerprint()` in `git_provider.py` hashes each file's name and patch with the `@@ -a,b +c,d @@` numbers removed, so a rebase onto `main` that leaves a commit's own patch alone does not review it again, while an amend or `--autosquash` fixup does. On GitLab, when a file's diff comes back empty (collapsed, too large or binary), the commit SHA is mixed into the fingerprint so two different commits never share one; such a commit is reviewed again after a rebase. A commit is recorded only after its review succeeds, including when every file was filtered out: `_run_review()` puts the marker line two lines below the comment's hidden incremental review identity, and a commit that gets no comment (no findings with `publish_output_no_suggestions = false`) goes into one record comment that starts with `<!-- pr-agent:review:commits -->` and is edited in place through `publish_persistent_comment_full()`. With default settings and no merge commits, no record comment is created. Before writing, the record is read again and merged, trimmed to commits still in the PR, and cut from the oldest end if it would pass the 65000 character comment limit. Markers count only at those fixed lines and only in comments `is_comment_authored_by_pr_agent()` confirms. A marker in a comment confirmed as someone else's is ignored. Markers are found by that hidden identity rather than the visible heading, so changing `review_heading` never reviews commits again. When comment authorship cannot be checked for the run, or marker comments exist but none can be confirmed and the author of at least one cannot be verified (for example a GitHub App whose login cannot be resolved), the run falls back to one whole PR review with a notice instead of reviewing every commit on each push. Each commit's files are loaded once per run and reused for its review; a commit whose patch is already recorded under another SHA (a rebase) is recorded under the new SHA too, and a commit with no changes of its own is recorded, so neither is loaded again. A failed commit is not recorded, so the next run retries it; the record counts failed attempts, and automatic runs stop after `PER_COMMIT_MAX_AUTO_ATTEMPTS` (3) while a manual `/review` always retries. Selection does not use commit dates, so a commit authored before the last review but pushed after it is still reviewed. If the comments cannot be read, the run fails with the usual failure comment instead of reviewing every commit. The `-i` lookup and its `minimal_*_for_incremental_review` thresholds are not used here, so a manual `/review` never stops silently. `docs/docs/commands/review.md` says so, and also says that if PR-Agent's comments are removed, the next run reviews every commit again unless `max_commits_per_review` is set (93cb7440).
* The commit message block opens and closes with `{{ commit_message_begin }}` and `{{ commit_message_end }}` from `prompt_boundary_markers("COMMIT_MESSAGE")` (the helper #4603 added to `pr_agent/algo/artifacts.py`), so a commit message containing `<<<COMMIT_MESSAGE_END>>>` cannot close the block early. It sits right above #4603's `commit_messages_str` block, which keeps its own `COMMIT_MESSAGES` markers.
* `_should_publish_review_no_suggestions()` checks the parsed findings for a commit review, so a commit where the model returned nothing or prose stays quiet with `publish_output_no_suggestions = false`.
* `per_commit_review` and `max_commits_per_review` are in the `pr_reviewer` entry of `CLI_HOST_ONLY_KEYS_BY_SECTION` and `PER_DIRECTORY_HOST_ONLY_KEYS_BY_SECTION`, so `/review --pr_reviewer.per_commit_review=true` in a comment is rejected.
* `max_commits_per_review` defaults to 0 (no limit). When more commits than the cap are not reviewed yet, the whole PR is reviewed once with a notice, and after that review succeeds all its commits are recorded, so the next push goes back to one review per new commit. GitHub lists at most 250 commits per PR, so a PR with more is reviewed as a whole with a notice.
* Merge commits, root commits and empty commits are skipped. One failing commit does not stop the rest; the run is marked failed afterwards.
* Upstream `main` is merged in with merge commits (181edc4c, 9723af3a), not a rebase, so no history is rewritten. Conflicts: `convert_to_markdown_v2()` keeps main's `get_bot_display_name()` next to the commit header, `CLI_HOST_ONLY_KEYS_BY_SECTION` keeps main's new `pr_reviewer` keys plus ours, and the key count in `test_config_reference.py` is main's 319 plus our 2. After #4798, `run()` no longer checks `is_answer`, and the tests set `config.is_auto_command`. After #4838 renamed `pr_agent/tools` to `pr_agent/commands`, the tests import from `pr_agent.commands` and the config links point at `../commands/review.md` (ed7715a5). `_prepare_code_suggestions()` on GitHub skips `validate_comments_inside_hunks()` while a commit scope is set, so a finding outside that commit's diff stays in the commit's summary instead of moving to a nearby line. `pytest tests/unittest` on 912963d8: 17692 passed, 34 skipped. `ruff check`: clean.

**What changes for a user**

* Nothing unless the host turns on `per_commit_review`. Default `/review` is unchanged.
* With it on: one model call per reviewed commit. The first run reviews every commit, and later runs review only new commits or commits whose own changes changed, so `-i` is no longer needed in `push_commands`.
* Each commit's review sees only that commit's diff, so it can flag something a later commit fixes, or miss a helper added in an earlier commit.
* Only GitHub and GitLab support it. Other providers get the usual whole PR review with a one line notice.

comment.body: While waiting I found and fixed a few edge cases in 7871e827: per commit reviews no longer see findings from earlier whole PR reviews, commit fetch errors now go through the normal failure path, and `/review -i` with nothing new says so. I also added a line to the docs (83a8240e) noting that the `--json-output` file and the Action `review` output describe the last reviewed commit. No rush at all on the bigger question.

issue.title: fix: Let Agent v3 run the legacy HTTP Request Tool and Call n8n Workflow Tool v1

labels.name: repo-361234ab
labels.description: Authored by a community member

labels.name: repo-361234ab
labels.description: Triage has been completed and issue is ready for internal teams

issue.body: ## Summary Agent v3 sends every tool call through the execution engine, which runs the tool node's `execute()`. #19997 added `execute()` to the AI tool nodes, but the legacy HTTP Request Tool (`toolHttpRequest`) and the Call n8n Workflow Tool v1 (versions 1 to 1.3) only have `supplyData()`. So the engine throws `has a "supplyData" method but no "execute" method` and the agent gets that error back instead of a result. This PR gives both nodes an `execute()`, using the same pattern as the Code Tool. The tool building moves into a `getTool(ctx, itemIndex, log)` function, and `execute()` invokes the tool once per input item and returns the result with `pairedItem`. When the engine runs the node, the tool skips `addInputData`, `addOutputData` and `logAiEvent` (the engine already records the run) and throws on errors, so the engine's continue on fail default for AI tools hands the error to the agent. Before: Agent v3.1 calls the tool, the engine throws, and the model sees `[{"error":"The node ... has a \"supplyData\" method but no \"execute\" method."}]`. After: the engine runs the tool, and the model sees the HTTP response or the child workflow's output. ```mermaid flowchart LR A[Agent v3] -->|tool call| E[Engine] E -->|before| X[throw: no execute] E -->|after| T["execute()"] --> G["getTool(log = false).invoke(item.json)"] G --> R["{ json, pairedItem }"] --> A ``` A few details: - HTTP Request Tool: the item is `{ response }`, the same shape the node already logs. HTTP failures and binary bodies still come back as readable error text, as they do today, so the model can react to them. Invalid model input throws. When the model input can't be parsed, the request is no longer sent at all, on both paths. Before, it still went out with the placeholders unfilled and the credentials attached. On `supplyData` the model now always gets `Input provided by model is not valid` for such input, instead of the error from the request that went out. An empty input on 1.0 is now validated too, so a required placeholder that is missing stops the request. When the tool fails, also while it is being built, the error carries the index of the failing item. - Call n8n Workflow Tool v1: the item is the child workflow's JSON (strings and other non object values are wrapped as `{ response }`), which matches what V2 returns from the engine. The child execution is linked with `setMetadata`, like V2 does. `execute()` follows the Code Tool's `execute()`: it calls `tool.invoke` and lets the tool's own Zod schema strip or validate the keys. Unlike the Code Tool, it first drops `toolCallId` from the engine item, because it isn't tool input and an open schema would pass it to the child workflow as data. The engine item also carries the agent input, and the node can't tell those keys from the model arguments. So two limits remain, the same as for V2 and the Code Tool: an open or record style schema (no properties, or `additionalProperties` true) passes the agent input fields to the child workflow too, and a schema that limits extra keys without declaring properties (for example only `patternProperties` or a typed `additionalProperties`) may reject them. The engine could fix this for V1, V2 and the Code Tool together by passing `action.input` separately through the task metadata, so each node gets the model's exact arguments. When the child workflow fails, or the tool can't be built (for example an invalid input schema), the error carries the index of the failing item, as in V2. - One small change I should mention for the Call n8n Workflow Tool v1 on the `supplyData` path: a child output that parses to something other than an object (a number or an array) is now logged as `{ response }` instead of the raw parsed value. The string the model receives is the same as before. - Apart from the changes above (the HTTP Request Tool no longer sends a request when the model input can't be parsed, an empty input on 1.0 is validated, and the Call n8n Workflow Tool v1 logs a non object child output as `{ response }`), the agent path through `supplyData` does not change. - One limit I want to flag, not changed here: the engine merges the agent input item into each tool item, so an optional key the model leaves out can be filled from the agent item, and an agent item key with the same name but a different type can make validation fail. This also affects the HTTP Request Tool 1.1 and the V2 and Code tools. ## Why Anyone with one of these nodes attached to Agent v3 or v3.1 can't use the tool at all. Thank you @kemrec for the clear repro, and @ardaerturk for confirming that `n8n-nodes-base.httpRequestTool` works as a replacement in the meantime. One question: I see the HTTP Request Tool is hidden and on the 3.x removal list (`removed-nodes-with-replacements.rule.ts`). Would you like both nodes fixed here, or only the Call n8n Workflow Tool v1? The changes are in two separate commits, so it's easy to drop the HTTP part if you'd prefer people move to the replacement node instead. ## How to test 1. Build a workflow: Manual Trigger, AI Agent 3.1, any chat model, and a legacy HTTP Request Tool (or a Call n8n Workflow Tool at version 1.3) connected as a tool. 2. Ask something that makes the agent call the tool. 3. Before this change the tool run fails with the "no execute method" error. After it, the response reaches the model. Tests: - `nodes/agents/Agent/test/integration/agent-v3.workflow.test.ts`: new case that runs Agent 3.1 with the legacy HTTP Request Tool through the real engine and checks that the HTTP response reaches the second model call. It runs for both 1.1 and 1.0, and fails on master with the exact error from the issue. - `ToolHttpRequest/test/ToolHttpRequest.execute.test.ts`: several items, pairing, no manual logging, HTTP error and binary responses, valid model input on 1.0 sent as `GET /users/42`, only the model arguments sent from the engine item on 1.0 and 1.1, invalid input on 1 and 1.1, that invalid input never sends the request, and the item index when the tool can't be built for the second item. `ToolHttpRequest.node.test.ts` checks the same on the `supplyData` path. - `ToolWorkflow.node.test.ts`: V1 `execute` with several items, subexecution metadata, the engine item without `toolCallId` for an object schema (agent keys stripped) and an open schema, a waiting child workflow, non object responses, a failing child workflow, and the item index when the second item fails, its input doesn't match the schema, or its tool can't be built. Locally `typecheck`, `lint` and the whole `@n8n/n8n-nodes-langchain` vitest suite pass. ## Related Linear tickets, Github issues, and Community forum posts Fixes #41604 ## Review / Merge checklist - [x] I have seen this code, I have run this code, and I take responsibility for this code. - [x] PR title and summary are descriptive. ([conventions](../blob/master/.github/pull_request_title_conventions.md)) - [ ] [Docs updated](https://github.com/n8n-io/n8n-docs) or follow-up ticket created. - [x] Tests included. - [ ] PR Labeled with `Backport to Beta`, `Backport to Stable`, or `Backport to v1` (if the PR is an urgent fix that needs to be backported)

issue.title: [BUG] Gemini: 503 UNAVAILABLE is not retried (Python ServerError, TS mid stream and non JSON 503), follow up to #4524 and #5751

labels.name: repo-13db12e3
labels.description: Something isn't working

labels.name: repo-13db12e3
labels.description: Pull requests that update python code

labels.name: repo-13db12e3
labels.description: Related to models or model providers

type.name: Bug
type.description: Something is broken or not working as documented. A functional defect in existing behavior.

issue.body:
### Human Overview

I ran into this while reading the Gemini provider next to the Bedrock 503 PR. A Gemini 503 means the model is overloaded and worth retrying, but right now it fails the agent straight away in Python and in two cases in TS. #4524 and #5751 both mentioned it as a follow up, so I wrote it down here. Happy to send a PR.

### Checks

- [x] I have updated to the lastest minor and patch version of Strands
- [x] I have checked the documentation and this is not expected behavior
- [x] I have searched [./issues](./issues?q=) and there are no duplicates of my issue

### SDK Language

Python

### Strands Version

main @ 40268cc5 (python/v1.64.0, typescript/v1.24.0); the TypeScript side has the same gap

### Language Runtime Version

Python >=3.10 with google-genai 1.68.0 and 2.34.0; Node.js 24.13.0 with @google/genai 2.3x

### Operating System

macOS 26.6

### Installation Method

git clone

### Steps to Reproduce

This is the follow up that #4524 and #5751 both pointed to as out of scope, and I don't think it got filed yet, so here it is. Huge thanks to the authors of those two PRs and to the reporter of #4523; the 429 fixes work really well, and this only picks up the 503 piece they flagged.

**Summary:** a Gemini 503 `UNAVAILABLE` still isn't retried in Python, and in TS it isn't retried when it comes mid stream or with a non JSON body.

**What the code is for:** map provider throttling and overload errors to the SDK's throttling error so the default retry strategy can back off and retry.

**Python**
1. Gemini returns 503 `UNAVAILABLE` (on the initial call or as a mid stream error chunk).
2. google-genai raises `genai.errors.ServerError`, which is a sibling of `ClientError` under `APIError`, not a subclass.
3. [`gemini.py#L740`](https://github.com/strands-agents/harness-sdk/blob/40268cc57937f6d344dde28462eb51db05f0318c/strands-py/src/strands/models/gemini.py#L740) only catches `genai.errors.ClientError`, so the `RESOURCE_EXHAUSTED | UNAVAILABLE` case on [L746-L747](https://github.com/strands-agents/harness-sdk/blob/40268cc57937f6d344dde28462eb51db05f0318c/strands-py/src/strands/models/gemini.py#L746-L747) never sees it.
4. The raw `ServerError` escapes, and [`_retry.py#L70`](https://github.com/strands-agents/harness-sdk/blob/40268cc57937f6d344dde28462eb51db05f0318c/strands-py/src/strands/event_loop/_retry.py#L70) only retries `ModelThrottledException`, so there is no retry.

```python
from google.genai import errors
try:
    errors.APIError.raise_error(503, {"error": {"code": 503, "status": "UNAVAILABLE", "message": "x"}}, None)
except Exception as e:
    print(type(e).__name__, isinstance(e, errors.ClientError))  # ServerError False
```

**TypeScript**
1. A 503 arrives either as a mid stream chunk (message `got status: UNAVAILABLE. {...}`, `ApiError.status` 503) or as a 503 with a non JSON body (message rewrapped with status "Service Unavailable").
2. [`classifyGoogleError`](https://github.com/strands-agents/harness-sdk/blob/40268cc57937f6d344dde28462eb51db05f0318c/strands-ts/src/models/google/errors.ts#L61) only short circuits on `ApiError` status 429.
3. `JSON.parse(error.message)` fails for both shapes, so [L73-L81](https://github.com/strands-agents/harness-sdk/blob/40268cc57937f6d344dde28462eb51db05f0318c/strands-ts/src/models/google/errors.ts#L73-L81) returns `undefined` before the `UNAVAILABLE` lookup on [L87](https://github.com/strands-agents/harness-sdk/blob/40268cc57937f6d344dde28462eb51db05f0318c/strands-ts/src/models/google/errors.ts#L87) is reached.
4. The raw error escapes, and the [default retry strategy](https://github.com/strands-agents/harness-sdk/blob/40268cc57937f6d344dde28462eb51db05f0318c/strands-ts/src/retry/default-model-retry-strategy.ts#L90) only retries `ModelThrottledError` or `ModelNetworkError`.

A 503 with a JSON `UNAVAILABLE` body is classified as throttling fine today; it's just these two shapes. The non JSON 503 shape is the one small detail I don't think was mentioned in #5751.

```mermaid
flowchart LR
  A[Gemini 503 UNAVAILABLE] --> P[Python: ServerError]
  P --> X[not caught by except ClientError] --> R[raw error, no retry]
  A --> T[TS: mid stream or non JSON body]
  T --> J[JSON.parse fails, returns undefined] --> R
```

### Expected Behavior

A 503 `UNAVAILABLE` from Gemini is mapped to `ModelThrottledException` / `ModelThrottledError` in both SDKs, whatever exception class or message shape it arrives in, so the default retry strategy retries it the same way it now retries 429.

### Actual Behavior

Python: in a live run with a full `Agent`, a 503 `UNAVAILABLE` produced a raw `ServerError` after 1 model call with no retry, while a 429 `RESOURCE_EXHAUSTED` was retried (6 calls) and then raised `ModelThrottledException`. Same on google-genai 1.68.0 and 2.34.0 (pyproject allows `>=1.68.0,<3.0.0`).

TS: `classifyGoogleError` returns `undefined` for both shapes above, so the error is not retried.

### Possible Solution

Would you prefer catching `genai.errors.APIError` in Python and keeping the same status matching (so `ServerError` 503 lands in the existing `UNAVAILABLE` branch), and treating `ApiError` status 503 as throttling in TS next to the existing 429 check? Or would you rather parse the JSON after the `got status:` prefix as #5751 suggested? Happy to go either way, and I'd be glad to send a PR for either or both if that helps.

A small side note on tests: `test_gemini.py` has no 503 / `UNAVAILABLE` / `ServerError` case, and the one near [L1357](https://github.com/strands-agents/harness-sdk/blob/40268cc57937f6d344dde28462eb51db05f0318c/strands-py/tests/strands/models/test_gemini.py#L1357) builds `ClientError(500, ...)`, which the real library wouldn't produce for a 5xx. Maybe worth adjusting in the same change?

### Additional Context

Why now: open PR #5530 (Bedrock 503) says it treats 503 as throttling "as we already do for Gemini", which holds for the TS JSON path but not yet for the Python `ServerError` path. Not a problem with that PR at all, just thought it was a nice moment to close the gap so the two providers really match.

### Related Issues

#4523, #4524, #5751, #5744, #5530, #5814

issue.title: @posthog/ai: Anthropic wrapper doesn't capture thinking tokens as $ai_reasoning_tokens
issue.body:
## Bug description

The Anthropic wrapper in `@posthog/ai` never sets `$ai_reasoning_tokens`, even when Claude reports thinking token counts.

The wrapper is there so Anthropic calls show up in LLM analytics with token counts and cost, same as the OpenAI and Gemini wrappers. Since 0.100.0, `@anthropic-ai/sdk` has `output_tokens_details: { thinking_tokens } | null` on both `Usage` and `MessageDeltaUsage`, so it exists on every version in the current peer range (`>=0.112.3 <0.135.0`). The Anthropic docs point people to `usage.output_tokens_details.thinking_tokens` for monitoring this, and when streaming it comes in on the final `message_delta`.

Right now:

1. A call with extended thinking enabled goes through the wrapper.
2. Anthropic returns `usage.output_tokens_details.thinking_tokens` (on the response, or on the last `message_delta` when streaming).
3. The streaming usage block in `packages/ai/src/anthropic/index.ts` (around L245 to L272) only reads `output_tokens`, and the non streaming path (around L390 to L397) does the same, so `reasoningTokens` is never set.
4. `captureAiGeneration.ts` (L192) only emits `$ai_reasoning_tokens` when `usage.reasoningTokens` is set, so the event goes out without it.

The Claude Agent SDK processor has the same gap: `AnthropicUsage` in `claude-agent-sdk/processor.ts` (around L70 to L76) and `readUsage` (around L870 to L880) don't read the field either.

Other wrappers already do this (`openai/telemetry.ts` L97 and L112, `gemini/usage.ts` L14, the Vercel middleware and the LangChain callbacks), so Anthropic is the odd one out. From what I can tell the ingestion side (`modality-tokens.ts` in PostHog/posthog) doesn't derive it from `$ai_usage` and drops `$ai_usage` afterwards, so Anthropic events never end up with the metric.

**Expected:** map `output_tokens_details.thinking_tokens` to `reasoningTokens` in the stream, non stream and agent SDK paths, like OpenAI and Gemini. A `null` `output_tokens_details` would just be treated as absent.

Cost isn't affected here. `output_tokens` already includes thinking, and the server only adds a separate reasoning cost for Gemini 2.5 and 3, so this is only about the reasoning token count being visible.

## How to reproduce

1. Wrap a mocked Anthropic client with `@posthog/ai` and have `messages.create` return:
   ```ts
   {
     id: 'msg_1',
     type: 'message',
     role: 'assistant',
     model: 'claude-sonnet-4-5',
     content: [{ type: 'text', text: 'hi' }],
     stop_reason: 'end_turn',
     usage: {
       input_tokens: 20,
       output_tokens: 600,
       output_tokens_details: { thinking_tokens: 512 },
     },
   }
   ```
2. Call `messages.create` through the wrapper (or stream with the same usage on the final `message_delta`).
3. The captured `$ai_generation` has `$ai_output_tokens: 600` but no `$ai_reasoning_tokens`.

## Related sub-libraries

- [ ] All of them
- [ ] posthog-js (web)
- [ ] posthog-js-lite (web lite)
- [ ] posthog-node
- [ ] posthog-react-native
- [ ] @posthog/react
- [x] @posthog/ai
- [ ] @posthog/convex
- [ ] @posthog/nextjs-config
- [ ] @posthog/nuxt
- [ ] @posthog/rollup-plugin
- [ ] @posthog/webpack-plugin

## Additional context

Related: #5375, which nicely captures the thinking text as reasoning content. This would be the count side of the same thing. #3160 covers Gemini reasoning cost.

Two questions before I touch anything:

- Would you want the Claude Agent SDK processor fixed in the same change, or kept separate?
- Is client side the right place for this, given the server drops `$ai_usage`? Or would you rather derive it during ingestion?

Happy to put up a PR for whichever way you prefer. Seen on main at a0e6485.

issue.title: fix(world-postgres): send one stream notify per writeMulti batch
issue.body:
A streamed answer made Postgres commit one notification and run one read for every few characters; now each batch of text costs one notification and one read.

### Description

**What this code is for**

`packages/world-postgres/src/streamer.ts` stores every stream chunk as a row in `workflow_stream_chunks` and tells readers about new rows with `pg_notify` on the `workflow_event_chunk` channel. Each process with an open reader listens on that channel, loads the new rows, and hands them to its readers. `streams.writeMulti()` is the path a workflow uses when it flushes several chunks at once, which is how a model's streamed answer reaches the database.

**Before this PR**

A workflow streams a model's answer, and the runtime flushes 50 chunks to `streams.writeMulti()` while one process is reading the stream.

1. `writeMulti()` makes 50 ids with `genChunkId()` and writes all 50 rows in one `INSERT`.
2. It then loops over the 50 ids and awaits `SELECT pg_notify($1, $2)` once per id, each payload being `{ streamId, chunkId }`.
3. Each `pg_notify` is its own committed transaction, and each commit takes the database wide NOTIFY lock.
4. The listening process gets 50 notifications and, for each one, runs a `SELECT ... WHERE chunk_id = $chunkId LIMIT 1`.
5. One batch of 50 chunks plus `close()` costs 51 `pg_notify` calls and 51 reads per listening process. In the issue, a 491 chunk answer measured about 3.5 committed transactions per chunk.

**After this PR**

Same workflow, same 50 chunk batch, same reader.

1. Same as above: 50 ids, one `INSERT`.
2. `writeMulti()` sends one `pg_notify` whose payload is `{ streamId, firstChunkId, chunkId }`, the first and last ids of the batch.
3. The listening process runs one `SELECT ... WHERE chunk_id BETWEEN firstChunkId AND chunkId ORDER BY chunk_id` and hands the rows to its readers in id order.
4. `write()` and `close()` still send `{ streamId, chunkId }` with no `firstChunkId`, so the range is that one id and the read returns exactly one row, as before.
5. One batch of 50 chunks plus `close()` costs 2 `pg_notify` calls and 2 reads per listening process.

**The diagram**

```mermaid
flowchart LR

classDef box fill:#eef1ff,stroke:#4c5bd4,color:#111827
classDef bad fill:#ffd6d6,stroke:#cc0000,color:#111827,stroke-width:3px
classDef good fill:#c8f0c8,stroke:#008800,color:#111827,stroke-width:3px

subgraph BEFORE["BEFORE: 51 NOTIFY and 51 reads"]
direction TB
  B1["workflow flushes 50 chunks"] --> B2["writeMulti: one INSERT of 50 rows"]
  B2 --> B3{"pg_notify per chunkId"}
  B3 -->|"50 chunks"| B4["50 NOTIFY, 50 reads by chunkId"]
  B3 -->|"close()"| B5["1 NOTIFY, 1 read"]
end

subgraph AFTER["AFTER: 2 NOTIFY and 2 reads"]
direction TB
  A1["workflow flushes 50 chunks"] --> A2["writeMulti: one INSERT of 50 rows"]
  A2 --> A3{"THE CHANGE: one pg_notify with firstChunkId"}
  A3 -->|"50 chunks"| A4["1 NOTIFY, 1 read BETWEEN first and last"]
  A3 -->|"write() or close()"| A5["1 NOTIFY, 1 read, same as before"]
end

B1 ~~~ A1

class B1,B2,B5 box
class A1,A2,A5 box
class B3,B4 bad
class A3,A4 good

linkStyle 2 stroke:#cc0000,stroke-width:5px
linkStyle 6 stroke:#008800,stroke-width:5px

style BEFORE fill:#fff5f5,stroke:#cc0000,color:#111827
style AFTER fill:#f3fff3,stroke:#008800,color:#111827
```

**The change**

- `writeMulti()` replaces the `for (const chunkId of chunkIds)` loop of awaited `notifyStream()` calls with one `notifyStream()` carrying `firstChunkId: chunkIds[0]` and `chunkId: chunkIds[chunkIds.length - 1]`. That is the fix on the write side.
- `StreamPublishMessage` gains an optional `firstChunkId`.
- The `listenChannel` callback reads `between(streams.chunkId, parsed.firstChunkId ?? parsed.chunkId, parsed.chunkId)` ordered by `chunkId` and emits every row, instead of reading one row by `eq(streams.chunkId, parsed.chunkId)`. That is the fix on the read side. The table's primary key is `(stream_id, id)`, so this is one index range read.
- `.changeset/postgres-batch-stream-notify.md` adds a patch changeset for `@workflow/world-postgres`.

**What changes for a user**

- A streamed answer costs one notification and one read per batch instead of per chunk, so many concurrent streams queue far less on the NOTIFY lock at commit.
- Readers still get every chunk once, in id order. The existing check in `streams.get()` that skips ids at or below the last one delivered is unchanged.
- `write()`, `close()`, the replay after a LISTEN reconnect, and `startIndex` work as before.
- A notification from an older writer, `{ streamId, chunkId }`, still reads exactly that one chunk, so a new reader keeps working next to old writers.
- The payload grows by about 50 bytes, far under the 8000 byte NOTIFY limit for any normal stream name.

Thank you so much @3lbrayan for the very clear report and the measurements; this follows your ask of one NOTIFY per batch with a range read. I went with the batch's first and last ids in the payload rather than a per process "last seen" cursor, so the listener needs no extra state per stream, but I would really value your view on which you prefer. I also noticed @Pom4H's #1881 (range reads plus polling for missed notifications) and @burn2delete's #4626 (starting the listener on first read); this PR only touches the batch notify and the notified read, so it should sit alongside either of them, and I am happy to rebase onto whichever lands first.

One question for the maintainers, if I may: during a rolling deploy where an older version is still reading, an older reader that receives a batch notification reads only the last chunk of that batch. Would you like me to keep this as is, gate it behind a version field in the payload, or handle it some other way? I am glad to go whichever direction you think is best.

### How did you test your changes?

- New `packages/world-postgres/test/stream-batch-notify.test.ts` opens a reader, writes 50 chunks with `writeMulti()`, closes the stream, and counts the `pg_notify` calls and chunk reads on the pool. On `main` it fails with 51 notifications where 2 are expected; with this change it passes and the reader receives all 50 chunks in order.
- The existing `stream-offset`, `stream-post-eof-duplicates`, `listen-reconnect` and `src/streamer.test.ts` tests pass. `stream-offset` sends an old style `{ streamId, chunkId }` notification by hand, which covers the older writer path.
- `pnpm typecheck`, `pnpm build` and `biome check` pass for `@workflow/world-postgres` (the two complexity warnings in `streamer.ts` are the same ones on `main`).

### PR Checklist - Required to merge

- [x] 📦 `pnpm changeset` was run to create a changelog for this PR
- [x] 🔒 DCO sign-off passes (run `git commit --signoff` on your commits)
- [x] 📝 Ping `@vercel/workflow` in a comment once the PR is ready, and the above checklist is complete

Closes #5061

issue.title: fix(awk): run every END statement after next or nextfile on the last record
issue.body:
**What broke:** when the last input record ran `next` or `nextfile`, `END` stopped after its first statement. `awk '{ next } END { print "E1"; print "E2" }'` printed only `E1`.

**Root cause:** `executeEnd()` cleared `shouldExit` but not `shouldNext` / `shouldNextFile`, so the leftover flag from the last record halted the END statement loop.

**Change:** clear both flags in `executeEnd()` next to `shouldExit` (`src/commands/awk/interpreter/interpreter.ts`). I also checked the other places these flags could leak: `shouldNext` is reset per record and `shouldNextFile` per file, so END was the only gap. A patch changeset is included.

**Tests:** new `awk.end-after-next.test.ts` covers `next` and `nextfile` on the last record, multiple files, stdin, a loop plus a second END block, and `exit` inside END still stopping and setting the exit code. All fail before the change and pass after. Typecheck, lint and the awk suites pass.

Fixes #483

Thanks @trieloff for the clear report. Happy to adjust anything if you'd prefer a different approach.

Happy (almost) Halloween! 🎃

issue.title: execute_sql runs MERGE ... WHEN MATCHED THEN DELETE without the destructive confirmation
issue.body:
Hey folks, I think `execute_sql` lets a `MERGE ... WHEN MATCHED THEN DELETE` (or `THEN UPDATE`) run without the destructive SQL confirmation, even when it touches every row.

### What the confirmation is for

When `execute_sql` is in `confirmation.enabledTools` (opt in, and the client needs elicitation support), the server asks before running SQL it considers destructive. The prompt text in `database-operation-tools.ts:502` says it covers "DROP, DELETE, TRUNCATE or UPDATE without WHERE". A MERGE that deletes or updates every matched row seems to fit that intent pretty squarely.

### Current behavior

1. Create a table with two rows: `create table films (id int, title text); insert into films values (1, 'a'), (2, 'b');`
2. Run the server not read only, with `execute_sql` in `confirmation.enabledTools`, using a client that supports elicitation.
3. Call `execute_sql` with `merge into films f using films s on true when matched then delete`
4. No confirmation is shown (the decision is recorded as `bypass` with reason `not_destructive`).
5. Both rows are gone.

### Expected behavior

The same confirmation you get for `delete from films` should show up before the MERGE runs.

### Minimal repro

Against main at 7e5037b:

```ts
import { isDestructiveSql } from './packages/mcp-server-supabase/src/tools/destructive-sql.js';

isDestructiveSql('merge into films f using (select 1) s on true when matched then delete');                  // false
isDestructiveSql('merge into films f using films s on true when matched then delete');                       // false
isDestructiveSql('explain analyze merge into films f using films s on true when matched then delete');       // false
isDestructiveSql('merge into films f using films s on true when matched then update set title = null');      // false

isDestructiveSql('delete from films');                // true
isDestructiveSql('update films set title = null');    // true
```

From reading the code, I think this is why:

* `destructive-sql.ts:70` only flags statements that start with `drop`, `delete` or `truncate`.
* `isUpdateWithoutWhereFromScan` (`destructive-sql.ts:191` to `197`) needs the statement to start with `update`.
* The `explain analyze` recheck (`destructive-sql.ts:272` to `279`) runs those same checks on the body, so it misses MERGE too.
* `database-operation-tools.ts:78` then skips the confirmation with `not_destructive`.

```mermaid
flowchart LR
  A[execute_sql with MERGE] --> B{starts with drop, delete, truncate or update?}
  B -- no --> C[not_destructive]
  C --> D[runs with no confirmation]
```

### Related work

Huge thanks to @barryroodt for #408, which added this whole confirmation flow, and for #426, which moves the check onto a real parser. The data modifying CTE forms (`with d as (delete ... returning) select ...`, and `explain analyze` of them) are already listed as a known trade off in #408 and handled in #426, so I'm only raising MERGE here. From what I can see, `classifyStatement` in #426 doesn't have a `MergeStmt` branch yet, so MERGE would still slip through after it lands.

### Question

Would you rather have MERGE added as a small check on the current scanner, or handled as a `MergeStmt` case in #426? Totally happy either way, and I'm glad to send a PR for whichever you prefer (or leave it to Barry if it fits better in #426). Let me know if I've misread anything!

issue.title: Question option descriptions are dropped on Telegram, Teams and Chat SDK cards, and cut on Discord

labels.name: repo-f1ccb1c0
labels.description: Something isn't working

issue.body:
Option descriptions from `ask_question` never reach the user on Telegram, Teams and Chat SDK cards, and get cut off on Discord, so people can pick an option without seeing its tradeoff.

Huge thanks to @mrud for the clear repro in #6031. This is the same thing on the other channels, so I wanted to write it down in one place.

### Link to a minimal reproduction

No separate repo yet, sorry. The repro is just one `ask_question` call (below), checked against `main` at 4f32632. Happy to put up a repo if that helps.

### Steps to reproduce

`ask_question` is how an agent asks the user to choose between options. Every option needs a `description` of 1 to 200 chars, described in the schema as "One short sentence on the impact or tradeoff of choosing this option" (`packages/eve/src/tools/provided/ask-question.ts` around L42 to L56). `ask-question-workflow.ts` (around L19 to L30) passes it through with `display: "select"`, and nothing adds the descriptions to the prompt text or sends them anywhere else.

Have the agent call:

```json
{
  "prompt": "Choose an option",
  "options": [
    { "id": "one", "label": "Option one", "description": "AAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAA IMPORTANT: selecting this option loses data." },
    { "id": "two", "label": "Option two", "description": "No data is lost." }
  ]
}
```

Then look at what each channel renders:

**Telegram** (`public/channels/telegram/hitl.ts` around L73 to L87)
1. The message text is only the prompt.
2. The buttons carry `truncate(label, 64)`.
3. The description is never shown, so the "loses data" warning is missing.

**Teams** (`public/channels/teams/hitl.ts` around L93 to L101, choices around L241 to L253, actions around L299 to L303)
1. The card shows the prompt and the option labels.
2. `formatApprovalInput` returns nothing for questions (around L346).
3. The description is never shown.

**Discord** (`public/channels/discord/hitl.ts` around L37 and L60 to L79)
1. The message content is only the prompt (`discord/defaults.ts` around L191).
2. The select option description is cut to 100 chars with `...` (that's Discord's own field limit).
3. The rest of the description, including the warning, is shown nowhere.

**Chat SDK** (`chat-sdk/input-actions.ts`)
1. Card buttons carry labels only (around L69 to L89).
2. Only the numbered text fallback for adapters that can't render cards (around L52 to L67, documented in `chat-sdk/reference.mdx` around L173) includes the full description.
3. On any adapter that does render cards, the description is never shown.

### Current vs. expected behavior

Current: on Telegram, Teams and Chat SDK cards the description is dropped completely, and on Discord it's cut at 100 chars with the remainder nowhere. In the repro, nobody sees "IMPORTANT: selecting this option loses data." before choosing.

Expected: users can read each option's full description somewhere on every channel, for example in the message body when the native control can't hold it, while the controls still respect each platform's limits and route the selected answer correctly.

### eve version

`main` at 4f32632 (packages/eve 1.0.0-rc.6)

### Environment

Found by reading the renderers on `main`; not tested in live Telegram, Teams or Discord clients yet.

### Where does the bug occur?

Production (`eve start` / deployed), any agent using `ask_question` on these channels.

### Additional context

Same class as #6031 (Slack cuts descriptions at 75), and #5134 touches the Slack picker side.

Quick question for you all: would you like this folded into the #6031 fix as one shared approach (say, rendering descriptions in the message body whenever the control can't carry them), or tracked per channel? Either way works for me, and I'm glad to help with a PR once you pick a direction.

issue.title: RestApiTool sends null header and cookie params as "null" and objects as [object Object]

labels.name: repo-03a26658
labels.description: Something isn't working

labels.name: repo-03a26658
labels.description: [Status] The PR/issue is awaiting review from the maintainer

issue.body:
**Describe the bug**
`prepareRequestParams` in `RestApiTool` turns `null` header and cookie args into the literal string `"null"`, and object or array values in path, header and cookie params into `[object Object]` or a lossy comma string.

`RestApiTool` is what `OpenAPIToolset` builds for each operation in a spec: the model fills in the params, and `prepareRequestParams` (core/src/tools/openapi_tool/rest_api_tool.ts) maps them onto the URL, query, headers, cookies and body before the request goes out.

Query params already handle this nicely (thanks to #1135): `null`, `undefined` and `''` are skipped and objects are JSON encoded. Path (~L343), header (~L355) and cookie (~L357) just use `String(argValue)`.

**To Reproduce**
1. Have an operation with a path param `id`, header params `X-Tenant` and `X-Filter`, a cookie param `session`, and a query param `q`. Any of them nullable in the spec is enough, since `gemini_schema_util.ts` (~L160) tells the model `null` is allowed.
2. The model calls the tool with `{id: {kind: 'a'}, 'X-Tenant': null, 'X-Filter': {role: 'admin'}, session: null, q: null}`.
3. `runAsync` passes `request.args` straight into `prepareRequestParams`.
4. The request goes out as:
   - url: `.../items/%5Bobject%20Object%5D`
   - headers: `{"X-Tenant": "null", "X-Filter": "[object Object]"}`
   - `Cookie: session=null`
   - `q` is correctly left out

`undefined` becomes `"undefined"` the same way, and an array like `[1, null]` becomes `"1,"`.

Minimal repro:

```ts
import {prepareRequestParams} from './core/src/tools/openapi_tool/rest_api_tool.js';

const p = (name: string, paramLocation: string) =>
  ({name, originalName: name, paramLocation, paramSchema: {}, required: false});

const out = prepareRequestParams(
  {baseUrl: 'https://api.example.com', path: '/items/{id}', method: 'get'},
  [p('id', 'path'), p('X-Tenant', 'header'), p('X-Filter', 'header'), p('session', 'cookie'), p('q', 'query')],
  {id: {kind: 'a'}, 'X-Tenant': null, 'X-Filter': {role: 'admin'}, session: null, q: null},
);
console.log(out);
// url ends with /items/%5Bobject%20Object%5D
// headers: { "X-Tenant": "null", "X-Filter": "[object Object]", Cookie: "session=null" }
// no q in the query string
```

**Expected behavior**
- Header and cookie params that are `null` or `undefined` are skipped, the same way query params are.
- Arrays and objects in path, header and cookie params are serialized per OpenAPI `style: simple`, matching `adk-python`'s `_to_param_string` (rest_api_tool.py ~L92 to 117): arrays comma joined with `None` dropped, objects as `k,v` pairs, booleans as `true`/`false`. Python also skips `None` for header (~L527) and cookie (~L530).

**Desktop (please complete the following information):**
 - OS: any
 - TS version/environment: Node
 - ADK version: main at eedc561

**Additional context**
One thing I wasn't sure about: Python sends `None` into the path too (no guard there), so a `null` path param is a gap in both. Should that be handled here as well, maybe by leaving it out or raising a clear error? Would you be open to one PR covering header, cookie and path in the same style as #1135?

Also kindly pointing to @OsamaAnsar's #1208, which fixes the same kind of serialization for form bodies, so this would be its sibling for the other param locations.

Happy to open a PR for this if it sounds good to you.

issue.title: Anthropic Chat Model (lmChatAnthropic v1.5): sends `thinking: {type:"disabled"}` (400 on claude-sonnet-5-5) and parallel tool calls reach AI Agent tools with missing arguments

issue.body:
### Bug Description

## Bug Description

Two issues when using the **Anthropic Chat Model** node as the language model of an **AI Agent** node that has several tools (HTTP Request tools + structured tools).

### 1. Claude Sonnet 5.5 rejects every request (400)

With model `claude-sonnet-5-5`, every call fails:

```
400 invalid_request_error — thinking type "disabled" is not supported for this model, use "between_tools"
request_id: req_011CgQLZKZVVJVAu1TXnmK9p
```

The node sends `thinking: {"type": "disabled"}` even though "thinking" is not enabled in the node options. Per Anthropic's Sonnet 5.5 docs, `disabled` returns 400 on this model; the lowest setting is `{"type": "between_tools"}`, or the field can be omitted (adaptive).
`@langchain/anthropic` **1.5.1** already fixed this ("Stop sending `thinking: { type: "disabled" }` on ChatAnthropic requests when the user never configured thinking"). Bumping the dependency (and/or exposing `between_tools` in the node options) should fix it.

### 2. Parallel tool calls arrive at tools with missing required arguments

With `claude-sonnet-4-6` (thinking issue avoided), when the model emits **several tool_use blocks in one turn**, the agent fails with:

```
Received tool input did not match expected schema
✖ Required → at search_query
```
and on another tool:
```
✖ Required → at analyse   ✖ Required → at pertinence   ✖ Required → at resume
```

The same workflow, same prompt, same tools and **same model through an OpenAI-compatible provider (OpenRouter `anthropic/claude-sonnet-4.6`)** works reliably. This suggests the tool inputs of parallel `tool_use` blocks are lost/partially assembled in the Anthropic path (streamed `input_json_delta` consolidation?), not a model issue.

## To Reproduce

1. AI Agent node (v1.6), ≥3 tools with required string parameters (e.g. one HTTP Request tool with `search_query`, one tool with `analyse`, `pertinence`, `resume`).
2. Connect **Anthropic Chat Model** (v1.5), model `claude-sonnet-5-5` → error 1 on first call.
3. Switch model to `claude-sonnet-4-6`, prompt that encourages several searches → error 2 as soon as the model issues parallel tool calls (reproduced on 2 consecutive runs).
4. Replace the model with OpenRouter Chat Model, `anthropic/claude-sonnet-4.6` → works.

## Expected behavior

- No `thinking` field sent unless configured (or `between_tools` available) so Sonnet 5.5 works.
- Every parallel `tool_use` block's full `input` is passed to the matching tool.

## Workaround

Use the same Claude model via OpenRouter (OpenAI-compatible) instead of the native Anthropic node.

## Environment

- n8n version: [n8n version] — self-hosted (Docker, Coolify), queue mode: no
- Nodes: `@n8n/n8n-nodes-langchain.agent` v1.6, `@n8n/n8n-nodes-langchain.lmChatAnthropic` v1.5
- Models: `claude-sonnet-5-5`, `claude-sonnet-4-6` (Anthropic API, direct key)
- OS: Linux (Ubuntu VPS)

## Related

- Anthropic — What's new in Claude Sonnet 5.5 (breaking change: `between_tools`): https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/models/sonnet-5-5/whats-new-sonnet-5-5
- @langchain/anthropic CHANGELOG 1.5.1 / 1.3.11 (input_json_delta consolidation): https://app.unpkg.com/@langchain/anthropic@1.5.2/files/CHANGELOG.md
- Community threads with the same schema error: https://community.n8n.io/t/received-tool-input-did-not-match-expected-schema-required/276546 and https://community.n8n.io/t/problem-in-node-ai-agent-received-tool-input-did-not-match-expected-schema/86219


### To Reproduce

1. Create an AI Agent node (v1.6) with 3+ tools that have required string parameters (e.g. an HTTP Request tool with `search_query`, a tool with `analyse`, `pertinence`, `resume`).
2. Connect an Anthropic Chat Model node (v1.5) with model `claude-sonnet-5-5` (no thinking option enabled) and run the workflow.
   → Every call fails: `400 invalid_request_error – thinking type "disabled" is not supported for this model, use "between_tools"` (request_id req_011CgQLZKZVVJVAu1TXnmK9p).
3. Switch the model to `claude-sonnet-4-6` and use a prompt that leads the agent to call several tools in the same turn.
   → As soon as the model emits parallel tool_use blocks, the agent fails with:
   `Received tool input did not match expected schema ✖ Required → at search_query`
   and on another tool: `✖ Required → at analyse ✖ Required → at pertinence ✖ Required → at resume`
   (reproduced on 2 consecutive runs).
4. Replace the Anthropic Chat Model with the OpenRouter Chat Model using `anthropic/claude-sonnet-4.6` (same prompt, same tools) → works reliably.

### Expected behavior

- The Anthropic Chat Model node should not send `thinking: {type:"disabled"}` when thinking is not configured (already fixed upstream in @langchain/anthropic 1.5.1), or should offer `between_tools`, so that claude-sonnet-5-5 works (see https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/models/sonnet-5-5/whats-new-sonnet-5-5).
- When the model returns several tool_use blocks in one turn, each tool should receive its full `input` with all required arguments, as it does with the same model via an OpenAI-compatible provider.

Hey @dtouidjine-maker, hope you're doing well! Thanks for such a thorough report. The request id and the pointer to the langchain changelog made this really easy to trace.

I checked the first part against current master. Your debug info shows 2.34.6, which pins `@langchain/anthropic` 1.3.27, and that version fills in `thinking: { type: "disabled" }` on its own. n8n moved to 1.5.6 by 2.38.0.
