comment.body:
Hey @sweethuman, hope you're doing well! Thanks for opening this, and a big thank you to @gouveags for building it out in #5091.

Quick update for anyone landing here: Interactions tracing shipped in `@posthog/ai` 8.15.0. `PostHogGoogleGenAI` now has `interactions.create`, which traces regular and streamed foreground model calls. A couple of things I noticed while reading main:

1. It needs `@google/genai` 2.18 or newer. You mentioned 2.13.0, so you'd want to bump that first, otherwise the wrapper throws an error asking for 2.18.
2. Background calls (`background: true`) and agent calls are rejected on purpose, since they complete outside the original request and need their own lifecycle tracking. The README calls this out too.

@sweethuman, are your calls all foreground? If so, would it be OK to close this one? If background or agent interactions matter for you, maybe we keep it open just for that part. Would love to hear what @marandaneto and @carlos-marchal-ph think as well.

issue.title: Bug: Generated CRL issuer DN does not match externally signed Intermediate CA certificate – revocation validation fails
issue.body:
### Product

Certificate Manager (PKI)

### Describe the bug

Summary

When using an Infisical-managed Intermediate Certificate Authority (CA) whose CA certificate was externally signed by Microsoft Active Directory Certificate Services (AD CS), Infisical generates Certificate Revocation Lists (CRLs) with an issuer Distinguished Name (DN) that differs from the Subject DN of the actual Intermediate CA certificate.

Although both Distinguished Names contain the same attributes and values, the Relative Distinguished Names (RDNs) appear in a different order.

As a result, OpenSSL cannot locate the corresponding CRL issuer certificate, and Windows certificate validation fails during revocation checking.

The issue affects certificates issued by this CA, including TLS certificates used for internal services.

The problem has been reproduced with Infisical v0.166.9 and v0.167.4, including a freshly generated CRL after upgrading to v0.167.4.

The issue may be related to how Infisical reconstructs the CRL issuer DN from the internally stored CA metadata rather than preserving the exact Subject DN of the signed Intermediate CA certificate.

Environment

Infisical: Self-hosted

Initially affected version: v0.166.9

Latest tested version: v0.167.4

CA type: Infisical-managed Intermediate CA

Intermediate CA signing: Externally signed by Microsoft AD CS

Root CA: Microsoft Active Directory Certificate Services

Intermediate CA private key: Managed by Infisical

Certificate issuance: Infisical ACME / Certbot

Certificate usage: Internal TLS services, including SMTP

Linux TLS validation: OpenSSL

Windows TLS validation: Windows certificate chain engine / .NET

Client application: .NET application using MailKit

CA key algorithm: ECDSA P-256

CRL signature algorithm: ECDSA with SHA-256

Certificate Authority hierarchy

The PKI consists of:

Microsoft AD CS Root CA
         |
         +-- Infisical Intermediate CA
                    |
                    +-- Internal TLS Server Certificate

The Intermediate CA was created and is managed by Infisical. Its CA certificate was signed by an existing Microsoft AD CS Root CA.

The signed Intermediate CA certificate was imported into Infisical to complete the CA setup.

Infisical subsequently issues and manages TLS certificates using this Intermediate CA.

The Intermediate CA certificate and its private key are valid, and certificate issuance works correctly.

### To Reproduce

Steps to Reproduce

1. Create an Intermediate CA in Infisical

Create a new internally managed Intermediate CA in Infisical and generate a CSR.

Have the CSR signed by an external CA, such as Microsoft AD CS.

Import the externally signed Intermediate CA certificate back into Infisical.

The resulting CA certificate has a Subject DN similar to:

CN=Example Intermediate CA,OU=IT,O=Example Organization,L=Example City,ST=Example State,C=DE

Note: All identifying values in this report have been anonymized. The RDN ordering shown here matches the observed behavior.

2. Issue a TLS certificate

Issue a server certificate using the Infisical Intermediate CA.

In our case, issuance is performed using Certbot through Infisical's ACME interface.

Certificate issuance succeeds.

The resulting certificate:

Has a valid digital signature.

Contains the expected DNS Subject Alternative Name.

Contains the appropriate TLS Server Authentication Extended Key Usage.

Contains an HTTP(S) CRL Distribution Point pointing to Infisical.

Chains successfully to the externally signed Intermediate CA and its trusted Root CA.

3. Download the CRL

Download the DER-encoded CRL published by Infisical using the CRL Distribution Point embedded in the issued certificate.

For example:

curl -fsS "$CRL_URL" -o infisical.crl

The downloaded CRL is a correctly encoded X.509 CRL and can be parsed with OpenSSL and Windows CertUtil.

4. Compare the Intermediate CA Subject DN with the CRL Issuer DN

Extract the Subject DN of the actual signed Intermediate CA certificate:

openssl x509 \
  -in intermediate-ca.pem \
  -noout \
  -subject \
  -nameopt RFC2253

Observed output (anonymized):

subject=CN=Example Intermediate CA,OU=IT,O=Example Organization,L=Example City,ST=Example State,C=DE

Next, inspect the Issuer DN of the Infisical-generated CRL:

openssl crl \
  -inform DER \
  -in infisical.crl \
  -noout \
  -issuer \
  -nameopt RFC2253

Observed output (anonymized):

issuer=L=Example City,CN=Example Intermediate CA,ST=Example State,OU=IT,O=Example Organization,C=DE

The Distinguished Names do not match.

The attributes and values are the same, but their relative ordering is different.

For clarity:

Actual Intermediate CA certificate Subject DN:

CN, OU, O, L, ST, C

Infisical-generated CRL Issuer DN:

L, CN, ST, OU, O, C

This difference is not merely cosmetic. The ordering of RDNs is significant for X.509 Name comparison.

5. Verify the CRL using OpenSSL

Run:

openssl crl \
  -inform DER \
  -in infisical.crl \
  -verify \
  -CAfile intermediate-ca.pem \
  -noout

Actual result:

Error getting CRL issuer certificate

Exit code:

1

Even though the correct Intermediate CA certificate is supplied, OpenSSL cannot identify it as the issuer of the CRL.

The same failure occurs when providing the certificate chain containing the Intermediate CA certificate.

6. Verify the CRL using Windows CertUtil

On a Windows Server with the Root CA and Intermediate CA certificates installed, download the Infisical CRL and run:

certutil -dump C:\Temp\infisical.crl

The CRL can be parsed successfully.

However, verification of the CRL against the issuing Intermediate CA certificate fails:

certutil -verify `
  C:\Temp\infisical.crl `
  C:\Temp\intermediate-ca.cer `
  C:\Temp\server.cer

Relevant output (translated from German):

CRL signature is valid

ERROR: CRL issuer does not match certificate issuer

The CRL could not be verified as issued by
the supplied Intermediate CA certificate.

Windows also reports:

CRYPT_E_REVOCATION_OFFLINE
0x80092013

When checking the TLS server certificate with:

certutil -verify -urlfetch C:\Temp\server.cer

the output includes:

CERT_TRUST_REVOCATION_STATUS_UNKNOWN
CERT_TRUST_IS_OFFLINE_REVOCATION

The CRL download itself succeeds. However, Windows reports that the CRL issuer is invalid.

7. Verify the certificate chain without revocation checking

To isolate the problem from certificate path building, we tested the same certificate with the Windows X509Chain API while disabling revocation checking only for this diagnostic test.

$cert = [System.Security.Cryptography.X509Certificates.X509Certificate2]::new(
    "C:\Temp\server.cer"
)

$chain = [System.Security.Cryptography.X509Certificates.X509Chain]::new($true)

$chain.ChainPolicy.RevocationMode = "NoCheck"
$chain.ChainPolicy.VerificationFlags = "NoFlag"

$ok = $chain.Build($cert)

Write-Host "Certificate chain valid: $ok"

$chain.ChainStatus | Format-List

Result:

Certificate chain valid: True

No chain validation errors are reported.

This demonstrates that the CA hierarchy and the server certificate can be validated successfully when revocation checking is excluded.

The Root CA and Intermediate CA are installed in the Windows Local Machine certificate stores.

The Intermediate CA certificate has also been checked against the certificate published through the Infisical Authority Information Access (AIA) endpoint. The certificate is identical.

### Expected behavior

Expected Behavior

Infisical should generate CRLs whose Issuer DN correctly matches the Subject DN of the actual Intermediate CA certificate used to sign certificates.

For externally signed Intermediate CAs, Infisical should preserve the signed CA certificate's Subject DN, including its RDN ordering and correct ASN.1 Name structure.

For example:

Intermediate CA Subject:
CN=Example Intermediate CA,OU=IT,O=Example Organization,L=Example City,ST=Example State,C=DE

CRL Issuer:
CN=Example Intermediate CA,OU=IT,O=Example Organization,L=Example City,ST=Example State,C=DE

OpenSSL and Windows should be able to associate the CRL with the correct issuing CA and perform normal certificate revocation checks.

Actual Behavior

Infisical generates the CRL with a reordered Issuer DN:

L=Example City,CN=Example Intermediate CA,ST=Example State,OU=IT,O=Example Organization,C=DE

This DN does not match the actual Intermediate CA certificate's Subject DN.

The CRL is downloadable and parseable, but it cannot be successfully associated with the issuing CA during certificate revocation validation.

Consequently, certificate validation fails when clients enforce revocation checking.

### Screenshots

_No response_

### Deployment Type

Self-hosted

### Additional context

Evidence That the Problem Persists After Upgrading

The issue was initially observed on Infisical v0.166.9.

We upgraded to Infisical v0.167.4 and repeated the tests.

Initially, the CRL still had timestamps from before the upgrade, so this alone was not considered conclusive.

We subsequently tested a newly generated CRL after the upgrade.

The newly generated CRL reported:

lastUpdate=Nov  1 00:00:53 2026 GMT
nextUpdate=Nov  8 00:00:53 2026 GMT

Its Issuer DN still contained the incorrect RDN ordering:

issuer=L=Example City,CN=Example Intermediate CA,ST=Example State,OU=IT,O=Example Organization,C=DE

CRL verification still failed:

Error getting CRL issuer certificate

This confirms that the issue persists in CRLs generated after upgrading to v0.167.4.

We also reviewed the changes in v0.167.6. No explicit fix for this issue was identified, but v0.167.6 has not yet been independently validated in our environment.

Possible Root Cause

While reviewing the Infisical source code, we noticed the following implementation in:

backend/src/services/certificate-authority/certificate-authority-fns.ts

Function:

rebuildCaCrl

Relevant code in v0.167.6:

const crl = await signer.createCrl({
  issuer: ca.internalCa.dn,
  thisUpdate,
  nextUpdate,
  entries: revokedCerts.map((revokedCert) => {
    // ...
  })
});

Source:

https://github.com/Infisical/infisical/blob/v0.167.6/backend/src/services/certificate-authority/certificate-authority-fns.ts

In particular, the following line appears relevant:

issuer: ca.internalCa.dn,

It appears that the CRL issuer is constructed from the CA Distinguished Name stored in Infisical's internal metadata.

Our suspicion is that this stored DN, or its serialization when creating the CRL, does not preserve the RDN ordering of the actual signed Intermediate CA certificate.

This might not be visible when Infisical generates and signs the CA certificate itself, but it becomes relevant when an Intermediate CA certificate is signed by an external PKI such as Microsoft AD CS.

We have not confirmed whether the ordering changes when storing ca.internalCa.dn or when serializing it through signer.createCrl().

Could the CRL generation logic derive the Issuer Name directly from the actual signed Intermediate CA certificate, preserving the ASN.1 representation or equivalent correct X.509 Name semantics, instead of reconstructing it from the stored DN string?

Impact

This issue affects environments that use Infisical as an Intermediate CA beneath an existing enterprise PKI.

In our case, the problem directly affects a .NET application using MailKit to establish a TLS connection to an internal SMTP server.

The server presents a valid certificate and chain, but the client refuses the TLS connection because revocation status cannot be established.

The original application error is:

An error occurred while attempting to establish an SSL or TLS connection.

The server's SSL certificate could not be validated
for the following reasons:

The server certificate has the following errors:
- The revocation function was unable to check revocation
  for the certificate.
- The revocation function was unable to check revocation
  because the revocation server was offline.

These messages are misleading in this particular case because the CRL is reachable.

The actual issue appears to be the invalid association between the CRL Issuer DN and the Intermediate CA Subject DN.

The practical consequences include:

TLS connection failures in applications requiring certificate revocation validation.

Failed SMTP submissions from .NET applications.

Inability to validate Infisical-issued certificates through standard Windows revocation checking.

OpenSSL CRL verification failures.

Potential pressure to disable certificate revocation checking as a workaround, which reduces security.

The issue is particularly relevant to enterprise PKI integration scenarios where Infisical is used beneath an externally managed Root CA.

Workarounds

We have identified two possible temporary workarounds:

Using a different TLS endpoint with a publicly trusted certificate chain.

Disabling revocation checking in the affected .NET client application.

Neither addresses the underlying Infisical CRL generation issue.

The second workaround is undesirable because it disables revocation validation and may allow certificates that have been revoked to continue being accepted.

We would strongly prefer to preserve normal certificate validation and revocation checking.

Suggested Fix

Please investigate how Distinguished Names are stored and serialized for externally signed Intermediate CAs, particularly during CRL generation.

The CRL Issuer DN should match the Subject DN from the actual signed Intermediate CA certificate.

Ideally, the fix should:

Preserve the correct ASN.1 X.509 Name representation of the signed CA certificate.

Avoid changing the RDN ordering during CRL generation.

Ensure CRLs generated for externally signed Intermediate CAs can be validated with OpenSSL and the Windows certificate chain engine.

Work with existing Intermediate CAs without requiring users to recreate or reissue their CA certificates.

Include a regression test using an Intermediate CA whose certificate was externally signed with a multi-attribute Distinguished Name in an ordering different from Infisical's internal DN serialization.

A useful regression test would compare the DER-encoded or correctly normalized X.509 Name of the actual CA certificate's Subject against the generated CRL's Issuer Name.

It should additionally verify the resulting CRL against that CA certificate using an independent X.509 implementation such as OpenSSL.

Additional Notes

The certificate chain validates successfully when revocation checking is disabled.

The Root CA and Intermediate CA are trusted by Windows.

The certificate's Subject Alternative Name is correct.

The server sends the certificate chain.

The CRL can be downloaded successfully over HTTPS.

The CRL is correctly parsed by both OpenSSL and Windows CertUtil.

The issue is reproducible using a freshly generated CRL after updating Infisical.

No changes to the mail server's TLS configuration are required to reproduce the issue with the certificate and CRL files alone.

No private keys, internal hostnames, infrastructure addresses, or organization-identifying information are included in this report.

If helpful, we can provide additional anonymized diagnostic output or perform further tests to isolate the DN serialization issue.

Thank you for looking into this. This appears to be an interoperability issue affecting Infisical Intermediate CAs integrated with existing enterprise PKI infrastructures.

comment.body: Thanks so much for the detailed write up and repro, it made this really easy to follow. I opened #9227, which takes the CRL issuer from the CA certificate's own subject instead of the stored DN, and rebuilds the CRL when a certificate is imported. Would love to hear if it fits what you're seeing!

issue.title: feat(review): review each commit of a PR separately
issue.body:
With per commit review turned on by the host, `/review` reviews each commit of a PR on its own diff and commit message, instead of only the combined diff.

Closes #4470. It is opt in and host only. The commit messages piece was split out into #4603, as suggested, and that has now landed on `main`.

**What this code is for**

`PRReviewer.run()` in `pr_agent/commands/pr_reviewer.py` handles `/review`. It asks the git provider for the PR diff, renders `pr_reviewer_prompts.toml` with that diff, makes one model call (or a few when chunking), and publishes one review comment.

**Before this PR**

A maintainer on GitLab has an MR with 4 commits, each with a message that explains one change, and comments `/review`.

1. `PRReviewer.run()` asks `GitLabProvider.get_diff_files()` for the diff of the whole MR.
2. The prompt gets that combined diff, plus the title and description.
3. The model returns findings with file and line, but nothing says which commit a finding belongs to.
4. One review comment for the whole MR. The maintainer has to work out by hand which of the 4 commits needs the fixup.

**After this PR**

Same maintainer, same MR, with `per_commit_review = true` in the host config or `.pr_agent.toml`.

1. `PRReviewer.run()` sees `per_commit_review` and calls `_run_per_commit()`.
2. `get_pr_commits()` returns the 4 commits, oldest first, with their parents, read fresh from the provider on every run. Merge commits are dropped here without loading them. `_commit_review_records()` reads the commits already reviewed from hidden markers in PR-Agent's own comments. For each commit not already listed by SHA, `set_commit_review_scope()` loads its files once and returns a fingerprint of its own patch, and only commits whose fingerprint is not recorded are kept. On the first run there are no markers, so all 4 are kept.
3. For each commit, `set_commit_review_scope()` scopes the diff to that commit against its parent, and `commit_under_review` puts its message (clipped to `max_commits_tokens`) in the prompt, between random markers made fresh for each run. `commit_messages_str` is cleared, so the prompt does not also list every other commit's message.
4. `_run_review()` runs once per commit and publishes one comment that names and links the commit. It uses the incremental review header, so it never replaces the persistent full review.
5. A commit with no findings gets no comment when `pr_reviewer.publish_output_no_suggestions = false`. With `inline_key_issues = true`, findings land inline on that commit's own diff.
6. 4 comments, one per commit, each with a `<!-- pr-agent:reviewed-commit <fingerprint> <sha> -->` line two lines below the hidden `<!-- pr-agent:review:incremental -->` identity. On the next push with 1 new commit, only that commit is reviewed. Without the setting, `/review` takes exactly the old path.

**The diagram**

```mermaid
flowchart LR

classDef box fill:#eef1ff,stroke:#4c5bd4,color:#111827
classDef bad fill:#ffd6d6,stroke:#cc0000,color:#111827,stroke-width:3px
classDef good fill:#c8f0c8,stroke:#008800,color:#111827,stroke-width:3px

subgraph BEFORE["BEFORE: 1 review for 4 commits"]
direction TB
  B1["Maintainer comments /review"] --> B2["PRReviewer.run"]
  B2 --> B3["get_diff_files for the whole MR"]
  B3 --> B4{"one prompt, combined diff"}
  B4 -->|"findings not tied to a commit"| B5["1 comment for the whole MR"]
  B4 -->|"per_commit_review off"| B6["same as today"]
end

subgraph AFTER["AFTER: 1 review per commit"]
direction TB
  A1["Maintainer comments /review"] --> A2["PRReviewer.run"]
  A2 --> A3["get_pr_commits"]
  A3 --> A4{"THE CHANGE: per_commit_review on"}
  A4 -->|"each commit: own diff and message"| A5["1 comment per commit, linked"]
  A4 -->|"setting off or provider unsupported"| A6["whole PR review, as today"]
end

B1 ~~~ A1

class B1,B2,B3,B6 box
class A1,A2,A3,A6 box
class B4,B5 bad
class A4,A5 good

linkStyle 3 stroke:#cc0000,stroke-width:5px
linkStyle 8 stroke:#008800,stroke-width:5px

style BEFORE fill:#fff5f5,stroke:#cc0000,color:#111827
style AFTER fill:#f3fff3,stroke:#008800,color:#111827
```

**The change**

* `PRReviewer.run()` now branches on `per_commit_review` into `_run_per_commit()`, and the old body moved into `_run_review()` unchanged apart from the commit header and the checks below.
* `GitProvider` gets `get_pr_commits()` (returns `None` by default, so other providers fall back to a whole PR review with a notice) and `set_commit_review_scope()`. GitHub and GitLab implement both on top of the existing incremental diff path. On GitHub, new side file contents are read at the commit when a head SHA is set.
* `_run_per_commit()` reviews only commits whose fingerprint is not recorded, so a plain `/review` and the default `push_commands` no longer review every commit again on each push (454174f1, 40cb6ee2, b52fbf25, bf4dd1b6, 9b159195). `commit_patch_fingerprint()` in `git_provider.py` hashes each file's name and patch with the `@@ -a,b +c,d @@` numbers removed, so a rebase onto `main` that leaves a commit's own patch alone does not review it again, while an amend or `--autosquash` fixup does. On GitLab, when a file's diff comes back empty (collapsed, too large or binary), the commit SHA is mixed into the fingerprint so two different commits never share one; such a commit is reviewed again after a rebase. A commit is recorded only after its review succeeds, including when every file was filtered out: `_run_review()` puts the marker line two lines below the comment's hidden incremental review identity, and a commit that gets no comment (no findings with `publish_output_no_suggestions = false`) goes into one record comment that starts with `<!-- pr-agent:review:commits -->` and is edited in place through `publish_persistent_comment_full()`. With default settings and no merge commits, no record comment is created. Before writing, the record is read again and merged, trimmed to commits still in the PR, and cut from the oldest end if it would pass the 65000 character comment limit. Markers count only at those fixed lines and only in comments `is_comment_authored_by_pr_agent()` confirms. A marker in a comment confirmed as someone else's is ignored. Markers are found by that hidden identity rather than the visible heading, so changing `review_heading` never reviews commits again. When comment authorship cannot be checked for the run, or marker comments exist but none can be confirmed and the author of at least one cannot be verified (for example a GitHub App whose login cannot be resolved), the run falls back to one whole PR review with a notice instead of reviewing every commit on each push. Each commit's files are loaded once per run and reused for its review; a commit whose patch is already recorded under another SHA (a rebase) is recorded under the new SHA too, and a commit with no changes of its own is recorded, so neither is loaded again. A failed commit is not recorded, so the next run retries it; the record counts failed attempts, and automatic runs stop after `PER_COMMIT_MAX_AUTO_ATTEMPTS` (3) while a manual `/review` always retries. Selection does not use commit dates, so a commit authored before the last review but pushed after it is still reviewed. If the comments cannot be read, the run fails with the usual failure comment instead of reviewing every commit. The `-i` lookup and its `minimal_*_for_incremental_review` thresholds are not used here, so a manual `/review` never stops silently. `docs/docs/commands/review.md` says so, and also says that if PR-Agent's comments are removed, the next run reviews every commit again unless `max_commits_per_review` is set (93cb7440).
* The commit message block opens and closes with `{{ commit_message_begin }}` and `{{ commit_message_end }}` from `prompt_boundary_markers("COMMIT_MESSAGE")` (the helper #4603 added to `pr_agent/algo/artifacts.py`), so a commit message containing `<<<COMMIT_MESSAGE_END>>>` cannot close the block early. It sits right above #4603's `commit_messages_str` block, which keeps its own `COMMIT_MESSAGES` markers.
* `_should_publish_review_no_suggestions()` checks the parsed findings for a commit review, so a commit where the model returned nothing or prose stays quiet with `publish_output_no_suggestions = false`.
* `per_commit_review` and `max_commits_per_review` are in the `pr_reviewer` entry of `CLI_HOST_ONLY_KEYS_BY_SECTION` and `PER_DIRECTORY_HOST_ONLY_KEYS_BY_SECTION`, so `/review --pr_reviewer.per_commit_review=true` in a comment is rejected.
* `max_commits_per_review` defaults to 0 (no limit). When more commits than the cap are not reviewed yet, the whole PR is reviewed once with a notice, and after that review succeeds all its commits are recorded, so the next push goes back to one review per new commit. GitHub lists at most 250 commits per PR, so a PR with more is reviewed as a whole with a notice.
* Merge commits, root commits and empty commits are skipped. One failing commit does not stop the rest; the run is marked failed afterwards.
* Upstream `main` is merged in with merge commits (181edc4c, 9723af3a), not a rebase, so no history is rewritten. Conflicts: `convert_to_markdown_v2()` keeps main's `get_bot_display_name()` next to the commit header, `CLI_HOST_ONLY_KEYS_BY_SECTION` keeps main's new `pr_reviewer` keys plus ours, and the key count in `test_config_reference.py` is main's 319 plus our 2. After #4798, `run()` no longer checks `is_answer`, and the tests set `config.is_auto_command`. After #4838 renamed `pr_agent/tools` to `pr_agent/commands`, the tests import from `pr_agent.commands` and the config links point at `../commands/review.md` (ed7715a5). `_prepare_code_suggestions()` on GitHub skips `validate_comments_inside_hunks()` while a commit scope is set, so a finding outside that commit's diff stays in the commit's summary instead of moving to a nearby line. `pytest tests/unittest` on 912963d8: 17692 passed, 34 skipped. `ruff check`: clean.

**What changes for a user**

* Nothing unless the host turns on `per_commit_review`. Default `/review` is unchanged.
* With it on: one model call per reviewed commit. The first run reviews every commit, and later runs review only new commits or commits whose own changes changed, so `-i` is no longer needed in `push_commands`.
* Each commit's review sees only that commit's diff, so it can flag something a later commit fixes, or miss a helper added in an earlier commit.
* Only GitHub and GitLab support it. Other providers get the usual whole PR review with a one line notice.

comment.body: Hi all, hope you're doing well! `main` moved quite a bit again, so I merged it back in e37d7105 to keep this conflict free while it's on hold. The per commit block still sits next to the commit messages block from #4603, and the unit suite, ruff and `pre-commit` pass locally. @IsmaelMartinez, now that #4603 is in, has it changed how you see the per commit question? I'm happy to park this until you've had a chance to compare them, or close it if the commit messages turn out to be enough. What does everyone think?

issue.title: fix(cli): deploy hangs forever when an AWS call gets no response
issue.body:
A deploy that got no answer from AWS used to wait until the job was killed, and now each silent call is dropped after 5 minutes and retried.

**What this code is for**

`sdkRequestHandler` in `packages/@aws-cdk/toolkit-lib/lib/api/aws-auth/awscli-compatible.ts` builds the HTTP settings that every AWS SDK client in the CLI and in the toolkit library uses. Both `packages/aws-cdk/lib/cli/cli.ts` (with the proxy agent, if any) and `Toolkit.sdkProvider` in `toolkit.ts` (with `sdkConfig.httpOptions.agent`, if any) call it, and the result is passed to every client next to a `ConfiguredRetryStrategy` that retries timeouts and other network errors. The one exception after this PR is `invokeCommand` in `SDK.lambda()` in `sdk.ts`, which uses a longer idle timeout.

**Before this PR**

A GitHub Actions job runs `cdk deploy`, and the connection under one `DescribeStacks` call goes silent after the request was sent, as described in #2097.

1. The CloudFormation client sends `DescribeStacks` through `NodeHttpHandler` with `connectionTimeout: 10000` and `requestTimeout: 300000`.
2. The connection was already open, so `connectionTimeout` never applies.
3. After 300000 ms the `requestTimeout` passes. `throwOnRequestTimeout` is not set, so Smithy only logs `[WARN] a request has exceeded the configured 300000 ms requestTimeout`.
4. The request is never failed, so `ConfiguredRetryStrategy` never sees an error and never retries.
5. The CLI waits on that same request with no further output. In the report on #2097 that was almost 6 hours, until the GitHub job timeout cancelled it. Against a local server that accepts and never replies, I saw the same thing on `main`: one connection, the warning at 300 s, and still waiting at 330 s.

**After this PR**

Same job, same silent `DescribeStacks` call.

1. Same as above, but the settings now also carry `socketTimeout: 300000`.
2. Once no data has moved in either direction for 300 seconds, Smithy destroys the request and rejects it with a `TimeoutError`.
3. `ConfiguredRetryStrategy` treats `TimeoutError` as a temporary error and sends the call again on a new connection.
4. If the new connection answers, the deploy carries on. If every attempt stays silent, the command fails with that `TimeoutError` instead of waiting. There are 7 attempts in total, so that is about 35 minutes plus the short retry delays. Against the same silent local server with a 60 s value, I saw the call retried on connections 2 to 7 and then failed at about 467 s, which is the same path with a shorter timer.
5. A slow call that keeps sending or receiving data, such as a large asset upload, never goes 300 seconds without data, so it is not cut off.
6. A hotswap of a `BucketDeployment` invokes its Lambda function synchronously, and Lambda sends nothing back until the function returns, which can take up to 15 minutes. `Invoke` therefore gets `socketTimeout: 960000`, which covers that maximum plus cold start init, so a long `s3 sync` is never dropped and started again while it is still running.

**The diagram**

```mermaid
flowchart LR

classDef box fill:#eef1ff,stroke:#4c5bd4,color:#111827
classDef bad fill:#ffd6d6,stroke:#cc0000,color:#111827,stroke-width:3px
classDef good fill:#c8f0c8,stroke:#008800,color:#111827,stroke-width:3px

subgraph BEFORE["BEFORE: waits until the job is killed, 1 connection"]
direction TB

```

**The change**

- `sdkRequestHandler` now returns `socketTimeout: 300000` next to the existing `connectionTimeout` and `requestTimeout`. This is the fix. I reused the 300 seconds that `requestTimeout` already has, because the Smithy docs for `throwOnRequestTimeout` say `requestTimeout` "was for a long time incorrectly being set as a socket idle timeout". So the CLI already ran with a 5 minute idle timeout that threw for years, and this brings that behavior back on purpose.
- `SDK.lambda()` in `sdk.ts` sends `Invoke` through a second client, created on the first invoke, with `socketTimeout: 960000` and every other setting unchanged. If the caller already set `socketTimeout` to 0 (no timeout) or to something longer, `Invoke` keeps that value. The other Lambda calls, such as `UpdateFunctionCode` and the hotswap waiters, keep the shared 300 s value, so a silent one of those is not held for 16 minutes per attempt. The hotswap of a `BucketDeployment` calls `Invoke` synchronously and the function may run for the full 15 minutes, so a shorter idle timeout would drop it and the retries would start overlapping `s3 sync --delete` runs.
- `RequestHandlerSettings` in `base-credentials.ts` gets an optional `socketTimeout` field, so the value type checks and a custom `IBaseCredentialsProvider` receives it in `clientConfig.requestHandler` too.
- `requestTimeout` and its warning are left as they are. I did not turn on `throwOnRequestTimeout`, because that timer runs from the start of the request until the response headers arrive, so it would fail a healthy upload that takes longer than 5 minutes. @JimNero009 pointed this out in the issue, and their suggestion of a `socketTimeout` is what this PR follows. Thank you for the very clear report and reproduction.
- Tests in `awscli-compatible.test.ts`: one checks the settings `sdkRequestHandler` returns, including the agent on both `httpAgent` and `httpsAgent`, and fails without this change. Two more run a real `STSClient` against a local TCP server with a 1 s `socketTimeout`. To be honest about what these two prove: they pass on `main` too, because they check how Smithy handles `socketTimeout` rather than this change. I kept them as a guard in case a future Smithy version changes that behavior, but I am very happy to drop them if you would rather not have a TCP server in a unit suite: a server that never answers gets a second connection and the call rejects with `TimeoutError`; a server that sends its whole response, headers included, in small pieces every 50 ms still succeeds on one connection. That second test fails if the settings use `requestTimeout` with `throwOnRequestTimeout` instead, which is why I went with `socketTimeout`.
- Tests in `sdk.test.ts`: one checks that `invokeCommand` is sent through a client with `socketTimeout: 960000` and the other settings unchanged, and fails without this change; four check that a disabled or longer caller value is kept and a shorter or unset one is raised to 960000; one checks the `Invoke` client is created only on the first invoke; two check that other Lambda calls and the CloudFormation client still get the shared settings.

I would really value your view on a few choices, and I am happy to change any of them:

- 300 seconds restores the old behavior. Would you prefer something shorter, such as the 60 to 120 seconds the issue suggested? If so, I would be glad to check the other clients for calls that can stay silent that long, the way the Lambda one does.
- The issue also asks for these timeouts to be configurable. I left that out to keep this small, but I can add it here or in a follow up if you think it belongs.
- The standalone `cdk-assets` CLI builds its clients in `cdk-assets-lib/lib/aws.ts` without any of these timeouts. Would you like the same change there as a separate PR?

**What changes for a user**

- A deploy, bootstrap or any other command whose AWS call goes silent no longer hangs. Each silent attempt is dropped after 5 minutes and retried.
- If AWS never answers at all, the command now fails with a `TimeoutError` after the existing retries, about 35 minutes, instead of running until the CI job is killed.
- Calls that answer normally, and slow calls that keep moving data such as large asset uploads, behave exactly as before.
- `cdk deploy --hotswap` and `cdk watch` with a `BucketDeployment` that takes many minutes keep working, because `Invoke` waits up to 16 minutes.
- A call that changes state, such as `ExecuteChangeSet` or `Invoke`, is now retried after a silent timeout instead of hanging. If AWS did process the first attempt, the retry can fail with a clearer error such as an existing change set. This is the same tradeoff the SDK already makes for a reset connection.
- Proxy users are covered, because the proxy agent goes through the same `sdkRequestHandler`.
- The `requestTimeout` warning after 5 minutes still appears for very long uploads, as it does today.

Fixes #2097

issue.title: files and base64 images get copied into every subagent checkpoint
issue.body:
We run deepagents 1.11.1 (JS) in prod with PostgresSaver and the default StateBackend. Most of our DB growth comes from checkpoint blobs, and digging into the biggest threads we found two patterns:

- Tool results over 80k chars go to /large_tool_results/ in the `files` state. The whole `files` map is passed to each subagent, comes back as a full write, and gets copied into every parallel tool call Send. On one thread, 30 MB of actual files ended up as ~1.7 GB in checkpoints.
- Images read with read_file are stored inline as base64 and get stored again at each subagent step. One thread had 3 PNGs stored 205 times.

Is that expected? Two questions:
1. Does `files` need to go to subagents at all? Could it be left out of the subagent state?
2. What do you recommend in prod to keep large tool results and images out of the graph state? We looked at offloadBinaryContent (1.14.2+), but from what we understand it needs a non-state route and doesn't touch image_url data URLs. Did we get that right?

DeltaChannel would probably help too, I left a comment on #788.

issue.title: Reuse AudioContext across WebAudioAdapter setup calls

labels.name: user-4b3cdbaf/repo-7293fba9
labels.description: Issues and PRs related to the `@elevenlabs/client` package.

labels.name: repo-3c882c4e
labels.description: Code refactoring or restructuring

issue.body:
## Problem

`WebAudioAdapter.setupOutputAnalysis()` creates a new `AudioContext` (and reloads the audio worklet module) every time it's called. If the agent reconnects and republishes a track, `TrackSubscribed` fires again, calling `setupAudioCapture` → `setupOutputAnalysis`, which creates a second `AudioContext` without closing the first — leaking it.

The same pattern exists in `setupInputAnalysis`.

## Proposed solution

Reuse the `AudioContext` across calls instead of closing and recreating it:

- Keep the `AudioContext` alive for the lifetime of the adapter
- On re-call, disconnect old nodes and create new ones on the existing context
- The worklet module is already loaded on the context, so subsequent calls skip the expensive `loadRawAudioProcessor()` await
- Only close the context in `cleanup()`

This would also simplify the class by removing the need for cleanup-on-re-call guards.

## Context

Identified during the platform isolation review (#784). The current code works for the common single-call case, but leaks resources in reconnection scenarios.

## Files

- `packages/client/src/platform/web/webAudioAdapter.ts` — `setupOutputAnalysis()` and `setupInputAnalysis()`

issue.title: fix(functions): run the SDK bin entry when no .bin shim exists
issue.body:
### Description

Deploying functions on Windows with Bun stopped because the CLI could not find the Functions SDK, and now it runs the SDK's own declared entry file instead.

**What this code is for**

`findFunctionsBinary()` in `src/deploy/functions/runtimes/node/index.ts` finds the program inside the `firebase-functions` package that reads a codebase and reports its functions. `spawnFunctionsProcess()` runs that program during `firebase deploy` and in the emulator, and the CLI builds the deploy plan from what it reports.

**Before this PR**

A developer on Windows installs dependencies with `bun install` and runs `firebase deploy --only functions`, as @philemonkipngetich described in #11386.

1. `spawnFunctionsProcess()` calls `findFunctionsBinary()`.
2. `require.resolve("firebase-functions", { paths: [this.sourceDir] })` succeeds and points into Bun's store, `node_modules/.bun/firebase-functions@7.4.0+<hash>/node_modules/firebase-functions/lib/v2/index.js`.
3. The loop checks four `node_modules` folders for a file named exactly `.bin/firebase-functions`.
4. Bun on Windows only wrote `.bin/firebase-functions.exe` and `.bin/firebase-functions.bunx`, so `fileExistsSync()` is false in all four folders.
5. The CLI throws `Failed to find location of Firebase Functions SDK` and the deploy stops.

**After this PR**

Same developer, same command. Same as above through step 4.

5. `findSdkBinEntry(sdkPath)` walks up from the resolved file to the `package.json` whose `name` is `firebase-functions`.
6. It reads the `bin` field, `{ "firebase-functions": "lib/bin/firebase-functions.js" }`, joins it to that folder, and checks the file is really there.
7. `findFunctionsBinary()` returns `[this.bin, "<sdk folder>/lib/bin/firebase-functions.js"]`, where `this.bin` is the node binary the CLI already resolved.
8. `spawnFunctionsProcess()` runs that node with `<that file> <sourceDir>`, the same program the `.bin` file would have run, and the deploy continues.

A developer using npm still has `.bin/firebase-functions`, so step 3 finds it and nothing else runs.

**The diagram**

```mermaid
flowchart LR

classDef box fill:#eef1ff,stroke:#4c5bd4,color:#111827
classDef bad fill:#ffd6d6,stroke:#cc0000,color:#111827,stroke-width:3px
classDef good fill:#c8f0c8,stroke:#008800,color:#111827,stroke-width:3px

subgraph BEFORE["BEFORE: deploy stops with an error"]
direction TB
  B1["firebase deploy on Windows with Bun"] --> B2["findFunctionsBinary()"]
  B2 --> B3["check 4 node_modules/.bin folders"]
  B3 --> B4{"file named .bin/firebase-functions?"}
  B4 -->|"only .exe and .bunx exist"| B5["Failed to find location of Firebase Functions SDK"]
  B4 -->|"npm, file found"| B6["spawn the .bin file"]
end

subgraph AFTER["AFTER: deploy continues"]
direction TB
  A1["firebase deploy on Windows with Bun"] --> A2["findFunctionsBinary()"]
  A2 --> A3["check 4 node_modules/.bin folders"]
  A3 --> A4{"THE CHANGE: no file, read bin from SDK package.json"}
  A4 -->|"only .exe and .bunx exist"| A5["spawn node lib/bin/firebase-functions.js"]
  A4 -->|"npm, file found"| A6["spawn the .bin file, as today"]
end

B1 ~~~ A1

class B1,B2,B3,B6 box
class A1,A2,A3,A6 box
class B4,B5 bad
class A4,A5 good

linkStyle 3 stroke:#cc0000,stroke-width:5px
linkStyle 8 stroke:#008800,stroke-width:5px

style BEFORE fill:#fff5f5,stroke:#cc0000,color:#111827
style AFTER fill:#f3fff3,stroke:#008800,color:#111827
```

**The change**

- The fix: after the existing `.bin` loop finds nothing, a new function `findSdkBinEntry(sdkPath)` reads the `bin` field from the SDK's own `package.json`. It accepts both forms npm allows, a single path string or an object keyed by `firebase-functions`. If there is an entry and the file exists, `findFunctionsBinary()` returns `[this.bin, entry]`; otherwise the same `FirebaseError` as before is thrown, instead of a later `MODULE_NOT_FOUND`.
- `findFunctionsBinary()` now returns the command and its leading arguments as an array, and `spawnFunctionsProcess()` spreads it into `spawn(command, [...args, this.sourceDir])`.
- It finds the `package.json` by walking up from the resolved file and checking its `name`, because `firebase-functions` does not list `./package.json` in its `exports`, so `require.resolve("firebase-functions/package.json")` throws.
- I kept the `.bin` lookup first so setups that work today run exactly the same command. I would really value your view on the order: would you prefer the `package.json` entry to be tried first, or kept as the fallback like this?
- `node` is `this.bin`, which comes from `getNodeBinary()` (the local `node_modules/node` or `process.execPath`), so it does not depend on `node` being on `PATH`. Reading `this.bin` also logs `Using node@N from host.` (or the version mismatch warning) during deploy, and only on this fallback path; setups that find the `.bin` file see no new log line.
- A `package.json` on the way up that cannot be read or parsed is logged at debug level and skipped, so it never stops the deploy.
- `findSdkBinEntry` is exported with `@internal` so the spec tests it directly.
- Added a `CHANGELOG.md` line.

**What changes for a user**

- Deploying and emulating functions works on Windows when Bun installs dependencies, including Bun's isolated `node_modules/.bun` store.
- It also works for any other layout where the SDK resolves but no `.bin/firebase-functions` file exists in the four folders checked.
- npm, Yarn and pnpm setups that already have the `.bin` file run the same command as before.
- If the SDK cannot be found at all, the error message is unchanged.

Thank you @philemonkipngetich for the very clear diagnosis in #11386. Your note that the SDK resolves but only `.exe` and `.bunx` shims exist is exactly what this builds on, and your workaround of running the declared `bin` entry with `node` is the same idea moved into the CLI.

### Scenarios Tested

- Added tests in `src/deploy/functions/runtimes/node/index.spec.ts` that build real folders in a temp directory: an npm layout with `.bin/firebase-functions`, a Bun store with only `.exe` and `.bunx`, a pnpm layout where the root `.bin` shim is absent (only `.cmd` and `.ps1`, since on Windows pnpm normally also writes the extensionless shim), a `bin` declared as a single path, an SDK with no `bin`, a `bin` pointing to a missing file, and a malformed `package.json` both above the entry point and at the SDK root. One more test runs `spawnFunctionsProcess()` against a bin file that prints its arguments and checks it receives exactly the source directory. Without the fix, the Bun, pnpm and single path cases fail with `Failed to find location of Firebase Functions SDK`.
- On macOS, installed `firebase-functions@7.4.0` with `bun install --linker isolated`, replaced the extensionless shim with `.exe` and `.bunx` files to match the Windows layout, and ran `Delegate.execAdmin()` from the built CLI. It exited 0 and wrote a `functions.yaml` listing the `hello` function. I do not have a Windows machine, so a run there would be very welcome.
- `npm run build`, `npx tsc --noEmit`, eslint and prettier on the changed files, and `npm run mocha:fast` (one failure in `src/frameworks/utils.spec.ts` that also happens without this change in my environment, since it runs `npm root`).

### Sample Commands

`firebase deploy --only functions`

Closes #11386

issue.title: [react] ConversationProvider: startSession() on mount never connects under React StrictMode
issue.body:
Hi! When a child of `ConversationProvider` calls `startSession()` on mount inside `<React.StrictMode>`, the session gets ended right after it starts and never comes back.

**What the provider is for**

`ConversationProvider` owns a single conversation and shares `startSession` / `endSession` with its children through `ConversationContext`, so any component in the tree can start or stop the call.

**Current behavior** (on main, b3bf0e4)

1. A child calls `startSession()` in `useEffect(..., [])`. `lockRef.current` is set to the pending start ([ConversationProvider.tsx:243](https://github.com/elevenlabs/packages/blob/b3bf0e4/packages/react/src/conversation/ConversationProvider.tsx#L243)).
2. StrictMode runs the simulated unmount. The provider cleanup ([:309-321](https://github.com/elevenlabs/packages/blob/b3bf0e4/packages/react/src/conversation/ConversationProvider.tsx#L309-L321)) sets `shouldEndRef` to true and chains `endSession` on the lock, but leaves `lockRef` set and doesn't bump `startSessionIdRef`.
3. On remount the child's effect calls `startSession()` again. It returns early at [:101](https://github.com/elevenlabs/packages/blob/b3bf0e4/packages/react/src/conversation/ConversationProvider.tsx#L101) because the lock is still there, so the reset of `shouldEndRef` at :105 never runs.
4. The first start resolves. `handleConversationCreated` (:174) and `handleConnect` (:183) bail on the flag, and the `.then` branch at :250-256 ends the conversation.
5. No session, and nothing starts it again.

**Expected behavior**

The session connects under StrictMode, the same way `useScribe` does since #1132.

**Minimal repro**

```tsx
function AutoStart() {
  const { startSession } = useContext(ConversationContext)!;
  useEffect(() => {
    startSession({ agentId: "agent_123" });
  }, []);
  return null;
}

render(
  <React.StrictMode>
    <ConversationProvider>
      <AutoStart />
    </ConversationProvider>
  </React.StrictMode>
);
```

I checked this with a vitest case in the style of `ConversationProvider.test.tsx`, with `Conversation.startSession` mocked:

* without StrictMode: 1 `startSession`, 0 `endSession`, conversation is set
* with StrictMode: 1 `startSession`, 2 `endSession`, conversation is null

```mermaid
sequenceDiagram
  participant Child
  participant Provider
  participant Client
  Child->>Provider: startSession() on mount
  Provider->>Client: start, lockRef set
  Note over Provider: StrictMode cleanup sets shouldEndRef, lockRef stays set
  Child->>Provider: startSession() on remount
  Provider-->>Child: returns early, lock still held
  Client-->>Provider: start resolves
  Provider->>Client: endSession() because shouldEndRef is true
  Note over Child,Client: no session
```

**Question**

#1132 handled this really nicely for `useScribe` (clearing the ref in cleanup at `scribe.ts:304`, plus the StrictMode test at `scribe.test.tsx:651`), thanks for that! Would you like the same approach here? Something like copying and clearing `lockRef` and `conversationRef` in cleanup, bumping `startSessionIdRef`, and ending the copied session.

Or would you rather it be handled inside #1014? @Enalmada, your PR is close to this area. From the diff it looks like the cleanup aborts the pending start but still leaves `lockRef` set until it settles, so I wasn't sure if it's meant to cover this case too. I may well be missing something, so happy to be corrected.

Glad to open a PR for whichever direction you prefer. The README doesn't mention StrictMode being unsupported, which is why I figured it's worth fixing.

issue.title: fix(telegram): add a deadline to polling getUpdates requests
issue.body:
In polling mode, an idle `getUpdates` request had no client side deadline. When the connection dropped without a reset (a network switch, suspend and resume, a middlebox dropping the flow), the request waited until the OS gave up on the socket, often 15 minutes or more, and the bot received nothing in that time.

Root cause: the only abort on `getUpdates` was the stop signal plus a timer that runs only while media group updates are pending.

**Change**

`getUpdates` now gets `AbortSignal.any([pollingAbortController.signal, AbortSignal.timeout(timeout * 1000 + 30_000)])`. The three abort reasons stay distinct by signal reason:

* Deadline: the signal aborts with a `TimeoutError`, `telegramFetch` turns it into a `NetworkError` with the message `Telegram getUpdates request timed out` (whether the stall was before headers or mid body), and the existing catch backs off and polls again.
* Stop: unchanged, an `AbortError` with `pollingActive` false returns from the loop.
* Media group collection: unchanged, an `AbortError` while collecting yields an empty batch.

`telegramFetch` also passes an `AbortError` raised while reading the body through as an abort, the same as one raised before headers, so stopping or collecting mid body is no longer logged as a parse error.

The grace is 30 seconds, the same as `TELEGRAM_FILE_TIMEOUT_MS` and the value the reporter runs in production, so a stalled poll recovers in about `timeout + 30s`. Happy to change it if you'd prefer something shorter. `getUpdates` is the only long poll in the adapter, and no other adapter shares this loop. `AbortSignal.any` needs Node 20.3, and `adapter-gmail` already uses it. The changeset notes that polling needs Node 20.3 or newer.

**Tests**

* A `getUpdates` that stalls before headers, then one that stalls mid body, until each deadline fires: the loop logs `Telegram getUpdates request timed out` for both, polls again, and delivers the next message. This test fails on `main`.
* A poll sent with `timeout: 0` because a media group is already due gets a 30_000ms deadline.
* Stopping during a poll stalled before headers or mid body returns cleanly without logging a failure.
* Existing media group, stop, and normal response polling tests pass unchanged.
* I also checked it against a local HTTP server that holds the first `getUpdates` socket open with real `fetch`: the poll failed at 30s with a `NetworkError` and the next poll delivered the message.

`pnpm check`, the Telegram typecheck, the Telegram tests (519) and the integration polling tests pass.

Fixes #1101

Thanks @antonio-antuan for the detailed report and the workaround, they made this easy to follow. Feedback on the grace value is very welcome.

comment.body:
Thanks so much @bensabic, this is such a thorough review! The smoke tests against a real server and the mutation run were really helpful to see. I pushed b07541e with:

* The timeout message: I applied your `telegramFetch` patch, so a stall before headers or mid body now logs `Telegram getUpdates request timed out` instead of a network or parse error. The deadline test now stalls once before headers and once mid body, and asserts that message for both. While in there, I also let an `AbortError` from the body read pass through as an abort, so `stopPolling()` or media group collection landing mid body isn't logged as a parse error. There's a small test for stopping at each stall point.
* The drain poll gap: there's a new test where a poll sent with `timeout: 0`, because a media group is already due, gets a 30_000ms deadline, so the `config.timeout` mutation now fails.

On the engines note: `adapter-gmail` also uses `AbortSignal.any` and declares `>=20` too, so I left `engines` as is and added a line to the changeset saying polling needs Node 20.3 or newer. Would you rather I bump it to `>=20.3` instead? Happy either way.

issue.title: fix(pubsub): respect batch limits when acks are added concurrently

labels.name: repo-86a251da
labels.description: Issues related to the Pub/Sub API.

issue.body:
When a subscriber acks or modAcks several messages at the same moment, one request could carry more messages than the configured batch limit, and now each request stays within it.

**What this code is for**

`MessageQueue` in `handwritten/pubsub/src/message-queues.ts` collects acks (`AckQueue`) and modAcks (`ModAckQueue`) and sends them to the server in batches. Every ack or modAck goes through `add()`, which is supposed to send the current batch first with `flush()` when adding one more message would reach `maxMessages` or `MAX_BATCH_BYTES`. `flush()` takes `this._requests` and replaces it with an empty array before its first `await`, then sends the batch it took.

**Before this PR**

An app sets `maxMessages: 1` and modAcks three messages at the same moment (the gist from @vienneraphael in #9303 does exactly this).

1. The first `add()` sees `this._requests.length + 1 >= maxMessages`, calls `flush()`, and stops at `await this.flush(reason)`.
2. The second and third `add()` run while the first is waiting. They see the same empty `this._requests`, pass the same `if`, and also stop at `await this.flush(reason)`.
3. All three flushes finish, and all three calls continue to `this._requests.push(...)`. Nobody checks the limit again.
4. The timer sends `this._requests` as one batch.
5. The server gets one `modifyAckDeadline` request with 3 ack IDs while `maxMessages` is 1. With `maxMessages: 2` and six messages the batches are `[1, 1, 1, 3]`, and the same thing happens to the byte limit.

**After this PR**

Same app, same three modAcks at the same moment.

1. The first `add()` sees the limit is reached and calls `flush()` without waiting for it. `flush()` has already taken the old batch by the time it returns its promise.
2. The first `add()` pushes its message into the new empty `this._requests` straight away, and only then waits for the flush and for its own response.
3. The second `add()` now sees one message in `this._requests`, so the `if` is true and it flushes that batch before pushing its own.
4. The third `add()` does the same.
5. The server gets three requests with 1 ack ID each. When the calls arrive one at a time, `add()` takes the same path as before, so those batches do not change.

**The diagram**

```mermaid
flowchart LR

classDef box fill:#eef1ff,stroke:#4c5bd4,color:#111827
classDef bad fill:#ffd6d6,stroke:#cc0000,color:#111827,stroke-width:3px
classDef good fill:#c8f0c8,stroke:#008800,color:#111827,stroke-width:3px

subgraph BEFORE["BEFORE: 1 request with 3 ack IDs, maxMessages 1"]
direction TB
  B1["3 modAcks at the same moment"] --> B2["add() checks this._requests"]
  B2 --> B3["limit reached, call flush()"]
  B3 --> B4{"await flush, then push"}
  B4 -->|"all 3 wake up and push"| B5["1 request with 3 ack IDs"]
  B4 -->|"one call at a time"| B6["1 ack ID per request"]
end

subgraph AFTER["AFTER: 3 requests with 1 ack ID each"]
direction TB
  A1["3 modAcks at the same moment"] --> A2["add() checks this._requests"]
  A2 --> A3["limit reached, call flush()"]
  A3 --> A4{"THE CHANGE: push, then await flush"}
  A4 -->|"next add() sees 1 message"| A5["3 requests with 1 ack ID"]
```

**The change**

In `MessageQueue.add()`, `await this.flush(reason)` becomes `flushed = this.flush(reason)`, and the method now ends with `await Promise.all([flushed, responsePromise.promise])` instead of `return responsePromise.promise`. The check, the start of the flush, and the push now happen together before `add()` waits on anything, so no other `add()` can run between them. This covers `maxMessages` and `MAX_BATCH_BYTES`, because both are checked in that same `if`.

`Promise.all` attaches to `responsePromise.promise` straight away, so if the message's own batch fails while the earlier flush is still running, the rejection still has a handler and reaches the caller as before.

Three tests in `test/message-queues.ts` call `add()` six times with `Promise.all` and check every sent batch: `maxMessages` of 1 and 2, and the byte limit. On `main` they fail with batch sizes `0,0,0,0,0,0,6`, `1,1,1,3`, and a batch of `783360` bytes. With the change, they pass, and so do the other 979 unit tests.

**What changes for a user**

- Acks and modAcks sent at the same moment now respect `maxMessages` and the byte limit. The reproduction from #9303 now gives `respectsLimit: true` for all six rows.
- When acks arrive one at a time, the batches are the same as before (`[0, 1, 0, 1, 0, 1]` for `AckQueue` and `[1, 1, 1]` for `ModAckQueue` at `maxMessages: 1`).
- `add()` still resolves only after the message is sent, and still waits for the flush it started.
- Out of scope: the empty `AckQueue` requests that @vienneraphael pointed out. They come from the existing `this._requests.length + 1 >= maxMessages` check, which flushes an empty batch when `maxMessages` is 1, and existing tests expect that flush. I left it alone so this PR only fixes the limit.

Thank you @vienneraphael for the very clear report and the gist. The numbered steps in the issue pointed straight at the `await`, and the table made the fix easy to check. I would really value the maintainers' view on two things:

1. Is starting the flush and pushing before the `await` the approach you prefer? The other option I looked at was checking the limit again in a loop after each `await`. With the current `+ 1 >=` check and `maxMessages: 1` that loop never ends, so I went with this one, but I am happy to change it.
2. Would you like the empty `AckQueue` requests handled here, or in a separate PR? That change would need two existing tests updated, so I wanted to ask first.

- [x] Make sure to open an issue as a bug/issue before writing your code! That way we can discuss the change, evaluate designs, and agree on the general idea
- [x] Ensure the tests and linter pass
- [x] Code coverage does not decrease (if any source code was changed)
- [x] Appropriate docs were updated (if necessary)

Fixes #9303 🦕

issue.title: fix(hooks): read SessionStart source to reset skill dedup
issue.body:
After `/clear` or a compaction, the plugin never forgot which skills it had already recorded for the session; this makes it start fresh at those moments, as intended.

**What this code is for**

`hooks/session-start-seen-skills.mjs` runs on every Claude Code `SessionStart` (the `startup|resume|clear|compact` matcher in `hooks/hooks.json`). Its job is to delete the session's `seen-skills` and `seen-context-chunks` files in the temp folder when the context window has just been wiped, so the plugin does not treat skills from the old context as still present. On Cursor it prints `{ env: { VERCEL_PLUGIN_SEEN_SKILLS: "" } }` and stops.

**Before this PR**

A developer runs `/clear` in a Claude Code session that already used the `nextjs` skill.

1. Claude Code calls the hook with `{"hook_event_name":"SessionStart","source":"clear","session_id":"..."}`, the shape in the [SessionStart input docs](https://code.claude.com/docs/en/hooks#sessionstart-input).
2. `main()` reads `input?.hook_event_name`, which is `"SessionStart"` on every call.
3. `CONTEXT_CLEARING_EVENTS.has("SessionStart")` is false, so `resetTriggered` is false.
4. `resetDedupStateForSession` never runs, and `vercel-plugin-<session>-seen-skills.d` still lists `nextjs` after the clear.

The tests passed anyway because the six fixtures sent `hook_event_name: "clear"` (and `"compact"`, `"startup"`), a payload Claude Code never sends.

**After this PR**

Same developer, same `/clear`.

1. Same payload as above.
2. `main()` reads `input?.source`, which is `"clear"`.
3. `CONTEXT_CLEARING_SOURCES.has("clear")` is true and `session_id` is not empty, so `resetTriggered` is true.
4. `removeAllSessionDedupArtifacts(sessionId)` deletes that session's `seen-skills` and `seen-context-chunks` files and folders, including the per agent ones.
5. On `startup` or `resume`, `source` is not in the set, so nothing is deleted.

**The diagram**

```mermaid
flowchart LR
```

**The change**

In `hooks/src/session-start-seen-skills.mts`, the input type gains `source?: string`, and the `if` that decides whether to reset now reads `input?.source` instead of `input?.hook_event_name`. The set is renamed `CONTEXT_CLEARING_SOURCES` and the debug log field is now `source`. The Cursor branch and the non empty `session_id` check are unchanged. `hooks/session-start-seen-skills.mjs` is rebuilt with `bun run build:hooks`, since the tests run the built file.

In `tests/session-start-seen-skills.test.ts`, the six fixtures now send `hook_event_name: "SessionStart"` with the matching `source`. New cases check that a clear leaves another session's files alone (including its per agent folder), and that nothing is deleted for `resume`, an unknown or missing `source`, the old `hook_event_name: "clear"` and `"compact"` payloads, a missing or empty `session_id`, and a Cursor payload. Eight of these fail on `main` and pass with the change. `bun run test` (typecheck plus 1288 tests), `bun run validate` and `bun run build:all` all pass.

This follows the plan @yuu-sugiyama laid out in the issue almost line for line, so the credit for finding it and for the list of cases goes to them. On their follow up about session ids that share a prefix with a scoped name: `session-end-cleanup.mts` already deletes by the same `vercel-plugin-<session>-` prefix on `SessionEnd`, and Claude Code session ids are UUIDs, so a different UUID cannot start with `<uuid>-`. The new test uses two UUIDs to check exactly that. Changing the file naming so the session and scope can never run together felt like a separate decision that belongs to you, so I left it out. Would you prefer that land first, or would you rather drop this reset path entirely? Happy to go either way.

**What changes for a user**

- After `/clear` or a compaction, the plugin starts the session's skill list fresh, so skills can be offered and counted again for the new context.
- `startup` and `resume` keep the list, same as before.
- Cursor output is unchanged.
- Only the current session's `seen-skills` and `seen-context-chunks` files are removed; other sessions' files stay.

Closes #169

issue.title: fix(jsii-pacmak): escape backslashes in .NET attribute strings
issue.body:
A library whose deprecation note contains a backslash could not be built for .NET at all, and now it builds and keeps the note exactly as written.

**What this code is for**

`DotNetRuntimeGenerator` in `packages/jsii-pacmak/lib/targets/dotnet/dotnetruntimegenerator.ts` writes the C# attributes that sit above every generated .NET class, method and property. `emitDeprecatedAttributeIfNecessary` writes `[System.Obsolete("...")]` with the text of the TypeScript `@deprecated` tag. `emitAttributesForClass`, `emitAttributesForMethod` and `emitAttributesForProperty` write `parametersJson`, `returnsJson` and `typeJson`, which the .NET runtime reads back with `JsonConvert.DeserializeObject` in `JsiiMethodAttribute` and `JsiiClassAttribute`.

**Before this PR**

A library author marks a method `@deprecated patterns like \d+ are not supported` (or `use the path C:\temp\`) and runs `jsii-pacmak --targets dotnet`.

1. `emitDeprecatedAttributeIfNecessary` takes `docs.deprecated`, turns `\n` into a space, and puts `\` in front of every `"`.
2. The backslash is copied as it is, so the file gets `[System.Obsolete("patterns like \d+ are not supported")]`.
3. C# reads `\d` as an escape sequence it does not know: `error CS1009: Unrecognized escape sequence`.
4. For a message ending in `\`, that backslash escapes the closing quote: `error CS1010: Newline in constant`.
5. `dotnet build` fails and no .nupkg is produced. I reproduced this on `main` with a small jsii library and the .NET 8 SDK: 8 compiler errors in `Thing.cs`, no package. This is the failure @rix0rrr hit with aws/aws-cdk#28737.
6. The same "quotes only" escaping feeds `parametersJson`. A parameter doc such as `e.g. "\d+"` first has every `\"` replaced by the word `test` (by `.replace(/\\{2}"/g, 'test')`), and the remaining `\d` reaches the runtime as JSON that Newtonsoft rejects: `Bad JSON escape sequence: \d`. The existing snapshot shows the `test` part today: the jsii-calc doc `(e.g: "${NOPE}"")` is stored as `(e.g: test${NOPE}testtest)`.

**After this PR**

Same author, same `@deprecated` text, same command.

1. `emitDeprecatedAttributeIfNecessary` still turns `\n` into a space, then passes the text to the new `toCSharpString`.
2. `toCSharpString` calls `JSON.stringify`, which escapes `\`, `"` and every control character with escapes that C# also accepts, then escapes U+0085, U+2028 and U+2029 as `\u0085`, `\u2028`, `\u2029`.
3. The file gets `[System.Obsolete("patterns like \\d+ are not supported")]` and `[System.Obsolete("use the path C:\\temp\\")]`.
4. `dotnet build` succeeds and produces `Mini.Backslash.1.0.0.nupkg`. Reading the attribute back with reflection gives the original message character for character.
5. `parametersJson`, `returnsJson` and `typeJson` go through the same `toCSharpString`, so the parameter doc reaches the runtime as `e.g. "\d+"` and Newtonsoft parses it.
6. A message with no backslash, control character or line separator produces exactly the same output as before: 477 of the 478 .NET snapshots are unchanged.

**The diagram**

```mermaid
flowchart LR

classDef box fill:#eef1ff,stroke:#4c5bd4,color:#111827
classDef bad fill:#ffd6d6,stroke:#cc0000,color:#111827,stroke-width:3px
classDef good fill:#c8f0c8,stroke:#008800,color:#111827,stroke-width:3px

subgraph BEFORE["BEFORE: 8 compiler errors, no package"]
direction TB
  B1["author writes @deprecated with a backslash"] --> B2["jsii-pacmak --targets dotnet"]
  B2 --> B3["emitDeprecatedAttributeIfNecessary"]
  B3 --> B4{"escape double quotes only"}
  B4 -->|"backslash copied as is"| B5["CS1009 or CS1010, build fails"]
  B4 -->|"no backslash in the text"| B6["builds as today"]
end

subgraph AFTER["AFTER: builds, message kept exactly"]
direction TB
  A1["author writes @deprecated with a backslash"] --> A2["jsii-pacmak --targets dotnet"]
  A2 --> A3["emitDeprecatedAttributeIfNecessary"]
  A3 --> A4{"THE CHANGE: toCSharpString"}
  A4 -->|"backslash becomes a C# escape"| A5["dotnet build succeeds, same message"]
  A4 -->|"no backslash in the text"| A6["same output as before"]
end

B1 ~~~ A1

style BEFORE fill:#fff5f5,stroke:#cc0000,color:#111827
style AFTER fill:#f3fff3,stroke:#008800,color:#111827
```

**The change**

- New function `toCSharpString(value)` at the bottom of `dotnetruntimegenerator.ts`: `JSON.stringify(value)` plus a `replace` for U+0085, U+2028 and U+2029. Every escape `JSON.stringify` can produce (`\"`, `\\`, `\b`, `\f`, `\n`, `\r`, `\t`, `\uXXXX`, including a lone surrogate) is also a valid C# escape, and those three characters are the only ones C# treats as a line break inside a string literal that JSON leaves raw.
- `emitDeprecatedAttributeIfNecessary` uses it for `[System.Obsolete(...)]`. This is the fix for this issue.
- `emitAttributesForClass`, `emitAttributesForMethod` and `emitAttributesForProperty` use it for `parametersJson`, `returnsJson` and `typeJson`, replacing the `.replace(/"/g, '\\"').replace(/\\{2}"/g, 'test')` chains. This is the same bug in the same file, and it changes one line of the .NET snapshot: the `ParamShadowsBuiltins` constructor docs now say `(e.g: \"${NOPE}\"\")` instead of `(e.g: test${NOPE}testtest)`.
- New test `test/targets/dotnet/dotnetruntimegenerator.test.ts`: messages with a trailing `\`, `\d`, quotes after a backslash, `\t`, `\r`, a control character, U+0085, U+2028, U+2029, a lone surrogate and an emoji, plus a parameter doc with quotes and `\d`. 7 of the 9 cases fail on `main`; the newline and emoji cases already worked and are there to show they still do.
- Other languages: I checked how the deprecation text is written for Java, Python and Go. Java writes a bare `@Deprecated` with the text only in Javadoc, Go writes it as a comment, and Python writes it into a docstring, so none of them place the text inside a string literal and none of them have this problem. .NET is the only target that needed a change.

Checks I ran: `jsii-pacmak` unit tests (everything except the Python tests, which could not install `mypy==2.4.0` on my local Python and so never reached the change), `yarn lint`, and `jsii-pacmak --targets dotnet --recurse` on `jsii-calc` with the .NET 8 SDK, which built all four packages.

I would really value your thoughts on two things, and I am glad to change either:

- I included the `parametersJson`, `returnsJson` and `typeJson` call sites because they had the same problem and one small function covers all five. If you would rather keep this PR to `[System.Obsolete]` only, I am happy to move those three into a separate PR.
- I kept the existing behavior of turning `\n` into a space in the `Obsolete` message. Now that every character can be escaped safely, it could keep the line breaks instead. I left that alone so existing messages do not change, but I am open to whichever you think reads better in the compiler warning.

**What changes for a user**

- A library with `\` anywhere in a `@deprecated` tag now builds for .NET. Before, the whole .NET build failed.
- The `Obsolete` message shown in Visual Studio and in compiler warnings is the exact text from the TypeScript tag.
- Parameter docs with quotes or backslashes are kept as written in `parametersJson`, and no longer cause a `JsonReaderException` when the runtime reads the attribute.
- Libraries whose docs have no backslashes, control characters or line separators get exactly the same generated code as before.
- Java, Python and Go output is unchanged.

Closes #4404

---

By submitting this pull request, I confirm that my contribution is made under the terms of the [Apache 2.0 license].

[Apache 2.0 license]: https://www.apache.org/licenses/LICENSE-2.0

This one is small: it escapes backslashes in the strings `jsii-pacmak` writes into .NET attributes, so a library whose deprecation note has a backslash builds again. GitHub says the branch is behind main, so I'm happy to merge main in whenever it helps. Would you like anything changed in the approach?

issue.title: fix: load custom cacheHandler in standalone apps built from a subfolder
issue.body:
Apps built from a subfolder with a custom cache handler answered 500 on every page under the standalone server, and this makes them load the handler and answer 200 again.

**What this code is for**

`RouteModule` in `packages/next/src/server/route-modules/route-module.ts` is the base class every page and route handler runs through at request time. Before it renders, it works out the project folder as `join(process.cwd(), relativeProjectDir)` and uses that folder to load the custom `cacheHandler` and `cacheHandlers`, to find instrumentation, and to look up the router server context. `relativeProjectDir` comes from the request meta that `next-server` sets, with the value baked in at build time (`__NEXT_RELATIVE_PROJECT_DIR`) as the fallback.

**Before this PR**

A developer builds the app in `web/` with `next build web`, `output: 'standalone'` and `cacheHandler: require.resolve('./web/cache-handler.js')`, then runs `node web/.next/standalone/web/server.js` and opens `/`.

1. `server.js` calls `process.chdir(__dirname)` and starts `next-server` with `dir = __dirname`.
2. `next-server` sets the `relativeProjectDir` request meta to `relative(process.cwd(), this.dir)`, which is `''` because both are the same folder.
3. `ensureInstrumentation` (run from `prepare`) reads `getRequestMeta(req, 'relativeProjectDir') || this.relativeProjectDir`.
4. `''` is falsy, so `||` swaps in the build time value `'web'`, the project folder becomes `<standalone>/web/web`, and `this.distDir` becomes `../.next` instead of `.next`.
5. `getIncrementalCache` imports the handler from `this.distDir`, one folder too high: `Cannot find module '<repo>/web/.next/standalone/cache-handler.js'`.
6. Every page answers 500. With `apps/site` it lands two folders too high.

**After this PR**

Same developer, same build, same `server.js`, same request to `/`.

1. Same as above through step 2: the request meta is `''`.
2. `ensureInstrumentation` (run from `prepare`) reads `getRequestMeta(req, 'relativeProjectDir') ?? this.relativeProjectDir`.
3. `''` is not `null` or `undefined`, so it is kept, the project folder is `<standalone>/web`, and `this.distDir` stays `.next`.
4. `getIncrementalCache` imports the handler from `<standalone>/web/cache-handler.js` and `/` answers 200.
5. When no server set the meta at all (it is `undefined`), `??` still falls back to the build time value, the same as before.

**The diagram**

```mermaid
flowchart LR

classDef bad fill:#ffd6d6,stroke:#cc0000,color:#111827,stroke-width:3px

end

direction TB

  A4 -->|"meta not set"| A6["build time folder is used, as before"]
end

B1 ~~~ A1

```

**The change**

All five reads of `getRequestMeta(req, 'relativeProjectDir') || this.relativeProjectDir` in `route-module.ts` now use `??` instead of `||`: in `getRouterServerContext`, `instrumentationOnRequestError`, `loadCustomCacheHandlers`, `getIncrementalCache` and `ensureInstrumentation`. The one in `ensureInstrumentation`, which turns the absolute `distDir` into a relative one, is the line that breaks the page; `getIncrementalCache` then imports the handler from that `distDir`. The one in `getRouterServerContext` matters too: `next-server` writes the router server context under `relative(process.cwd(), this.dir)`, which is the same `''`, so with `||` the lookup used the key `'web'` and missed it.

Huge thanks to @GabrielJesusS for the report. The bisect to #81944 (15.4.2-canary.15), the root cause walkthrough and the `??` suggestion are all theirs, and this PR just applies that suggestion to every place the same read happens. I reproduced it on `16.5.0-canary.30` with their repository before changing anything.

The new test in `test/production/standalone-mode/subfolder-cache-handler` builds the same app at the root, in `web` and in `apps/site`, starts the generated `server.js`, and checks that `/` and `/dynamic` answer 200 and that the custom handler was loaded. Without the change the `web` and `apps/site` cases fail with the same `Cannot find module` error from the issue, and the root case passes. With it all six pass with Turbopack and with webpack. The existing `test/production/standalone-mode/required-server-files` suites still pass with Turbopack (147 passed, 16 skipped).

I went with the smallest change here, but I would really value your opinion: would you prefer one small method on `RouteModule` that all five places call, so the fallback rule lives in one spot? Happy to switch to that, or to anything else you think fits better. I also noticed two spots that read `routeModule.relativeProjectDir` directly (the pages `optimizeCss` dist folder in `pages-handler.ts` and the app `renderOpts.dir` in `app-page-runtime.ts`); they do not cause a 500, so I left them out, but I am happy to fold them into the same helper if you think that is worth it.

**What changes for a user**

- Standalone apps built from a subfolder with a custom `cacheHandler` or `cacheHandlers` serve pages again instead of answering 500 on every request.
- Apps built at the root (where the build time value is already `''`) behave exactly as before.
- `next start web` behaves as before, because the meta there is the non empty `'web'`.
- Setups where no server sets the meta, such as minimal mode, still fall back to the build time value, as before.

Fixes #100839
