labels.name: repo-0e7dac05
labels.description: Extra attention is needed

issue.body:
#### Is your feature request related to a problem? Please describe.
<!-- A clear and concise description of what the problem is. E.g., I'm always
frustrated when ... -->
Knip reports a sizable possible-dead-code inventory, but entrypoint wiring and shared-type exports can be false positives. Do not treat all candidates as proven dead code.

#### Describe the solution you'd like
<!-- A clear and concise description of what you want to happen. -->
Configure real Vite/Jest/E2E entrypoints and fixture wiring, then remove or de-export only candidates confirmed to have no in-repository consumers.

#### Describe alternatives you've considered, if relevant.
<!-- A clear and concise description of any alternative solutions or features
you've considered. -->
Keep necessary shared/public exports and document intentional entrypoints rather than deleting based on tool output alone.

#### Additional context
<!-- Add any other context or screenshots about the feature request here. -->
Measured inventory: 15 potentially unused exported values and 62 exported types, plus 2 unused files and 2 devDependencies. These are candidates, not confirmed defects. Tested commit d3446e045960b5ebee4641aa70fdeb03af186587, PyRIT 1.2.0.dev0, offline Knip inventory. Evidence: files/evidence/round4/knip.txt; local path is not an attachment.

comment.body:
Hi @romanlutz, hope you're doing well! I really like that this was written up as candidates instead of a delete list, it made the triage easy to pick up. I ran Knip 5.88 against main (851d40f) and got almost the same inventory (2 files, 2 devDependencies, 16 exports, 60 types), then went through each group.

**False positives that config can fix**

- `jest-import-meta-transformer.ts` is loaded by path from ts-jest's `astTransformers`, which Knip's Jest plugin doesn't follow.
- `e2e/fixtures/numeric-controls.tsx` is loaded by a `<script>` tag in `e2e/fixtures/numeric-controls.html`, which `numeric-controls.spec.ts` opens. Knip only treats the root `index.html` as a Vite entry.
- The unlisted `python` binary comes from the `start`, `restart` and `stop` scripts.
- 59 of the 60 types are props or result types that are only used inside their own file.

With this `knip.json` in `frontend/`, all of those go away:

```json
{
  "$schema": "https://unpkg.com/knip@5/schema.json",
  "entry": ["jest-import-meta-transformer.ts", "e2e/fixtures/*.tsx"],
  "ignoreBinaries": ["python"],
  "ignoreExportsUsedInFile": { "interface": true, "type": true }
}
```

Small heads up if CI ever runs Knip: it loads `vite.config.ts`, which shells out to `python` for the compatibility stamp, and that script needs Python 3.11+ (`tomllib`). Setting `PYRIT_PYTHON` was enough for me.

**Exports**

- `MAX_SEED_SEARCH_LENGTH` (`seedExampleQuery.ts`) and `BASELINE_TECHNIQUE` (`scenarioConfigForm.ts`) look like duplication rather than dead code. `services/api.ts` and `ScenarioDetail.tsx` each define an identical local copy, so importing the shared one feels nicer than dropping the export, and the two can't drift apart.
- `techniqueSetOptionLabel` has no callers at all, and once it goes, `techniqueSetDisplayName` has none either.
- The other 12 are only used inside their own file, so dropping the `export` keyword looks safe.
- The one type left, `ScenarioRunEstimator` in `src/types/index.ts`, isn't referenced anywhere.

**devDependencies**

- `ts-node`: Jest 30 only falls back to it for `jest.config.ts` when Node can't strip types natively. With it moved aside, `jest --listTests` still loaded the config for me on Node 24, so it can go as long as CI's Node 22 resolves to 22.18 or newer. Otherwise an `ignoreDependencies` entry keeps it.
- `scheduler`: nothing in `src` or `e2e` imports it, and `react-dom` already brings in `scheduler ^0.28.0`. Was it added on purpose, maybe for the React 19 test setup?

Would a PR with the config plus these cleanups be useful, or would you rather keep the config change separate from the source edits?

issue.title: unassign-inactive-assignees never detects linked PRs, so assignees with open PRs get unassigned

labels.name: user-c64ca2e7/repo-78cd3e02
labels.description: Issues that need to be triaged by the triage automation.

labels.name: user-3ef72433/repo-27383830
labels.description: Issues related to Build infra, Release mgmt, Testing, Eval infra, Capacity, Quota mgmt

issue.body:
### What happened?

It looks like `unassign-inactive-assignees` never recognizes a linked PR, so contributors with an open, ready PR are getting unassigned after 7 days anyway.

First, thank you for all the work getting this workflow running again (#29298, #29326, #29609, #29770). It's been running cleanly since Oct 17, which is how I noticed this.

**What the workflow is for:** per the [file header](https://github.com/google-gemini/gemini-cli/blob/6814e00d6b148c3a1d57244d5d7040f7c541009d/.github/workflows/unassign-inactive-assignees.yml#L3-L10), it frees up "help wanted" issues whose assignee has no non draft PR (open and ready, or merged) linked within 7 days.

**Current behavior:**

1. The workflow loads the issue timeline and looks at `cross-referenced` events.
2. [Line 184](https://github.com/google-gemini/gemini-cli/blob/6814e00d6b148c3a1d57244d5d7040f7c541009d/.github/workflows/unassign-inactive-assignees.yml#L180-L189) skips any event where `event.source.type !== 'pull_request'`.
3. As far as I can tell, the REST timeline API reports cross referenced PRs as `source.type: "issue"`, with `source.issue.pull_request` set instead.
4. So every event is skipped, and the [readiness check](https://github.com/google-gemini/gemini-cli/blob/6814e00d6b148c3a1d57244d5d7040f7c541009d/.github/workflows/unassign-inactive-assignees.yml#L201-L216) (`pulls.get`, then `isReady`) never runs.
5. `linkedPRAuthorSet` stays empty, and every non privileged assignee past 7 days is removed, even with an open, ready PR that closes the issue.

**Minimal repro:**

```sh
gh api repos/google-gemini/gemini-cli/issues/28052/timeline --paginate \
  --jq '.[]|select(.event=="cross-referenced")|{t:.source.type, pr:(.source.issue.pull_request!=null), n:.source.issue.number}'
```

Every PR (28054, 28069, 28200, ...) comes back as `"t": "issue", "pr": true`.

The run logs seem to agree: the `PR ... state=` line never prints in runs 41291334509, 41186944793, 41030516312, 40478041559 or 39019643178. A couple of examples:

- Run 41030516312 (Oct 30) unassigned the assignee on #22589, while #29859 (open, not a draft, closes #22589) had been open since Oct 21.
- Run 39019643178 (Oct 17) unassigned people on #27400, #22590, #27406, #19638 and #29546, which all had open non draft PRs.

Where the PR check stops today:

```mermaid
flowchart TD
  A[cross-referenced event] --> B{source.type === 'pull_request'?}
  B -- "no (API sends 'issue')" --> X[skip event]
  B -- yes --> C[pulls.get]
  C --> D{isReady?}
  D -- yes --> E[keep assignee]
  D -- no --> F[may unassign]
  X --> F
```

**Suggested fix (one line):**

```diff
-                  event.source.type !== 'pull_request' ||
+                  !event.source.issue?.pull_request ||
```

I also noticed #28798 was closed on Oct 28 on the idea that open PRs keep assignments indefinitely. From the logs it seems to be the reverse right now, so it might be worth a second look once this is sorted.

### What did you expect to happen?

An assignee with an open, non draft PR linked to the issue (or a merged one) should stay assigned, as the file header describes. The `PR ... state=` log line should show up for each linked PR.

### Client information

<details>
<summary>Client Information</summary>

Not applicable, this is the `.github/workflows/unassign-inactive-assignees.yml` GitHub Actions workflow on `main` (6814e00).

</details>

### Login information

Not applicable.

### Anything else we need to know?

One question I wasn't sure about: which policy would you prefer here? The smallest fix above counts any cross referencing non draft PR. A stricter option would be to only count PRs that actually close the issue (`closingIssuesReferences` via GraphQL), so a passing mention can't keep an assignment alive. Happy to open a PR for whichever you think fits best, and of course I may be missing some context.

comment.body:
Hey @yuvrajangadsingh, thanks so much for adding this, and sorry the bot caught you too. I checked the #29945 timeline and it lines up exactly: #29948 and #29977 both show up as `source.type: "issue"` with `source.issue.pull_request` set, and #29977 is yours, open and not a draft. So it looks like the same root cause, and a really helpful second data point.

Hi @ANUBprad, thank you for offering to pick this up, that's really kind! In case it saves you some digging: the filter is in the `cross-referenced` loop in `.github/workflows/unassign-inactive-assignees.yml`, around lines 180 to 189 on current main, where `linkedPRAuthorSet` gets filled. The #29945 timeline might be handy for checking the fix, since it has two real PRs plus a cross reference from this issue (`pull_request` not set) that should still be skipped.

I'm very happy for you to take it, I'll just leave the call to the maintainers. The open question from the original post still stands too: should any linked non draft PR count, or only PRs that actually close the issue (`closingIssuesReferences`)? I'd love to hear what everyone thinks.

issue.title: fix(core): publish step failures for thrown thenables and bad causes
issue.body:
### Description

When a step fails with an unusual thrown value, its retry or failure was never recorded and the run sat idle for minutes; now it is recorded right away.

**What this code is for**

`executeStep` in `packages/core/src/runtime/spec8/step-executor.ts` and `packages/core/src/runtime/spec9/step-executor.ts` runs one step body. When the body throws, it calls `normalizeUnknownError` (in `packages/core/src/types.ts`) to turn the thrown value into `{ name, message, stack }` for logs and span attributes, then writes a `step_retrying` or `step_failed` event whose `error` comes from `dehydrateStepError`. That event is what lets the workflow retry the step or see the failure.

**Before this PR**

A step with `maxRetries: 3` throws `{ then() {} }` (an object with a `then` that never calls back), the shape rpinckne describes in the issue.

1. The body throws, and `executeStep` enters its `catch`.
2. It calls `normalizeUnknownError(effectiveErr)`.
3. `normalizeUnknownError` sees a `then` function and runs `await value`.
4. `then` never calls back, so the `await` never finishes.
5. `step_retrying` is never written. The run waits until queue redelivery starts attempt 2, about 824 s later in the report on the issue.

The same thing happens two other ways:

- A thrown `chain` whose `then(r)` calls `r(chain)`: native `await` keeps calling `then` again on the microtask queue forever. A timer cannot stop it, because timers only run once the microtask queue is empty. In the tests here the vitest worker stayed at full CPU and its own 5 s timeout never fired.
- `new Error('upstream returned 503', { cause: new ApiResponse() })`: `normalizeUnknownError` is fine, but `dehydrateStepError` throws `SerializationError: Failed to serialize step error at path ".cause"` inside the `createEvent` call. The event is lost and the original error is never recorded.

**After this PR**

Same step, same thrown `{ then() {} }`.

1. Same as above through step 2.
2. `normalizeUnknownError` calls `then` itself through `settle`, passing callbacks that resolve a plain `{ value }` object, never the thenable itself.
3. It races `settle` against a 10 second timer (`getThrownThenableTimeoutMs()`, which `WORKFLOW_THROWN_THENABLE_TIMEOUT_MS` overrides). The timer wins and it returns `Promise rejection: thrown thenable did not settle within 10000ms`, with `unwrapped` set to a plain `Error` carrying that message.
4. `executeStep` records `unwrapped` in place of the thenable, so `step_retrying` is written about ten seconds after the throw, with no serialization warning, and the step retries on schedule.

For the other two:

- `chain`: each call to `then` hands back `chain` again through the boxed callback, so nothing goes to native `await`. After 8 rounds it returns `Promise rejection: thrown thenable kept resolving to another thenable after 8 steps`.
- The class instance `cause`: `dehydrateFailure` catches the error from `dehydrateStepError` and dehydrates `toPlainError(value, fallback)` instead, then logs a warning. That is a plain `Error` with the same name, message and stack, whose `cause` is reduced the same way (here an `Error` with message `{"status":503}`). `step_retrying` is written with `upstream returned 503`.
- An `AggregateError` with an unserializable member: `toPlainError` keeps `errors`, with each member and each member's `cause` reduced the same way, so nested `AggregateError` members keep their own `errors`, and an error listed twice is kept twice. Each original error is copied once and later visits reuse that copy, so 40 copies of one member at each of four nested levels makes 44 copies, not 2.56 million. It follows at most `MAX_CAUSE_LINKS` (4) links below the thrown error, the same limit `formatErrorCauseChain` uses, so a 50,000 link chain or a `cause` getter that returns a new error on every read still finishes. A link that is cut off, or that repeats one above it, becomes a plain `Error` with the same name and message and no further `cause` or `errors`, because the `AggregateError` reviver throws on an aggregate that contains itself.
- A thrown real `Promise` that rejects with `new Error('quota exceeded')` still gives `Promise rejection: quota exceeded` in logs, as #989 made it, and `executeStep` now records the reason itself, so `new Error('outer', { cause: new Error('inner') })` arrives in the workflow with `message: 'outer'` and its `cause`. The retry decision reads the same value, so a promise rejected with a `FatalError` fails the step without retrying, and one rejected with a `RetryableError` waits for its `retryAfter`. A thenable that resolves to a value that is not an `Error` (for example `res.json()` giving `{ error: 'quota' }`) is recorded as that plain value, the same as `throw { error: 'quota' }`. One that rejects after 5 seconds (for example `throw res.json()` while a slow upstream is still sending its error body) also gives its reason, since it settles inside the 10 seconds.

**The diagram**

```mermaid
flowchart LR

classDef box fill:#eef1ff,stroke:#4c5bd4,color:#111827
classDef bad fill:#ffd6d6,stroke:#cc0000,color:#111827,stroke-width:3px
classDef good fill:#c8f0c8,stroke:#008800,color:#111827,stroke-width:3px

subgraph BEFORE["BEFORE: step_retrying never written, about 824 s idle"]
direction TB
  B1["step body throws a thenable"] --> B2["executeStep catch"]
  B2 --> B3["normalizeUnknownError"]
  B3 --> B4{"await value"}
  B4 -->|"then never calls back"| B5["waits forever, no event"]
  B4 -->|"real Promise settles"| B6["step_retrying written"]
end

subgraph AFTER["AFTER: step_retrying written within 10 s"]
direction TB
  A1["step body throws a thenable"] --> A2["executeStep catch"]
  A2 --> A3["normalizeUnknownError"]
  A3 --> A4{"THE CHANGE: settle with 10 s and 8 round limit"}
  A4 -->|"then never calls back"| A5["did not settle message, step_retrying written"]
  A4 -->|"real Promise settles"| A6["Promise rejection: reason, as before"]
end

B1 ~~~ A1

class B1,B2,B3,B6 box
class A1,A2,A3,A6 box
class B4,B5 bad
class A4,A5 good

linkStyle 3 stroke:#cc0000,stroke-width:5px
linkStyle 8 stroke:#008800,stroke-width:5px

style BEFORE fill:#fff5f5,stroke:#cc0000,color:#111827
style AFTER fill:#f3fff3,stroke:#008800,color:#111827
```

**The change**

The fix is in `normalizeUnknownError`. `await value` and the call back into itself are replaced by a loop: `getThen` reads `then` once (a getter that throws counts as no `then`), `settle` calls it with callbacks that resolve `{ value }`, and `Promise.race` against one shared timer stops after `getThrownThenableTimeoutMs()` (default `THROWN_THENABLE_TIMEOUT_MS = 10_000`, read through `envNumber` with `max: 2_147_483_647` the same way `getStepStreamDrainTimeoutMs()` reads its variable, since Node.js fires a larger timer after 1 ms; documented in `runtime-tuning.mdx`) or `THENABLE_MAX_DEPTH = 8` rounds. It returns the settled reason as `unwrapped`, or a plain `Error` when nothing settled. The round limit is the one rpinckne runs in production; the time limit started at the 1 second rpinckne uses and was raised to 10 seconds after bluepegasus123 pointed out that a slow upstream or a large HTML error page can take longer than 1 second to arrive. `describeValue` also stops `String(v)` from throwing for values with a throwing `toJSON` and `toString`, and describes a function as `function <name>` rather than its source. `getErrorStack` and `normalizeSyncError` now return only strings, so an error with an object in `stack` or `message` cannot break the plain copy.

The second change is in `executeStep`: a local `dehydrateFailure` is used at the body failure sites (fatal, retries used up, retry, and in spec9 retry past message retention). It records `unwrapped` when `normalizeUnknownError` set it, otherwise the thrown value. If that cannot be dehydrated, it records `toPlainError(...)`: a plain `Error` with the same `name`, `message` and `stack`, its `cause` chain reduced the same way, and for an `AggregateError` its `errors` reduced the same way (the `AggregateError` reviver throws when `errors` is missing). If the plain copy also fails, only an infrastructure failure is left (for example encryption is down), so it rethrows the original error without the warning and the queue retries as before. This follows the approach rpinckne suggested in the follow up comment.

**What changes for a user**

- A step that throws a thenable which never settles records its retry or failure about 10 s later (or after `WORKFLOW_THROWN_THENABLE_TIMEOUT_MS`), instead of after queue redelivery.
- A step that throws a thenable which keeps resolving to itself no longer pins a CPU.
- A step error whose `cause` cannot be serialized is still recorded with its name, message and stack, and the first links of its `cause` chain are kept as plain errors with their names and messages. A warning is logged.
- A step that throws a rejected promise records the rejection reason, cause chain included, and retries or fails according to that reason (`FatalError`, `RetryableError` and its `retryAfter`).
- An `AggregateError` recorded this way keeps its `errors`, including nested `AggregateError` members and each member's `cause`.
- A thrown `undefined`, function or symbol is now described as text, instead of leaving the message undefined. A function is described by its name only.
- `FatalError` still fails the step without retrying, because the fallback keeps `name: 'FatalError'`, which `FatalError.is` checks.
- Real thrown promises still unwrap to their reason. One change: a thrown real `Promise` that takes longer than 10 s to settle is now described as not settling, since #989 awaited thrown promises with no limit. The limit is a tradeoff between waiting for a slow error body and writing the event late; `WORKFLOW_THROWN_THENABLE_TIMEOUT_MS` lets a deployment move it, up to `2147483647`.

### How did you test your changes?

New tests in `packages/core/src/types.test.ts` and `packages/core/src/runtime/spec8/step-executor.test.ts` and `spec9/step-executor.test.ts` (the step tests use `world-local`). They cover a promise that settles after 5 s and after 20 s with the limit raised, an oversized limit being clamped, a thenable that never settles under a 50 ms limit, a rejected promise whose reason has a cause, nested `AggregateError` members, a member listed twice, a member shared across four nested aggregates, promises rejected with `FatalError` and `RetryableError`, non-Error and primitive causes, a cause getter that throws or returns a new error on every read, a 50,000 link chain, an error whose `stack` is an object, an encryption failure during the fallback, a thrown function, and cyclic causes and aggregates. Every test added in the last two commits fails on the commit before it. Without the fix, seven fail (two time out, three throw `SerializationError` while serializing the cause, two throw from the normalizer) and the two self resolving cases spin until the process is killed. With the fix all pass, and the three cases covering #989 (rejected promise, nested promise, `then` that throws) pass both before and after. The full `@workflow/core` suite passes (`pnpm test`: 215 files, 4160 tests), `pnpm typecheck` is clean, and `biome check` on the changed files shows no new findings.

### PR Checklist - Required to merge

- [x] 📦 `pnpm changeset` was run to create a changelog for this PR
- [x] 🔒 DCO sign-off passes (run `git commit --signoff` on your commits)
- [x] 📝 Ping `@vercel/workflow` in a comment once the PR is ready, and the above checklist is complete

Thank you rpinckne for the detailed report and the recheck on `main`; this follows your design closely, and I would be glad to hear if your patch handles anything this misses.

Closes #2994

comment.body:
Thanks so much @bluepegasus123, that's a really good point about redelivery being the backstop. It makes me a lot more comfortable that a slightly early limit is never worse than a retry.

So 14289f9 stays as is: a 10s default with `WORKFLOW_THROWN_THENABLE_TIMEOUT_MS` to override it. Two small follow ups landed right after it. 313d620 caps the override at 2147483647, since Node fires a larger timer after 1ms. 1d05769 makes a thenable that rejects with a `FatalError` or `RetryableError` get classified by that reason, so it fails fast or honors `retryAfter` like a direct throw would.

Is there anything else that would help with this one? Happy to adjust whatever you'd like.

issue.title: Custom command {{args}} and system prompt substitution expand `$` replacement patterns

labels.name: user-6ec56081/repo-566d0f35
labels.description: Important but can be addressed in a future release.

labels.name: user-3ef72433/repo-efde29d2
labels.description: Issues related to User Interface, OS Support, Core Functionality

labels.name: user-3784fdbb/repo-a70605d4
labels.description: 1 day or less: trivial logic, UI adjustments, docs

issue.body:
### What happened?

When a custom command's `{{args}}` (or a system prompt placeholder) is filled in, any `$` patterns in the inserted text get expanded by JavaScript instead of being kept as typed.

Custom commands insert whatever the user typed after the command into the prompt at `{{args}}`. The docs promise this text is "injected exactly as the user typed them" ([custom-commands.md#L71](https://github.com/google-gemini/gemini-cli/blob/6814e00d6b148c3a1d57244d5d7040f7c541009d/docs/cli/custom-commands.md?plain=1#L71)).

The substitution passes the user's text as the replacement _string_ to `replaceAll` ([shellProcessor.ts#L73](https://github.com/google-gemini/gemini-cli/blob/6814e00d6b148c3a1d57244d5d7040f7c541009d/packages/cli/src/services/prompt-processors/shellProcessor.ts#L73), [#L93](https://github.com/google-gemini/gemini-cli/blob/6814e00d6b148c3a1d57244d5d7040f7c541009d/packages/cli/src/services/prompt-processors/shellProcessor.ts#L93), [#L158](https://github.com/google-gemini/gemini-cli/blob/6814e00d6b148c3a1d57244d5d7040f7c541009d/packages/cli/src/services/prompt-processors/shellProcessor.ts#L158), [#L210](https://github.com/google-gemini/gemini-cli/blob/6814e00d6b148c3a1d57244d5d7040f7c541009d/packages/cli/src/services/prompt-processors/shellProcessor.ts#L210)), so JS treats `$$`, `$&`, `` $` `` and `$'` in it as special patterns.

1. Have a custom command whose prompt is something like `say {{args}}`.
2. Run `/explain costs $$5 and $&`.
3. The model receives `say costs $5 and {{args}}`: `$$` collapsed to `$`, and `$&` turned back into the literal placeholder.

`applySubstitutions` in `packages/core/src/prompts/utils.ts` has the same pattern for `${AgentSkills}`, `${SubAgents}` and `${AvailableTools}` ([#L72](https://github.com/google-gemini/gemini-cli/blob/6814e00d6b148c3a1d57244d5d7040f7c541009d/packages/core/src/prompts/utils.ts#L72), [#L85](https://github.com/google-gemini/gemini-cli/blob/6814e00d6b148c3a1d57244d5d7040f7c541009d/packages/core/src/prompts/utils.ts#L85), [#L93](https://github.com/google-gemini/gemini-cli/blob/6814e00d6b148c3a1d57244d5d7040f7c541009d/packages/core/src/prompts/utils.ts#L93)), so a skill or subagent description containing a `$` pattern would also be altered in the system prompt.

### What did you expect to happen?

The text should arrive exactly as typed: `say costs $$5 and $&`.

Minimal repro in plain Node:

```js
"say {{args}}".replaceAll("{{args}}", "costs $$5 and $&");
// => 'say costs $5 and {{args}}'

"say {{args}}".replaceAll("{{args}}", () => "costs $$5 and $&");
// => 'say costs $$5 and $&'
```

### Client information

Found by reading the source on main at 6814e00 (source review, not a running client).

### Login information

N/A

### Anything else we need to know?

This looks like the same class as #29044, which #30035 fixed really nicely for the summarizer, llm edit fixer and session summary. Thanks for that work! These two spots just weren't in its scope. The `applySubstitutions` half was also raised in #27993, which went stale and was closed.

Which fix would you prefer here: a replacer function (`() => value`) or `split().join()`? Happy to send a small PR with tests if you're open to adding `help wanted`.

issue.title: Functions: isolate the list and tree to one folder
issue.body:
On a big monorepo the Functions tab mixes every sub-project together. On one repo with 9,942 functions, the List shows the top functions from every sub-project at once, and the Tree shows 850 starting points under a single project card. There is no way to look at just one folder.

What we want:

- A folder picker in the Functions header, next to List and Tree. It shows the current folder as a breadcrumb (for example `wildcard-card / reporter / frontend`), and each part of the breadcrumb takes you back up.
- A searchable dropdown that lists the folders inside the current one with their function counts, biggest first. Picking one narrows the view to it.
- In the List, clicking the folder part of a row's file path narrows to that folder. Clicking the rest of the row still opens the code.
- The chosen folder is remembered per project. If it no longer exists, the view goes back to the whole project.
- Inside a folder, importance is worked out again from only the functions in that folder and the calls between them, so the 1 to 5 spread means something there. "Used in N places" counts callers inside the folder, and a note says when the function is also used from outside it.
- Inside a folder, the Tree starts from a card named after the folder. Its first level is the functions nothing else in the folder calls, real starting points first.
- The header count reads like "1,204 functions in reporter/frontend".
- With no folder chosen, everything behaves exactly as it does today.

release.name: repo-29010712
release.body:
This is the first tagged release of Architect. The main new thing is a Functions tab that shows every function in your project, ranked by how much the rest of the code leans on it.

## Highlights

**Functions tab.** Architect now opens on Functions. Every function in the project is listed with its line count, an importance score from 1 to 5, and a one line description. You can sort by importance, lines or name, and filter by name, file or description. (#206)

**Instant ranking, no AI and no API key.** Importance comes from PageRank over the call graph plus a few plain facts, such as whether a function is exported or is a starting point. Descriptions come from the author's own comments, or from the function name when there are none. Nothing is sent anywhere, and it takes about 3 ms for 1,300 functions. (#207)

**Tree view.** A List | Tree switch on the Functions tab draws an org chart of who calls whom, from the starting points of the program down. You can open and close branches, search, and zoom. Functions that nothing reaches are shown on their own. (#208)

![Functions list](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/abhiramshaji-cyber/Architect/main/docs/screenshots/functions-list.png)

![Functions tree](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/abhiramshaji-cyber/Architect/main/docs/screenshots/functions-tree.png)

In dark mode:

![Functions list, dark](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/abhiramshaji-cyber/Architect/main/docs/screenshots/functions-list-dark.png)

![Functions tree, dark](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/abhiramshaji-cyber/Architect/main/docs/screenshots/functions-tree-dark.png)

## Other changes

- Architect no longer writes an `architect.md` on its own when a Claude session opens a project without one. The Draft button on the Contract tab still drafts one when you ask. (#206)
- The Diff tab is calmer, and files in nested projects open correctly. (#204)
- The README shows the Functions tab, the screenshots are refreshed, and there is a feedback form. (#210)
- Earlier work that lands in this first release includes live Claude Code sessions with a history of every change, worktree browsing, the Diff view with commit, push and pull, the `architect check` command for CI, the `architect.md` language server, and a fix that keeps the MCP bridge alive when it gets a malformed line from the app (#187).

## Install

There is no packaged download yet. Build and install from source:

```bash
git clone https://github.com/abhiramshaji-cyber/Architect.git
cd Architect
npm install
npm run install:local
```

That installs the app and writes the MCP bridge to `~/.architect/bin/architect-mcp.mjs`. If the `claude` CLI is on your PATH it also registers the bridge with Claude Code. Setup for Claude Desktop and Codex is in the [README](https://github.com/abhiramshaji-cyber/Architect#install). I build and test it on macOS, and the scanner reads TypeScript and JavaScript.

## Tell us what you think

This is early, and I would really like to know where it helps and where it gets things wrong, especially whether the importance ranking matches your own sense of the code.

- Reply in the discussion: https://github.com/abhiramshaji-cyber/Architect/discussions/209
- Or fill in the short feedback form: https://github.com/abhiramshaji-cyber/Architect/issues/new?template=feedback.yml

issue.title: Functions tab: hybrid deterministic + AI function map
issue.body:
## Goal

Add a Functions tab that lists every function in the open project as a plain, readable list. Each row shows the function name, its file, how many lines it has, an AI ranked importance from 1 to 5, and one short sentence in everyday words saying what it does, so someone who does not write code can follow it. The tab is first in the tab bar and is the default view, with Contract second.

## How the ranking works

The engine is hybrid, so it is fast, precise and cheap.

1. Facts, computed instantly with no AI, from the code map on every scan: line count, how many other functions call it, how many functions it calls, whether it is exported, and whether its file is a starting point (nothing in the project loads it, or package.json names it as main or bin). Every row appears straight away from these facts, sorted in a provisional order (most callers first, then longest) that the header labels as provisional.
2. Meaning, from AI: one Claude Code call per file using the haiku model. The facts go in as evidence, and the model returns the importance and the summary for each function. The model decides what matters; there is no hand tuned formula blending the facts into a score.
3. Efficiency: results are cached per file by a hash of its content, so an unchanged file is never sent again and only changed files are ranked. At most 3 files are ranked at once. Work in flight is cancelled when the project is closed or the tab switches to another project. Each request is bounded: at most 50 functions per call and a fixed number of source lines per function, sized against the haiku context window, and no function is ever dropped.

If Claude Code is not installed, or a file fails, the list still shows every function with its facts and says plainly what could not be ranked.

## Auto draft is turned off

Architect no longer writes a first architect.md on its own when a Claude Code session touches a project that has none. The Contract tab, the manual Create architect.md and Draft with Claude buttons, architect.md parsing and the MCP tools are unchanged.
